The frame layout types a stack slot from its own loads and stores and, where two readings of the same bytes differ only in signedness, keeps the one the data-type ordering ranks more specific (`unsigned int` over `int`), so an out-parameter comes back declared by its bit tests and cast at the call. With the option on, the callee's declaration decides the slot's signedness when every frame reference to it is a plain `&local` handed straight to a direct call at a parameter whose type is locked (a declared or libc signature; never a trial, a format-string position or an override) and is `T *` for one plain 4- or 8-byte integer `T`; every access the frame model sees inside the slot covers it whole at that width and is an integer or unknown, and the layout would not stretch it into an array; and every operator whose C meaning depends on the operand's sign (`<`, `/`, `%`, `>>`, a widening), reached through copies, phis and the operators whose result keeps its type, computes with `T`'s sign: one reader that wants the other sign declines. A value re-declared signed is also left alone when `+`, `-`, `*`, unary `-` or `<<` reads it, directly or through the expression it prints into (signed overflow is undefined where the binary wraps), or when it meets a constant with its top bit set in `==`, `!=`, `&`, `|` or `^`. An address kept in a variable, stored, compared, offset or passed at another type, a byte read of one half, a wider copy, a float, a type lock or a reader the walk does not model (an address, an index, a float conversion) declines. Only the declaration moves, and the cast pass computes with the merged variable's type, which a slot stored from a register can keep at the old signedness; so after merging, a re-declared slot whose variable has another type is checked again over every member of the variable, and when some reader disagrees the slot and its Symbol go back to the variable's type.
- **When to flip:** On by default. An out-parameter local is declared the way the callee declares it -- `waitpid`'s and `wait`'s `int *` status, `pthread_setcancelstate`'s `int *` old state -- when the body reads it with bit tests and signed operators only; the call then passes `&v1` uncast and an arithmetic shift of the status reads it uncast. A status the body also shifts right logically (the -O2 form of `WEXITSTATUS`), compares unsigned or zero-extends stays unsigned. Flip OFF to see the frame layout's own reading of the slot (`unsigned int v5; waitpid(v2,(int *)&v5,0)`), for a bisect or an ablation. The flip's evidence is docs/features/castobject/default-on-evaluation.md.
- **Where / provenance:** P6/stack-frame-layout · kuna · type-inference · kuna-castobject
- **Example:** `option castobject on`

### `stackviews` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a reused stack slot is assigned a value of an incompatible type; two object views of one frame address become unrelated local variables.
- **What it does:** Represent incompatible stack-object incarnations as typed views of shared backing storage.
- **When to flip:** Enable when a frame address is passed with incompatible declared pointee types, or when separate byte-definition families need lifetime-scoped name/type assertions. Shared backing keeps old pointers and simultaneous views at the same address, retains escaped frame writes, and preserves byte-copy semantics for reinterpreted accesses. Fixed and bounded indexed byte extents can share a backing object. Unbounded indices and explicit user-locked layouts retain their existing mapping. Complete leaf-callee bodies can refine frame read and write barriers; unresolved effects remain conservative.
- **Where / provenance:** P6/alias-facets · kuna · opt-in-tool · #810
- **Example:** `option stackviews on`

### `stackalias` -- on | off, default `off` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** spurious uninitialized local (xStack_N) returned after storing through a pointer to a local; store through a take-address-of-local pointer dropped as dead so the later read is garbage.
- **What it does:** Hold a store-through-a-stack-pointer-alias (int *p=&x; *p=x; return *p) alive across the deadcode race so it is not dropped to an uninitialized stack read.
- **When to flip:** Set on PER FUNCTION when a take-address-of-local + store-through-pointer returns a spurious uninitialized local (xStack_*); DESTRUCTIVE as a global default (conservatively pins stack stores live, suppressing legitimate dead-store removal).
- **Where / provenance:** P6/alias-facets · ghidra-upstream · opt-in-tool · GH-8500
- **Example:** `option stackalias on`

### `sparcstructret` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** bogus (*pcVar1)() indirect call after calling a struct-returning function on sparc; function tail dropped after a sparc call followed by unimp.
- **What it does:** On SPARC, let the struct-return `unimp` word after a call fall through instead of becoming a non-returning indirect call.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a SPARC function calling a struct-returning callee keeps its tail instead of rendering a bogus (*pcVar1)() and dropping everything after the call. The marker is recognized by the `IllegalInstructionTrap` user-op only the SPARC SLEIGH declares, so it is inert on every other processor; on SPARC a genuine `unimp` trap that is not an ABI marker is folded the same way, so flip off when auditing code that relies on the trap.
- **Where / provenance:** P2/flow-classification · ghidra-upstream · opt-in-tool · GH-6882
- **Example:** `option sparcstructret on`

### `loweredswitch` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** switch rendered as nested if/else-if compare tree over one variable; binary-search cascade of constant compares where source had a switch; flip off to keep the compiler's lowered compare-tree rendering.
- **What it does:** Reconstruct a compiler-lowered comparison cascade (a GCC binary-search if/else tree over one variable) back into a switch with a synthesized BRANCHIND + jump-table (the S2 artifact Ghidra renders switches from). The re-roll carries the cascade's range-comparison signedness onto every label, labels every case value, is installed only when it dispatches on the value the cascade compared (or is withdrawn) and routes every value and keeps every statement as its compare tree does, and is tried behind every head on the switch variable, not only the first.
- **When to flip:** On by default (DIV-4); the required binary-search-structure guard (a range/jle split) keeps it off hand-written linear if/else-if chains. Set OFF to restore the upstream if/else-if rendering of a lowered switch. The exactness, every-head, signedness and value guards are the only way the re-roll runs and have no switch of their own.
- **Where / provenance:** P2/switch-model · angr · structure-recovery · angr-LoweredSwitchSimplifier
- **Example:** `option loweredswitch off`

### `callmechanisms` -- off | auto | on, default `auto`

- **Symptoms:** values below an x87 call are read from the wrong register-stack positions after consecutive calls; a store the compiler spec says a callee always makes is missing after the call; a custom compiler spec's uponentry or uponreturn p-code has no effect on the output; a PPC64 ELFv1 switch after an external call is a jump-as-call through r2 plus a constant; a PPC64 ELFv1 function reads an r2 local that is never assigned after a call; a TOC-relative global after an external PPC64 call prints as an unknown pointer plus an offset.
- **What it does:** Apply the p-code a compiler spec attaches to a prototype model's call boundaries: `<prototype><pcode inject="uponentry">` before the first operation of a function evaluated with that model, and `<pcode inject="uponreturn">` right after every modeled call whose callee uses it, both installed before SSA so the effects reach dataflow (upstream `ActionConstbase` / `FuncCallSpecs::insertPcode`). A model that declares the x87 register-stack rotation a callee performs, or a store a callee always makes, then reads the values below the call from their real positions. Only payloads with a locally compiled body are applied: a `dynamic` payload with no body (the JVM and Dalvik `uponentry` models), and every payload in ghidra mode, stay unresolved. A late prototype restriction that changes a call's return effect requests a full reflow. At `auto` (the default) a return payload is installed only on a PPC64 image whose ELFv1 function descriptors the loader validated, from a linked image's or a relocatable object's `.opd`, and only at a call whose next instruction loads back a slot the payload stores. There the effect is applied by forwarding: that load reads the stored register directly, and no store is left in the frame (a payload with any other effect is installed as written). Entry payloads are not installed. The stock PPC64 models store `r2Save` (set by `bl`) to `0x28(r1)`, the TOC save doubleword the ELFv1 ABI reserves in every frame, so the `ld r2,40(r1)` that follows an external call reads back the caller's TOC instead of an unwritten stack slot, and a TOC-relative jump table or global after the call keeps its address. A call with no reload, or whose reloaded `r2` is never read, therefore prints as `off` prints it: an unread store after each call would keep a short-circuit `a() && b()` from forming. `on` installs every payload after every modeled call and at every entry, on any image; `off` installs none.
- **When to flip:** Default `auto` is right for nearly every program: it acts only on a PPC64 ELFv1 image (big-endian, with a validated `.opd`, linked or relocatable), where `0x28(r1)` is the TOC save slot, and only at calls the caller follows with the TOC reload; it is inert on every other image, every XML test and every spec that declares no prototype p-code (every stock x86, ARM, AArch64, MIPS and RISC-V spec). Do not force it ON for an ELFv2 PPC64 binary (every little-endian one): there the TOC is saved at `0x18(r1)` and `0x28(r1)` is ordinary frame storage, so a local the function keeps there is replaced by the TOC pointer after each call. Turn ON for upstream Ghidra's behaviour (every payload at every call and entry), for a custom compiler spec whose models declare boundary effects, or for ELFv1 code the loader could not validate (no section headers, or a raw image) whose calls restore `r2` from `0x28(r1)`. Turn OFF to see an ELFv1 function as the bytes alone describe it, with the post-call TOC reload reading an unknown stack slot.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/abi-trust · ghidra-upstream · correctness-fix · kuna-call-mechanisms
- **Example:** `option callmechanisms on`

### `varargsharedfloat` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a 32-bit PowerPC -O0 variadic call drops a trailing double that an earlier argument is computed from; `sumi(2, x * 2, x)` prints as `sumi(2,x + x)` on PowerPC.
- **What it does:** Keep a variadic double on 32-bit PowerPC whose register also feeds an earlier argument of the same call. `sumi(2, x * 2, x)` with `sumi(int, ...)` compiles at clang -O0 to `lfd 2,16(31); fadd 1,2,2; li 3,2; crset 6; bl sumi`: x is loaded once into f2 and `x + x` is computed from it into f1. Upstream's checkCallDoubleUse (funcdata_varnode.cc:1802) refuses a value that also feeds another active argument, so the f2 trial is inactive and, as the last one, dropped: `sumi(2,x + x)`. The same instructions are what a scratch register looks like (`sumi(1, *a * *b + *c)` is `lfd 0; lfd 1; lfd 2; fmadd 1,0,1,2; crset 6`), and CR bit 6 says only that some FPR is passed, so the evidence is the register choice: a scratch double gets the lowest free FPR. With the option on, an inactive 8-byte trial of a variadic call whose block sets CR bit 6 is active when it is a floating-point entry past the first, every earlier floating-point entry is an active trial, its value is written in the call's block, f0 or one of those earlier registers is free from the instruction after the write to the last instruction before the call that reads the value, and every other use of the value reaches only another active argument slot of the same call.
- **When to flip:** Off by default. Turn it on for 32-bit PowerPC code built without optimization (-O0) when a variadic call such as `sumi(2, x * 2, x)` prints `sumi(2,x + x)`; the callee must be declared variadic (DWARF or `--assert prototype`). The register-choice evidence holds only when nothing reorders instructions after register allocation. Measured on 1,200 random clang calls of a non-format variadic double function: at -O0 it restores 91 dropped arguments and adds none; at -O2 and -Os it restores 11 and adds 23 arguments the source never passed, because the post-allocation scheduler moves a scratch value's readers so f0 or f1 looks free. Optimized code rarely needs it: -O2 copies the shared value (`fmr 2,1; fadd 1,1,1`) and prints correctly already.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/active-input-trial-scoring · kuna · correctness-fix · GH-841
- **Example:** `option varargsharedfloat on`

### `narrowargs` -- off | on | callers, default `callers`

- **Symptoms:** a uint8_t parameter prints as unsigned int and is only ever used as a1 & 0xff or (char)a1; an int parameter prints as unsigned long on x86-64 and is used as (unsigned int)a0; a caller passes v + 5 to a callee whose parameter is a byte and another caller passes v - 8 & 0xff.
- **What it does:** Declare a register parameter at the narrow width its body actually reads. An ARM AAPCS or x86-64 caller passes a `uint8_t`, a `short` or an `int` in a whole register, so a callee that computes with the register at full width (`and.w r2, r1, #7`, `mov %edi,%eax` beside a forwarded `%rdi`) keeps the input Varnode register-wide and recovers `unsigned int` or `unsigned long`. `ActionDeadCode` knows which bits of every register input any use can observe. Once `mainloop` settles, `fullloop`'s dead-code pass looks at each input that is a whole integer argument register of the model: when those bits all lie in its low 1, 2 or 4 bytes and reach that part's top bit, the input is replaced by that low part, zero-extended back to the register at the function entry. Every use then reads the same bits it read before, so every value the function computes is unchanged, and `ActionInputPrototype` recovers the parameter at the narrow width. In the callee-first `decompile-all` run, the narrow parameter a callee states through `protoorder` caps the bytes `ActionDeadCode::markConsumedParameters` treats as consumed at each call to it (`FuncCallSpecs::getInputBytesConsumed`), so a caller that only forwards its own parameter there narrows too. A left shift (`priority << 24`, `(a0 ^ 0x8000) << 0x10`, a multiply by a multiple of 256) and a register shift amount (ARM's `lsl r6, r7, lr` reads `lr & 0xff`) are not evidence about the value, and a mask that stops below the part's top bit (`flags & 0x10`, `x & 7`) is as often an `int` of flags as a narrow value, so none of them narrows. With `callers` (the default) a whole-binary `decompile-all` of a 32-bit ARM image also narrows a parameter from its call sites, because the AAPCS has the CALLER extend a `uint8_t`, `int16_t` or `_Bool` argument and the callee body then holds no evidence of it. After the first pass, a function whose callers kuna can list (no loaded value at any byte offset is its address or a self-relative offset to it, no dynamic relocation targets it, no `movw`/`movt` pair, `adr` or PIC `ldr`/`add pc` builds it, no decompiled body holds it as a constant or resolves an indirect call or branch to it, it is exported nowhere, and the calls and tail jumps decompiled as calls are exactly the instructions that branch to it; an image with Android packed relocations closes nothing) is decompiled again with a register parameter replaced by its low 1 or 2 bytes, zero- or sign-extended back at the entry, when every call passes a value that fits (its nonzero bits, a sign extension, a constant) and at least one caller extended the value itself (`uxtb`, `sxth`, a mask by exactly `0xff` or `0xffff`); a parameter every call passes 0 or 1, one of them computed, becomes `bool`. A caller passing a wider value, a sign and a zero extension, or a function reached any other way keeps the register-wide parameter. The redo pass reprints at most 5% of the lines the first pass printed (a function of at most 32 lines always fits). Unseen: a table of offsets relative to the table or another function, read through an index kuna cannot resolve (hand-written assembly; C compilers do not emit one on 32-bit ARM).
- **When to flip:** On by default. The tell it fixes is a `uint8_t` or `uint16_t` parameter printed as `unsigned int` on ARM firmware, or an `int` printed as `unsigned long` on x86-64, whose every use reads only its low bytes (`a1 & 0xff`, two byte stores of `a1` and `a1 >> 8`, `(unsigned int)a0`). Set it off to get the register-wide parameter back, or when a parameter the source declares `int` (a byte written through `*p = c`, a 32-bit `len` passed as a `size_t`) should keep its source width; the C is the same value either way. Callers of a narrowed callee may print a narrower argument expression (`(unsigned char)(v2 + 5)` for `v2 + 5`): the callee reads only those bytes. Measured against `off` with decbench's published type_match: 96 ARM firmware slices 2,505 -> 2,631 perfect functions (mean .2287 -> .2366, 19 functions off a perfect score), the 444-slice x86-64 campaign set 1,664 -> 1,683 (none off), the 96-binary nightly optimized sample 1,517 -> 1,597; every function that leaves a perfect score declares an `int` or enum the body reads one byte or one word of. `callers` (the default) also fixes a 32-bit ARM `uint8_t`, `int16_t` or `_Bool` parameter printed `unsigned int` or `int` although every caller extends what it passes (`uxtb r1, r4; bl f`); set `on` to keep only the body rule when such a parameter is an `int` or a short enum in the source (every caller passing a byte cannot tell the two apart). Measured against `on` with decbench's published type_match: 96 ARM firmware slices 3,279 -> 3,351 perfect functions (115 onto a perfect score, 43 off: `int` flags every caller passes a truth value, short enums), 23 mostly-Thumb slices 1,055 -> 1,086; the x86-64 sets do not move.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/own-input-prototype-recovery · kuna · type-inference · ty17-narrow-register-parameters
- **Example:** `option narrowargs on`

### `regnarrow` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a uint8_t loop counter prints as unsigned int v with v = v + 1 & 0xff; a byte loaded with ldrb is declared unsigned int and used as an index; an int local prints as unsigned long on x86-64 though every value is a zero-extended 32-bit result.
- **What it does:** Declare a register local at the narrow width all of its values fit. A `uint8_t` loop counter on ARM lives in a whole register (`adds r5, #1; uxtb r5, r5`), a byte read with `ldrb` stays zero-extended in it, and an x86-64 `unsigned` written through `%eax` is zero-extended into `%rax`, so the SSA web that becomes the variable keeps the register's width and prints as `unsigned int` or `unsigned long` with `v = v + 1 & 0xff` in the body. Once `mainloop` settles, `fullloop`'s dead-code pass looks at every web of register varnodes that MULTIEQUALs join, and at a single register definition read twice or more: when the nonzero-bit analysis proves all of its values fit a low 1, 2 or 4 bytes whose top bit they can set, and every value entering the web is an explicit narrowing (a zero extension from at most that width of a value not tied to memory, a mask that keeps only those bytes, a constant or a copy), the web is rebuilt at the narrow width with upstream's `SubvariableFlow` in a zero-extended mode. Arithmetic whose result is read only in the low bytes (`v + 1` feeding the `& 0xff`) is narrowed with it, a value whose definition cannot be narrowed is read through its low bytes, and every other reader that needs the register's width (an index, a compare, a call argument, a store) reads the zero extension of the narrow value, which is exactly the value it read before: the p-code computes the same values, and the printer casts a narrow expression wherever C's promotion to `int` would change what a read sees (an extension, a comparison, a division, a right shift, a switch selector). A narrowed value nothing else types is declared unsigned; one loaded through a `char *` stays `char`. A web that reaches a function input, a RETURN or a user-op operand is left alone, and so are a single masked value with no MULTIEQUAL (every wide reader would mask it again) and a value small only by arithmetic (`x / 60`, `x >> 24`, a counter incremented a few times): it is as often an `int`. A copy can carry the narrowing into a stack slot that is not tied to memory (a `-O0` local). On ARM the shift guard prints such a narrowed count without a second cast.
- **When to flip:** On by default. The tell it fixes is a byte or halfword local printed `unsigned int` on ARM firmware (`v = v + 1 & 0xff`, `v = (unsigned int)*p` used as an index), or an `unsigned` counter printed `unsigned long` on x86-64 whose every value is a zero-extended 32-bit result. Set it off to get the register-wide declarations back, or when a local the source declares `int` or as an enum is only ever loaded from a byte field (an enum kept in a `uint8_t`, a `numRows` read from a `uint16_t`): the binary cannot tell the two apart. The p-code computes the same values either way. Measured with decbench's published type_match: 96 ARM firmware slices 3,232 -> 3,279 perfect functions (mean .3068 -> .3105; 492 functions better, 106 worse), the 96-binary nightly optimized sample 2,315 -> 2,337, the 444-slice x86-64 set 1,903 -> 1,905; the functions that lose a perfect score declare an enum or `int` the body only loads from a byte field.
- **Where / provenance:** P3/simplification-quiescence · kuna · type-inference · ty17-narrow-register-locals
- **Example:** `option regnarrow on`

### `regsigned` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a signed char loaded with ldrsb is declared int; a short counter prints as int with (int)(short) casts at every use; an int local prints as long on x86-64 though every value is a movsxd.
- **What it does:** Declare a register local whose every value is a sign extension at the narrow width those values are extended from. A `signed char` or `short` read with `ldrsb`/`ldrsh` or `movsx`, or an x86-64 `int` widened with `movsxd`, lives sign-extended in a whole register, so the web that becomes the variable keeps the register's width and prints as `int` or `long`. With `regnarrow` on, its pass also looks at the webs whose values the nonzero-bit masks cannot fit (their sign bits are set): when every value entering the web is a sign extension from at most 1, 2 or 4 bytes (one of them from exactly that width), a copy, a bitwise op of such values or a constant that is the sign extension of its low bytes, the web is rebuilt at that width with upstream's sign-extended `SubvariableFlow`, extended the way `regnarrow` extends the zero-extended one: a copy, a phi, a wider sign extension, a bitwise op, a constant arithmetic right shift, a truncation and a call argument whose parameter is no wider carry the narrow value, and every other reader that needs the register's width (arithmetic, a compare, an index, a call argument, a store) reads the sign extension of the narrow value, which is exactly the value it read before. A narrowed value nothing else types (or only a bitwise op's `uint`) is declared signed. A web that reaches a function input, a RETURN, an INDIRECT, a user-op operand or a switch is left alone, and so is one with a value whose definition is anything else (arithmetic, a load at the register's width, a call) or that was stored to a frame slot wider than the narrow width (the `-O0` spill of `int v = c;`), and so is a web with no phi that only widens function inputs.
- **When to flip:** Off by default: on decbench type_match it gains only a few perfect functions (ARM firmware +4, x86-64 +0) and adds casts where a narrowed value is widened again (`(long)(int)v` on AArch64). Turn it on when a `signed char`/`short` local prints `int` on ARM firmware (`v = (int)*(char *)p`, a counter compared as `(int)(char)v`), or an x86-64 `int` prints `long` whose every value is a `movsxd`. The p-code computes the same values either way.
- **Where / provenance:** P3/simplification-quiescence · kuna · type-inference · ty17-narrow-signed-register-locals
- **Example:** `option regsigned on`

### `protoorder` -- off | types | cycles | lock, default `cycles`

- **Symptoms:** a FILE * or char * the caller holds becomes long at the callee's parameter; a function that only hands a string on to a recursive function (quotearg_buffer_restyled, a tree walk, a pair of functions calling each other) keeps an integer parameter; an argument is typed at one call site of a callee and not at another; decompiling one function alone gives it a prototype the whole-binary output does not use at its call sites; the same sub_ address is called with one argument at one site and three at another in the same function.
- **What it does:** Decompile a whole binary callees-first and state each function's RECOVERED parameter types where its callers read declared ones from, so what one function learned about its own parameters reaches every call to it. `TypeOpCall::getInputLocal` (typeop.cc:689) already types a call argument from the callee's parameter -- but only from a DECLARED prototype, and the only writers of that slot are facts from outside the decompile: a libc/`libctypes` table entry, a DWARF or demangled signature, `--assert prototype`, `parse line extern`. Nothing states what a RECOVERY found, so an internal callee tells its callers nothing and each caller types the call from its own local evidence alone. coreutils fmt -O2 shows the cost: `sub_3700` recovers as `unsigned long sub_3700(FILE *a0, unsigned long a1)` and its caller still renders `sub_3700(stdin,v7)` with `char *v7` typed from nothing. With the option on, `kuna decompile-all` orders the run by the call graph `kuna xrefs` already publishes (`kuna_analysis::listing::xrefs`, the same edges `--reachable-from` walks), decompiles each callee before its callers over Tarjan's SCCs of those edges, and records the parameter types the callee recovered against the storage it recovered them in. Inside a recursive component (a function that calls itself, or a cycle of functions calling each other) `callees first` has no meaning: `cycles` (the default) still lets every member state its types, decompiling a larger component's members once each in a depth-first order over the component's own calls that starts from the members something outside it calls, so each member reads the partners it reaches and the component's callers read every member; `types` states nothing for a member of a recursive component, which stops the chain at the first recursion (every coreutils caller that passes a file name to gnulib's self-recursive `quotearg_buffer_restyled` kept it an integer). At each later call site, argument `i` takes the callee's recovered type for parameter `i` when the two agree about the storage -- position and storage both, so the two recoveries are talking about the same argument. Results are buffered and emitted in address order, so only the decompile ORDER changes and the output stays byte-stable. A function never reads its own statement, and before `structsynth`'s convergence sweep decompiles anything again it forgets every stated list that names a superseded structure (a redone callee states again before its redone callers), so a redone recursive function never takes the structure the redo exists to replace from its own first answer or a cycle partner's. `types` and `cycles` state ONLY parameter types: nothing is locked, so `ActionFuncLink` runs the caller's own argument recovery at every call exactly as it does with the option off and no call gains an argument; the one argument a call can lose is the trailing clobbered one `argclobber` drops on the evidence of a stated list, under `cycles` at a recursive callee too. The recovered type arrives as one more vote in `Varnode::getLocalType`'s `type_order` fold; it is never the type a cast is measured against, so where it loses the argument renders as it does off, and it is refused outright where the caller holds evidence the fold cannot weigh: the argument is the address of a frame object, the value (its COPY/CAST/MULTIEQUAL/INDIRECT family) is declared, global, a frame address, frame memory, an element of a stack struct, array or indexed frame region, or loaded through itself (`p = *p`), the vote is deeper than the inferred pointer cap, a pointer vote lands on a constant inside a function's code (a Thumb address would render as `&sub_8130[1]`, a subscript of a function), another call reads or writes the same value as a different kind (pointer, integer, float), float-ness disagrees with the value or its register, or what the caller loads and stores through a pointer disagrees with a float, composite or non-character primitive pointee (an access or address outside the object, an access across or inside its members, a step of other than one element, integer bits moved through a float member, or a constant stored wider than a non-character primitive pointee, which `SplitDatatype` would print as one store per element; a caller with too many derived addresses to check is refused as well). The callee's recovered return type is not stated: a call's result has no competing evidence, so a wrong one spreads into the caller. `lock` instead parks the recovered prototype in the symbol table, where `ActionDefaultParams` reads a declared one from, which does decide the call's arity: the parked list is a FLOOR rather than a ceiling (the first slot past the recovered parameters starts a variable tail, so `func_link_input` keeps active-input recovery on and a caller that passes more still recovers the rest), and four further rules read the callee's own machine code through the entry-liveness walk `calleedeadarg` owns -- a trailing parameter the body never reads is trimmed rather than stated, a callee that provably READS the register its next argument would arrive in has under-recovered and is declined, a recovered list that saturates the convention's argument registers is declined (the shape a variadic register-save prologue leaves: exactly six parameters on SysV, exactly four on AAPCS), and a list the model would not place in the storage it was recovered in is declined outright. Every mode declines when the function's decompile errored, when it says nothing, when model selection did not settle, when a parameter is a hidden return pointer, and -- always -- when a prototype is already DECLARED for that entry; `types` and `lock` also decline for a function in a recursive component, so an operator's `--assert prototype`, a libc signature, DWARF or a demangled name outranks anything recovery found. The statement is a caller-side fact only: the locked-input branch of `ActionPrototypeTypes` is stubbed, and the callee has already been decompiled when its types are stated.
- **When to flip:** On by default (`cycles`) on a whole-binary `kuna decompile-all`; a whole-binary surface otherwise, except that a single-function `kuna decompile` on a compiler spec with preferred register splits bootstraps the recovered parameter types of the direct callees whose own call sites pass a preferred-split register in an active input trial (at most 32, no recursion, isolated from the caller's own drive state, types only). That bootstrap is what lets a split-register argument take the callee's type; a value merely loaded from a `q` register but passed only through integer registers selects nothing, and it never states arity; batch/--jobs/decompile-project keep the schedules below. A run narrowed by `--functions`, `--addr` or a triage filter, selecting one function, or on a `--raw-image` (which has no call graph), decompiles in address order and builds no call graph unless the option is named, which orders the selection and notes on stderr that a callee outside it states nothing. `decompile-project` and `decompile-graph` have their own schedules and are not callee-first either; both warn on stderr when the option is asked for explicitly. `types` is the same statement without recursive components: set it if a caller's argument takes a type from a recursive callee whose own recovery is wrong about it (a member of a cycle is decompiled before the partners that call back into it, so what it states was recovered without their statements; over the 444-slice campaign corpus `cycles` moves 46 functions onto a perfect type_match and none off, 162 up and 1 down, and renders the same call arguments at every site of 15 binaries). Leave it on when a type the caller clearly knows -- a `FILE *` from `fopen`, a `char *` from `getenv` -- stops at a call and the callee's parameter stays `long`, or when the same internal callee's parameters are typed at one site and not at another. `types` and `cycles` lock no call spec, so no call gains an argument, and a vote is refused where the caller's own evidence contradicts it; the one argument a call can lose is the trailing clobbered one `argclobber` (on by default) drops where the callee's stated list and body both say the register is free, which under `cycles` includes a recursive callee (`rtarget(a0,5)` where `types` and `off` render `rtarget(a0,5,v3)`). It does change spellings, so read a changed function rather than assume it is cosmetic: a vote that wins adds a cast at the argument it types (`caller((unsigned char *)0x402000,3)`), a character pointee guessed for a pointer can split one wide constant store through it into character stores of the same bytes (`*(unsigned long *)(a0 + 0xa0) = 0` becomes eight `'\0'` stores -- the same memory contents, a different access width, which matters on memory-mapped I/O; text prints as `builtin_strncpy`, and a pointee of any other primitive type narrower than a constant stored through the pointer is refused, a buffer filled a word at a time included) or widen a narrow load into a truncation of the wider element (`*(short *)(a0 + 0xc)` becomes `(short)a0[3]` -- the same value, read at a different width), and an unsigned vote can make a caller's parameter unsigned, with casts keeping its signed uses (`(int)a0 >> 2`). A float vote is stricter than the others: it is refused unless every other use of the value is a float or a copy of its bits, so a word the caller also adds, compares, truncates, takes bytes out of or stores, or returns or passes on outside a float register, stays an integer -- where a float travels in a general register (MIPS o32, ARM softfp) a float vote there printed `(short)((unsigned int)v1 >> 0x10)` and `a2[1] = (int)v1`, value conversions of the bits. A pointer vote is held to the same standard one level down: where the caller's own loads and stores through the pointer disagree with the pointee -- an access or address outside it, an access across or inside its members, a step of other than one element, or integer bits moved through a float member -- the vote is refused, so `*a0 = (double)(a1 + 1)` never prints for a union a callee sums as doubles. Measured over 60 stripped binaries (32,406 functions: x86-64 userland, ARM Cortex-M firmware and two PE files) against main with structsynth on: the same call arguments in both arms (every one of more than 258,000), zero functions gaining a parameter of their own, no stack object split, no stack local read without a write, and no new array subscript of a structure or piece assignment; over the 444-slice campaign corpus more than 110 functions reach a perfect type_match and none leave it. Flip to `off` if a caller's parameter or local takes a type from a callee whose own recovery is wrong about it and nothing at the call site contradicts it -- the vote only loses to contrary evidence, not to a better guess. `lock` is the opt-in arity claim: it also states how many parameters the callee has, which collapses a caller that over-recovered (`ext2fs_mmp_start` renders 3 arguments and takes 1) and gains 818 call arguments at 418 sites over the x86-64 half of a 22-binary corpus -- but it FABRICATES parameters where the callee's own recovery over-counted, 155 of 7,553 x86-64 functions and 630 of 6,589 ARM Cortex-M ones gaining an argument row nothing sets, which `type_match` cannot see at all because a decompiled variable with no ground-truth counterpart is never a false positive. Use `lock` on a program where you have checked that, not as a default, and prefer `argclobber` where the complaint is a trailing register argument a previous call left behind -- `argclobber` declines a locked-and-variadic call spec, so `lock` disables it at every stated site, while `types` and `cycles` compose with it (under `cycles` a recursive callee's stated list is evidence for `argclobber` too, and its callee-body walk proves nothing about a register handed on into a cycle). Mutually exclusive with `--jobs N` when asked for explicitly (each worker process loads the binary into its own `Architecture`, so a stated type cannot cross a chunk boundary), exactly like `--assert`; a `--jobs` run under the default states nothing and says so on stderr, and `--option protoorder off` makes it byte-identical to the serial run. Set `KUNA_PROTOORDER_TRACE=1` to have each statement and each decline printed with its reason on stderr.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/prototype-source · angr · analysis-enablement · typecampaign-callee-first-prototypes
- **Example:** `option protoorder types`

### `calleevote` -- off | types | fields, default `fields`

- **Symptoms:** a callee's parameter is void * or long while every call to it passes a struct_N * or a string; a one-field getter reads *(unsigned long *)((long)a0 + 0x10) and its caller's own parameter is a synthesized record; the same record is struct_N * in the caller and void * in the function it passes it to; a wrapper that only compares or forwards a pointer keeps an integer parameter.
- **What it does:** Let the complete caller set of a function decide what its parameters are. `protoorder` carries a callee's recovered types to its callers; nothing flowed the other way, so a callee that only forwards, compares or stores a pointer kept `void *` or `long` while every one of its callers held a named record or a `char *` for the same value. A whole-binary `decompile-all` already decompiles every caller, so `types` records, after each function, the type the caller gave every argument of every direct call and the callee's own recovered parameters. After the pass a parameter the callee typed only as `void *`, `undefined1 *` or a pointer-width integer takes the type every call passes when all of these hold: the callee has no declared prototype and is not variadic; its recorded calls are exactly the direct calls and tail jumps the cross-reference walk finds (a failed or skipped caller states nothing); the image is x86-64, where code takes a function's address in one instruction the cross-reference walk reads (on AArch64, ARM, MIPS, PowerPC, RISC-V and i386 PIC an address is built from two instructions the walk does not join, so no function there qualifies, and neither does one of a relocatable object or of an image without section headers); its address is taken nowhere the image shows it -- not in code, not as a pointer-width word at an aligned offset of any section the image loads (by `SHF_ALLOC` on ELF, whatever the address, code sections included), not as a Mach-O chained-fixup rebase, a dynamic relocation, an exported symbol or the entry point -- since such a function has callers nobody can list; every call passes the argument in the storage the callee recovered it in; and every call passes the SAME committed pointer -- a named record or union that carries its layout (a synthesized `struct_N` the ledger shares, a record a program declares), a `char *` or a `char **`; a name with no layout behind it, the `FILE` shell `libctypes` interns, says no more about the object than `void *` does and is not one, so a `FILE *` is voted only where the shell carries its fields (`--option libctypes glibc`). A self-recursive call is not a vote. The callee is then decompiled again with that type as one more vote in `Varnode::getLocalType`'s fold for its input, and the vote is refused wherever the callee's own uses disagree, with the refusals `protoorder` applies to its own votes: an integer operation on the value (a pointer difference included), a family member that is type-locked, a global or frame memory, a class conflict at another call, or a load or store that does not land on exactly one member of the record (an access into a caller's filler bytes included); a `char *` is also refused where the callee stores a constant wider than a byte through the value, which would print as one character store per byte, and a `char **` where it does so through any pointer it loads through the value or stores through it (a node written into a caller's record); a pointer to a pointer some caller passes as the address of one of its own frame objects (`&cfg` of a frame record whose first member is a `char *`) types that one object, so it is refused where the callee reaches through the value anywhere but that one pointer; and any vote is refused for a value the callee adds to an address as an index (`((char *)0x1018)[a0]`). Redone functions record their calls again and the decision repeats up to three rounds, so a wrapper passes on what its own callers gave it; every round decides against the parameters the function's first decompile recovered, so a statement keeps every vote an earlier round made, and a first statement that only repeats the types a function already has is not made. The second decompile is the option's whole cost and costs what the first decompile of that function cost, so a function's printed length is what redoing it charges: the pass may reprint 5% of the lines the first pass printed, one budget for all three rounds, admitted shortest first, and a function printing at most 32 lines -- the shapes the vote exists for, a forwarder, a getter, a comparator -- is admitted even once that is spent. A function the budget cannot reach is declined for the run: the statement just decided is withdrawn, no later round proposes it, and its parameters keep what its own body found. The redo pass therefore costs a share of the binary's own decompile instead of an unbounded number of long bodies -- unbudgeted it is 10.5% of a `kmod -O2-noinline` run and 30.1% of an `mv -O0` one, over the project's +5% -- while a binary with room, `fmt -O2` at 0.2%, redoes every candidate it has. `fields` adds one more reading of the same closed caller set: a pointer parameter of a function every caller of which is a known direct call, whose pointee no declared prototype it is handed to (`pipe (int *)`) gave it, nor a callers' vote the field fits (a record, or a `char **` read as whole aligned pointers), read at exactly one constant offset other than zero with an access of four bytes or more, and not stepped through a loop from there (an address at a constant offset from it reaching a phi walks an array), is synthesized a one-field record by `structsynth` (which otherwise demands two offsets including 0), and such a function is given one more propagation pass when its main loop would end before the type lattice was ever seen settled, which is the only reason a short getter was never offered to the synthesizer. A one-field record gives way to the record every caller passes. A function whose address the image stores or code takes is never given one: a `qsort` comparator or a hash-table callback reads one field of what it was handed exactly the way a getter does, and its contract declares `void *`. An address stored other than as an aligned pointer-width word -- a function pointer at an unaligned offset of a packed struct in an image with no dynamic relocation for it, or an offset added to another address at run time (a 32-bit offset table, a relative vtable, a self-relative pointer) -- is not seen, so a callback reached only that way and also called directly can still be voted on.
- **When to flip:** On by default (`fields`) on a whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` or `decompile-project` of an x86-64 image, and inert everywhere else: on other architectures a function's address is built from two instructions the call graph does not join, so no caller set is known; `kuna decompile` forks one `decomp_dbg` per function, and a run narrowed by `--addr`, `--functions` or a triage filter, a `--jobs N` run, `decompile-project --stream`, a raw image and `--option protoorder off` have no callee-first pass to hang it on. The tell it fixes is a parameter declared `void *` or `long` in a function whose every caller passes a `struct_N *` or a string, and a one-field getter printed as `*(unsigned long *)((long)a0 + 0x10)`. Measured against `off` on the 444-slice decbench typesweep (10,748 functions, pinned metric) when the option landed, on a main scoring 1,522: 1,522 -> 1,567 perfect, mean .3553 -> .3597, 144 functions up and 3 down (all three gnulib `xmemdup`); O0 1,065 -> 1,090, O2 74 -> 80, O2-noinline 383 -> 397; `ptr_char` +143 and `ptr_ptr` +16 matched variables; under decbench#93 crediting 1,781 -> 2,133 perfect. What the redo pass may cost is a budget rather than a flat refusal: it may reprint 5% of the lines the first pass printed, one allowance for all three rounds spent shortest first, and a function printing at most 32 lines is decompiled again even once that is gone. Measured on the same tree against that budget set to zero, which is the flat 32-line bound it replaces, on a main scoring 1,609: 1,609 -> 1,615 perfect, mean .3688 -> .3697, 69 functions up and none down in that single sweep (per-row movement in one sweep is not stable; the perfect count is). With no bound at all the same tree scores 1,618. No function's exported variable count moves. Over 31 whole binaries (16,843 functions: coreutils, grep, gzip, diffutils, findutils, bzip2, tar, bash, dash, libexpat, mirai, kmod, dpkg-divert, ssh-add, crontab, init, setfacl, libedit, zlib and ARM Thumb crazyflie firmware) 1,894 functions change, none in the ARM image: 1,213 only by a `struct_N` number (a new one-field record takes a ledger slot), 677 a parameter's type and how accesses through it print, and 4 the spelling of the same memory through a record whose first field is an array (`*(unsigned long *)v1->field_0x0` for `*v1`) or a `char *` return's `NULL`. No call, argument count, parameter count or exported variable count moves, and no store is split into characters. Following a new parameter type, 23 functions declare a different number of register locals (which same-typed locals merge changes), and 24 declare as a plain integer a local that held `void *` only because a callee declared one before (dash `sub_eb30`). An array read at one constant index and nothing else reads like a getter and becomes a one-field record; its C is still exact. Speed: the option's whole cost is the second decompile, so what the redo pass reprints is what it charges, and the budget is that in the binary's own units. It reprints 96 of `fmt -O2`'s 3,718 printed lines (2.6%), 362 of `ls -O2`'s 12,833 (2.8%), 419 of `sort -O2`'s 10,708 (3.9%), 185 of `cmp -O0`'s 3,840 (4.8%), 569 of `dpkg-divert -O2`'s 11,965 (4.8%), 708 of `kmod -O2-noinline`'s 13,366 (5.3%, the 32-line floor taking it past the share) and nothing at all on `crontab -O2-noinline`, whose one candidate is 189 lines. Unbudgeted the same pass takes 10.5% of a `kmod -O2-noinline` run and 30.1% of an `mv -O0` one in wall clock, over the project's +5%. Against the flat bound it replaces, whole-run interleaved min-of-15 at both defaults: +1.6% on `kmod -O2-noinline`, `dpkg-divert -O2` and `cmp -O0`, and within noise on `crontab`, `fmt`, `ls`, `sort` and `bash -O2`. Flip to `types` if a one-field record is wrong for a program -- a buffer read at one fixed word offset declared as a record -- and to `off` if a callee takes a caller's type that its own body contradicts in a way the refusals miss; the known losing shape is a `void *` parameter (gnulib `xmemdup`) whose callers all happen to pass strings. Set `KUNA_CALLEEVOTE_TRACE=1` for each decision and its reason on stderr.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/prototype-source · angr · type-inference · typecampaign-callee-vote
- **Example:** `option calleevote fields`

### `callerptr` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a parameter is long or unsigned long while every call to it passes a struct_N *, a void * or a string; unsigned long sub_8514(void *a0,unsigned long a1) for a hash_insert whose callers pass two different records; a list or table insert keeps an integer item parameter although its callers pass malloc results; a wrapper that only forwards a pointer to a function pointer keeps an integer parameter.
- **What it does:** Declare a pointer-width parameter a pointer when every caller passes it one. `calleevote` states a parameter's type only where every direct call passes the same committed pointer (a laid-out record, a `char *`, a `char **`), so a callee whose callers hold a pointer to nothing in particular -- a `void *` from an allocator, the address of a frame object, two different records, a string beside a null -- keeps the integer its own body recovered: gnulib's `hash_insert(Hash_table *, void const *entry)` prints `unsigned long sub_8514(void *a0,unsigned long a1)` while its two callers pass a `struct_12 *` and a `struct_5 *`. On a whole-binary `decompile-all` or `decompile-project` this states a pointer for a parameter its own recovery typed only as a pointer-width integer when every recorded call passes, in exactly that storage, either the constant zero or a value its caller holds as an address for a reason of its own -- read or written through, the address of a frame object or a string literal, the result of or an argument to a declared pointer (`malloc`, `free`), or a parameter the caller's own callers stated a pointer for, judged over the value and its copies but never through a merge with other values -- and at least one passes a pointer: the callers' type where every pointer they pass is the same committed type, `void *` otherwise. A HighVariable's type alone is not enough, since a register the caller reuses for a size and a pointer is one variable typed as the pointer. The statement rides `calleevote`'s closed caller set, rounds and vote, and is refused by the same uses of the callee (an integer operation on the value, a member the pointee does not cover, a family member that is declared or global), with two differences: a call the callee hands the value to speaks only through a declared prototype, not another recovery's integer for that slot, and a pointer-width value in the frame slot at an address the function takes but never indexes (the `&matched_ent` out-parameter `hash_insert` passes on) does not refuse it; an address the callee derives from the value by a literal offset and then masks, shifts, divides or multiplies refuses it (`(p + 7) & ~7` over a `uintptr_t`), and, as for every statement the input fold takes (a strict fix in `calleevote`'s vote), a character pointer is refused for a value the callee merges with a constant, or that it or an address it derives from it compares with, adds to or subtracts from an address constant that is not a recovered string literal, which would otherwise print as a string literal ending at the table's first zero byte (`return a0 == "\x01\x02";`). A function whose statement adds nothing but these votes (any committed type in it repeats one the function already has) is decompiled again within its own budget, 2% of the lines the first pass printed (functions of at most 32 lines are always admitted), apart from `calleevote`'s 5%, so it never takes a redo from a new committed type.
- **When to flip:** On by default, and inert unless a whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` or `decompile-project` runs its callee-first pass on an x86-64 image with `calleevote` on: `kuna decompile`, `--addr`, `--functions`, `--jobs N`, `decompile-project --stream`, a raw image and `--option protoorder off` decide nothing. The tell it fixes is a parameter declared `long` or `unsigned long` in a function that only stores, compares, forwards or hands to an indirect call a value every caller holds as a pointer -- a hash-table entry, a list item, a callback's data. Measured on the 444-slice decbench sweep (published address-correspondence `type_match`, decbench 14e14b8) against main 0e35a1ff5: 244 decisions move onto the DWARF type and 1 off (a register loop counter in diffutils -O2 `diff3`'s `dotlines` that address overlap stops matching once an address temporary folds into its uses), 181 functions score better and 1 worse, perfect functions 1869 -> 1871, and the mean per-function score rises 0.4292 -> 0.4340; on the 96-binary optimized nightly sample 15 functions score better and none worse. Turn it off to keep the integer a function's own body recovered, when a script matches body text an older run printed: the retyped value prints with `(long)` casts at its integer uses and field arithmetic over it is spelled as indexing (`((unsigned long *)a0)[v2]` for `*(unsigned long *)(a0 + v2 * 8)`).
- **Where / provenance:** P4/prototype-source · kuna · type-inference · ty17-ptrargs
- **Example:** `option callerptr on`

### `callbacktype` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a qsort comparator's parameters print as unsigned long * or int * where the program declares const void *; a signal handler renders void sub_1100(void) and its ground truth takes the signal number; a pthread start routine takes a pointer-width integer instead of void *; a function reached only through a function pointer keeps whatever its own body recovered, with no prototype anywhere.
- **What it does:** Give a function whose address is handed to a library callback slot the prototype that slot declares. kuna already resolves the library's own prototype at the call site, so `qsort(dat_d148,dat_d150,0x10,sub_3a72)` renders with the name; nothing was ever said about `sub_3a72`, which is reached only through the pointer and so has no call site of its own to recover from. Its body is all it has, and that leaves a comparator `int sub_3a72(unsigned long *a0,unsigned long *a1)` and a signal handler that ignores its argument `void sub_1100(void)`. The library declares both: `qsort`'s fourth parameter is `int (*)(const void *,const void *)` and `signal`'s second is `void (*)(int)`. On a whole-binary `decompile-all` this records, at every call to one of 23 entry points that declare a function-pointer parameter (`qsort`, `bsearch`, `lfind`, `lsearch`, `signal`, `__sysv_signal`, `bsd_signal`, `sigset`, `atexit`, `on_exit`, `pthread_create`, `pthread_once`, `pthread_key_create`, `pthread_atfork`, `scandir`, `scandirat`, `ftw`, `nftw`, `tsearch`, `tfind`, `tdelete`, `tdestroy`, `glob`), the constant the callback slot carries -- the slot's argument register read from the prototype model's own assignment for that entry point's declared parameters, so the register comes from the program's convention -- and then, after every other decompile of the run, parks the slot's declared prototype on that function and decompiles that function once more -- and nothing else: every other function, a direct caller of the callback included, prints exactly what it prints with the option off. A declaration that is exactly the signature the body already printed -- the same parameter types in the same order, the same return, no `...`, as a `pthread_once` routine recovered `void f(void)` is -- is not parked. The park is the same seam `protoorder lock` uses (`Architecture::set_function_prototype_pieces_at`, read back by `ActionDefaultParams`), so it moves the callback's ARITY: 16 of the 50 scored callbacks in the decbench corpus are handlers that never read `edi`, where the parameter has to appear. On a successful park the statements the run made about that function (`protoorder`'s recovered types, `calleevote`'s decision) are dropped so its own redo reads the declaration alone. Fourteen things refuse it: a declared prototype already covers the function (DWARF, a user `--assert`, the libc tables, and under `--option protoorder lock` the callee's own recovered prototype, parked in the same place) and outranks this one; two callback slots disagree about the same address; a direct call its caller already printed contradicts the declaration -- it passes another number of arguments (clang -O0 passing an `idiv` remainder left in `rdx` to a comparator, clang -O2 forwarding its own registers untouched and printing the call with none) or uses a result the declaration does not return -- or sits in code the run did not decompile, since no caller is ever decompiled again; a direct call site reads more of the return register than the declared return holds (a `long` comparator returning a zero-extended comparison writes only `eax`, but the call that hands the whole `rax` to `printf("%ld")` would print `CONCAT44(dat_4,zcmp(..))` once `int` is declared, and a comparator whose result another comparator returns straight through its own `ret` would leave that outer one returning a register half of which nothing set); the address reaches somewhere the callback arguments do not explain -- the function is exported, is the entry point, is stored as a pointer-width word of a loaded section, is a Mach-O chained-fixup or dynamic-relocation target, has a cross-reference materializing its address in a function that handed it to no slot, has more such cross-references than there were callback arguments (a function in a dispatch table that is also passed to `qsort` is not declared by the `qsort` call), or was USED by a registering body somewhere no slot accounts for -- the cross-reference walk counts address-taking instructions, and one hoisted `lea` feeds `signal(SIG,f); atexit(f);` from a single instruction, so the bodies answer for the uses, following the value through copies, phis and the INDIRECTs calls leave, and counting a write of it into a global or an address-taken local as a use even when nothing reads it back; the function's own recovery found MORE inputs than the declaration passes (the parked list is closed, so a three-argument function cast into `qsort`'s slot would lose its third argument at every direct call site and read it uninitialized); it found FEWER and anything calls or tail-jumps to the function directly (the closed list would materialize the missing argument at each such site out of whatever the register last held: `signal(SIGALRM,(void (*)(int))cleanup); ... cleanup();` on a `void cleanup(void)` would print `cleanup(v2)` after an invented `v2 = 0x2006;`) -- with NO direct call site the shorter list is parked by design, since the slot is then the only caller and the binary cannot tell `void h(int unused)` from a cast, and the unread parameter is exported to `--json` as an `arg` with empty `line_numbers` and `addresses`; an input its own recovery found is not inside the storage the declaration gives that position, with or without a direct caller (a `struct ctx *` routine cast into `signal`'s `void (*)(int)` reads all eight bytes of the register the slot declares a four-byte `int` in, so the declaration would rebuild the pointer as `CONCAT44` of half a register and an unset one and print a direct call as `cleanup((int)G)`); the body reads the argument register one past the declared list before writing it (the one-sided entry walk `calleedeadarg` caches -- it sees reads, not liveness, so a body that forwards its arguments in a tail call states nothing and is held by the recovered-arity refusal instead); the signature says `void` and every live RETURN hands back a value the body computed; the signature returns a value and the body computes none (the register's leftover would print as an invented return, e.g. `(void *)CONCAT44(dat_4,puts(a0))` for a `void` start routine in `pthread_create`'s slot) -- a body whose every live RETURN is reached from a direct call along a straight line of machine code (fall-through and unconditional jumps, read from the image) that writes no byte of the callee's DECLARED output, where that output covers every byte of the declared return, does compute it, so `return strcmp(a,b);`, which recovers `void` on its own because nothing reads its result, is declared `int` whether the call is a `jmp` or `call; leave; ret`, while a value that reaches the RETURN through a join or past a conditional branch is not proved and is refused; the value handed back -- computed by the body, or the declared output of the call the proof traced it to -- is wider than the storage of the declared return (a `long` comparator cast into `qsort`'s `int` slot would subtract in the low half, and a direct caller printing the whole result would read its high half back as `CONCAT44(dat_4,...)`) -- measured by the bits the value can set, so an `int` comparator whose 32-bit result x86-64 zero-extends into an 8-byte `rax` output is parked when nothing calls it directly; the value the body computes is NARROWER than the declared return and the machine code, walked from the entry over every path, does not leave the bytes above it zero at every RETURN (a `signed char` comparator that clang compiles to `mov (%rdi),%al; sub (%rsi),%al; ret`, or a `bool` start routine that is `setg %al; ret`, leaves the rest of the register as its caller left it, and declared it printed `CONCAT31`/`CONCAT71` of a variable nothing sets; gcc's `movzbl` then `sub %al`, an `xor %eax,%eax` before the `setg`, and any 32-bit write leave zero there and are parked); or the prototype model cannot place the declared parameters (or this run never decompiled the function, so there are no body facts to check). `__cxa_atexit` is deliberately NOT one of the 23: glibc's `<stdlib.h>` rewrites `atexit(f)` into `__cxa_atexit(f,0,__dso_handle)` with `f` cast from `void (*)(void)`, so the slot's declared `void (*)(void *)` would give every `atexit` handler in a glibc program a parameter its source never wrote; `sigaction` is absent because its handler is a structure member, not an argument; `qsort_r` is absent because glibc and musl pass its comparator fourth while macOS and FreeBSD before 14 pass an opaque data pointer there, and the imported name does not say which library the image links. On an architecture whose code builds an address from two instructions (AArch64 `adrp`+`add`, MIPS `lui`+`addiu`, ARM `movw`+`movt`, i386 PIC) the cross-reference walk cannot see the address taken, so the escape question has no answer and nothing is parked.
- **When to flip:** On by default, and inert unless a whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` or `decompile-project` decompiles the caller that registers the callback. It fires on a program that registers one -- a `qsort` comparator, a `signal` handler, a `pthread_create` start routine -- where the tell is a comparator whose parameters print as `unsigned long *` or `int *` instead of `void *`, or a handler declared `void sub_1100(void)` whose ground truth takes the signal number. Measured over the 444-slice decbench corpus (coreutils, grep, gzip, diffutils, bzip2, findutils, tar, shadow, x at O0/O2/O2-noinline): 294 callback arguments name 114 distinct functions, 50 of which decbench scores, and all 50 DWARF declarations are exactly the slot's signature -- none contradicted, none reached through two disagreeing slots. 67 ground-truth parameters move, of which 16 are a parameter kuna recovers no trace of. Inert outside a callee-first whole-binary pass: `kuna decompile` forks one `decomp_dbg` per function, and a `--jobs N` run, `decompile-project --stream` and `--option protoorder off` have no pass to hang it on (a `--jobs N` run parks nothing unless the option is named, and naming it alongside `--jobs N` is refused). The flip evidence -- datatests, stages, the 444-slice typesweep with every worse row read, gained and lost parameters checked against DWARF, whole-binary hunks, speed and casts -- is docs/features/callbacktype/default-on-evaluation.md. Flip it off if a program passes the same function to two different libraries' callbacks through one slot the table names, or if the declared `void *` of a comparator is less useful to you than the `struct_N *` `structsynth` synthesizes for the same pointee -- the declared type wins, which is the one place the two options disagree. Set `KUNA_CALLBACKTYPE_TRACE=1` for each decision and its reason on stderr.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/prototype-source · ida · type-inference · typecampaign-callback-slot
- **Example:** `option callbacktype on`

### `callrettype` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a call to a function the same listing declares char * prints (char *)sub_43ee(a0); v7 = (char *)sub_e8ca(4,(char *)sub_43ee(a0));; a caller converts a call's result to the type the callee is declared to return; (FILE *)f(a0) under FILE * f(int a0).
- **What it does:** A call's result takes the return type its callee's own recovery gave it earlier in the same callee-first run. Upstream's `TypeOpCall::getOutputLocal` answers only for a LOCKED output, so a call to a function the same listing declares `char * sub_43ee(unsigned long *a0)` produced an unknown of its width, and every caller that kept the result as a `char *` printed `(char *)sub_43ee(a0)`; the 2026-09-24 cast census counted 1,994 `(char *)<call>` casts on the 4,815 functions kuna and IDA both emit (IDA 1,172), 682 of them on a callee whose own listing already declared `char *`. When on, `decompile-all` records after each function's final decompile its recovered return value (storage, width, type) when that is a pointer, an integer wider than a byte or a float, the function has no declared prototype, and every live RETURN hands back a value the body computed or read out of global memory (`kuna_callrettype::record`); a later call whose output sits in exactly that storage and width takes the type as the CALL output's local type: the def-side vote of `Varnode::getLocalType`, and the type the call produces when `ActionSetCasts` asks whether its result needs converting. Nothing is locked, so no call gains or loses an argument or a result, and a `void` callee states nothing. The vote is refused where the caller holds better evidence: the family refusals `protoorder` applies to an argument vote (an integer operation on a pointer, a float conflict, a record the caller reads past), an integer statement whose signedness an ordered comparison, a shift, a division, an extension, a declared parameter or another declared or stated call result in the same value contradicts, or a widening at the other sign that the p-code no longer spells, of the result or a value computed from it at its width, where it leaves the function: returned (on x86-64 every 32-bit write zero-extends into the whole register, so a -O0 reload or a move back from the register the result was kept in across another call keeps the function's return unsigned) or passed to a parameter whose zero-extension the dead-bit trimming dropped (`mov %eax,%edi` before a callee that reads all of `%rdi`), a pointer statement a declared parameter, or another declared or stated call result in the same value, types as a pointer to a different known pointee, and a pointer statement whose pointee the caller reads or writes at another width, offsets or steps by other than whole elements, or (for `void *`) offsets at all, counting everything else the function returns when it returns the result. Another call result of the other class (an integer beside a pointer) in the same value refuses it, and so does a value loaded through the pointer that flows back into its own variable. A byte (`bool` or character) is not stated. The finished caller is audited (`kuna_callrettype::contradicted`): the merge ties the return register whole-function after types are inferred, so a statement whose variable also holds another call's result of the other class, a number that is not an address, a value loaded through the pointer or a sum of integers, or whose result the function returns beside such a number, is withdrawn for that caller and the caller decompiled again (du -O0 `map_inode_number` otherwise printed `long * sub_6b45`, `(long *)0xffffffffffffffff` and an integer assigned to the pointer); a function over 1,000 p-code ops is not audited. Inert without a callee-first pass (`kuna decompile`, `--addr`, `--functions`, `--jobs N`, `--option protoorder off`). On the 45-binary cast corpus casts on the 4,815 shared functions go 35,588 -> 34,808 (0.941x -> 0.920x IDA): 393 functions fewer, 25 more, each a conversion where two recovered types now meet (a pointer result stored into an integer field, a pointer difference, a callee's pointer in a caller that keeps an integer).
- **When to flip:** On by default: `decompile-all` and `decompile-project` type a call's result with the return type the same listing prints for the callee, so a caller that keeps a `char *` result prints `v1 = sub_43ee(a0);` instead of `v1 = (char *)sub_43ee(a0);`. Set it off to diff against output from before the option existed, or where a callee's recovered return type is known to be wrong and should not reach its callers. It never changes a call's arguments or whether a result is read, and it does nothing for a single-function `kuna decompile`.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/output-prototype · kuna · type-inference · kuna-callrettype
- **Example:** `option callrettype off`

### `narrowret` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a function declared unsigned char sub_x(...) whose callers hold the result in an unsigned int; v1 = sub_8017ac6(a0); with unsigned int v1 beside unsigned char sub_8017ac6; a bool-returning callee's result kept in an int and only tested; an x86-64 unsigned-int-returning callee's result held in an unsigned long.
- **What it does:** A call reads the narrow value its callee returns. A function that returns a `uint8_t`, a `uint16_t`, a `bool` or (x86-64, AArch64) an `unsigned int` hands it back in a whole register, and a caller that relies on the callee having zero-extended it -- AAPCS requires it, and an x86-64 callee's own `movzbl` or 32-bit write performs it -- reads the register at full width, so the CALL's output is register-wide and every local holding the result is declared `unsigned int` or `unsigned long`, however narrow the callee's own listing prints its return. The callee's decompile already narrows a returned value whose upper bits the nonzero-bit analysis proves clear: `SubvariableFlow`'s RETURN pull trims the RETURN to the narrow value. When on, each such trim records on the RETURN whether every trim from the whole return register on dropped only known-zero bits, and in the callee-first `decompile-all` run a function whose every live RETURN carries that record, or hands back unchanged the result of a call to a callee that states the same storage (a wrapper), states it (`kuna_narrowret::record`) with the type its listing declares, when that is a `bool` for a truth value (one byte that every RETURN computes as a comparison or a constant 0 or 1) or an unsigned integer of the width for a value that can set its top bit (an enum of small numbers is as often an `int`); the proof shows a zero extension and no sign, so a callee declared signed states nothing. At a later call to it whose recovered output is a wider part of that register holding the narrow storage as its low part, and whose variable takes no value but such calls' results and constants of the width (a result merged with other values, or returned beside them, keeps the register), `ActionActiveReturn` makes the CALL write the narrow value and zero-extends it back into the old output (`narrow_call_output`): every reader sees the bits it read before, now as the zero extension the callee performed, and the sub-variable and type passes can declare the value at its own width. A one-byte call then produces the type the callee declares (the def-side vote of `TypeOpCall::getOutputLocal`, so `ActionSetCasts` converts it where the caller keeps it otherwise), and a stated truth value marks the CALL a calculated boolean, which `boolbyte` counts as a truth-valued definition beside every other value the byte takes. A declared prototype, an indirect call, a sign-extended or signed return and a return any trim narrowed from bits not known to be zero state nothing. Inert without a callee-first pass (`kuna decompile`, `--addr`, `--functions`, `--jobs N`, `--option protoorder off`): a function decompiled alone narrows its own return exactly as with the option off.
- **When to flip:** On by default. The tell it fixes is a `uint8_t`, `uint16_t` or `bool` returned by a function the same listing declares `unsigned char`, `unsigned short` or `bool`, held by its callers in an `unsigned int` local (ARM firmware), or an `unsigned int` result held in an `unsigned long` on x86-64. Set it off to get the register-wide call results back, or when an `int` or enum local that holds a narrow callee's result should keep its source width; the C computes the same values either way. A caller may print an explicit widening of the narrow result (`(unsigned int)v1 * 3`) where it computes with it at register width.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/output-prototype · kuna · type-inference · ty17-narrow-call-results
- **Example:** `option narrowret off`

### `spillargtrial` -- off | reload | spill, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** call rendered with fewer arguments than the disassembly passes when the missing argument register is spilled to the frame before the call; floating-point argument dropped at the FIRST of several calls that reuse the same value; a spurious 4-byte stack local appears where a call argument should be; clang -O2 packed-double code calls atan2 with one argument instead of two; argument register stored to a caller-frame slot and reloaded after the call is not recognized as an argument.
- **What it does:** Tolerate the caller's own caller-save spill of an argument when scoring an active input trial. Funcdata::onlyOpUse (funcdata_varnode.cc:1891) answers whether the Varnode reaching a CALL in a candidate parameter register is used ONLY as that call's argument, and it rejects on ANY CPUI_STORE among the Varnode's descendants; checkInputTrialUse then calls markInactive, which also sets CHECKED, so the trial is never re-scored and the argument-producing chain dies to dead-code elimination. That blanket rejection also rejects the opposite idiom: on x86-64 SysV NO xmm register is callee-saved, so a floating-point value that is both an argument and live across the call MUST be spilled by the caller, and the spill is a second descendant of the very Varnode the trial is scoring. At `reload` the STORE stops rejecting only when it writes the walked Varnode's own value (operand 2, never the pointer) into a caller-frame slot AND a later LOAD reads that slot back at the same width, i.e. a genuine caller-save spill/reload pair. Since ActionActiveParam runs before ActionStackPtrFlow, the frame reference is still the raw INT_ADD(stack pointer, #const) and the reload straddles the call that re-defines the stack pointer, so the search walks forward from the store's own base Varnode carrying the running offset delta rather than matching raw constants. At `spill` the reload requirement is dropped and any caller-frame store of the value is tolerated. This is a deliberate DIVERGENCE from upstream, not a port fix: the rule it relaxes exists precisely to stop a value the caller writes to its frame before a call from becoming a bogus extra argument.
- **When to flip:** Turn ON (`reload`) when a call is rendered with FEWER arguments than the disassembly passes and the missing argument's register is spilled to the frame just before the call -- the canonical rendering is `atan2(SUB168(v1,0));` from clang -O2 packed-double code that calls atan2 more than once, where `movapd XMMWORD PTR [rsp+0x20],xmm1` is the caller-save spill and `movaps xmm1,XMMWORD PTR [rsp+0x20]` after the call is its reload. The dropped argument often leaves a spurious 4-byte stack local in its place (`unsigned int v5; // stack - 0x18`). PREFER `reload` OVER `spill`: `spill` admits any frame store of the value, which fabricates arguments out of ordinary local writes -- measured on a clang -O2 inlined 64-byte memcpy, `spill` turns `sptr2(&v1,a0)` into `sptr2(v1,v5,v9,v13,&v1,a0)`, four arguments invented from the four `movaps` stores that fill the local buffer, while `reload` correctly declines because nothing reads those slots back. Use `spill` only to bisect whether the reload requirement is what is blocking a recovery. DEFAULT OFF: the failure mode of relaxing upstream's rule is a SPURIOUS TRAILING ARGUMENT, and no gate can see one -- the datatest corpus is prototype-declared and GED is blind to arity -- so the option ships as an opt-in with its evidence rather than as a default. Flip back off if a call gains an argument the disassembly does not pass, or if an argument appears whose value is a stale pre-call definition (that second shape is calloverlap's territory: the two options compose, and on the GH-275 copysign variant only `calloverlap full` plus `spillargtrial reload` gives both the right arity and the right values).
- **Where / provenance:** P4/active-input-trial-scoring · kuna · opt-in-tool · GH-275
- **Example:** `option spillargtrial reload`

### `regionstructure` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** goto placement follows the sailr region walk instead of ghidra's collapse order (flip off to force CollapseStructure); uncompilable c where a loop body folded into a while condition; structuring differs from upstream ghidra on the same function.
- **What it does:** Structure the CFG by walking the KunaRegionIdentifier region tree and matching angr Phoenix/SAILR schemas (acyclic sequence + ITE + cyclic loops [Inc 3] + acyclic switch-case [Inc 4], with the SAILR H1/H3-ordered virtualize-to-goto fallback) instead of running Ghidra's CollapseStructure. DIV-12 default-on: the primary structuring path. Byte-identical to Ghidra's CollapseStructure on reducible code; falls back to CollapseStructure on irreducible (multi-entry) loops.
- **When to flip:** On by default (DIV-12): the region-driven structurer is the primary S8 path. It is byte-identical to Ghidra on reducible code and falls back to CollapseStructure when a function cannot be collapsed to a single structured root (irreducible/multi-entry loops). Set OFF to force the upstream Ghidra CollapseStructure path unconditionally.
- **Where / provenance:** P8/goto-quality · angr · structure-recovery · angr-region-structurer
- **Example:** `option regionstructure on`

### `guardarm` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** guard clause with a fatal no-return call comes out inverted and the whole body is nested inside the if; the function's only return sits inside an if-arm and the body ends on a no-return call; kuna negates a guard condition that ida and ghidra leave alone; a leading validation guard is emitted at the tail of the function.
- **What it does:** Break the ARM TIE in CollapseStructure::ruleBlockIfNoExit by code layout instead of by out-index. The rule folds the condition block and ONE terminal out-arm into a BlockIf; the other arm survives as the fall-through, so the pick decides which half of the function is nested inside the `if`. Upstream walks the out-edges in index order and takes the first eligible one (in-degree 1, out-degree 0, a decision edge).
