- **What it does:** Leave out an integer widening on an arm of the conditional `iteregion` prints, `dest = c ? (int)*(char *)p : 0;`, when the conditional operator performs that conversion itself. The second and third operands of `?:` undergo the usual arithmetic conversions (C11 6.5.15p5), integer promotion first, so the `char` arm above is converted to `int` whether or not the cast is written, and the same diamond printed as if/else already has no cast (`castimplied`). `castimplied` refuses the arms because leaving one arm's cast out can change the type of the whole conditional (`c ? (long)i : u` is a `long`, `c ? i : u` an `unsigned int` for `int i` and `unsigned int u`). When on, `kuna_castternary` leaves the cast out only when it is a value-preserving integer widening (never a narrowing, a sign change, a conversion from or to bool, an enum, a float or a pointer), when the usual arithmetic conversions of the two arms give the cast's target type both with the cast and without it, and when the conditional is assigned to a variable declared with an integer type. The conditional then converts the arm to that type itself and keeps its own type and value, so the assignment stores what it stored before (a pointer-declared destination, a merged variable, keeps its casts). Each arm's C type is carried as the set of promoted types (`int`, `unsigned int`, the signed and unsigned 8-byte integers) it may have: one type for a declared variable, a cast that stays or a load through a pointer printed with its pointee; every promotion its width allows for an expression nothing states the type of; for a literal, the type C gives the token the printer writes (base, suffix and magnitude: `0xffffffff` is `unsigned int`, `3000000000` is `long`). The conversions must give the target for every combination. When both arms carry a cast, both go only when the conditional over both bare operands still has that type, else one of them. Only where `int` is 4 bytes, and C output only (Rust's `if c { a } else { b }` needs both arms of one type). On the 45-binary cast corpus casts on the 4,815 functions kuna and IDA both emit go 37,477 -> 37,474 (2 functions fewer, 0 more; gcc -O0 conditionals over a byte are rare there); 0/675 datatest assertions and no existing stage assertion move, and the 444-slice typesweep is identical on all 10,748 functions.
- **When to flip:** On by default: `v2 = c ? *(char *)p : 0;` rather than `v2 = c ? (int)*(char *)p : 0;`. Set it off to get every arm cast `iteregion` printed before the option existed, for example when diffing against older output. It never changes the conditional's type, so the value assigned, passed or compared is the same bit for bit.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/cast-policy · kuna · presentation-default · kuna-castternary
- **Example:** `option castternary off`

### `castwiden` -- off | on | literal, default `literal`

- **Symptoms:** an int widened to long beside a long operand, ((long *)a0)[1] + (long)a1; a widened index times a literal, (long)i * 8 + 0x2b200; v = (unsigned long)i; into a variable already declared unsigned long; a store of (long)i through a long pointer; memchr(p,c,(long)n) for an int n.
- **What it does:** Leave out a 64-bit widening that C's own conversions perform. `CastStrategyC::isExtensionCastImplied` (cast.cc:249) hides an `INT_SEXT`/`INT_ZEXT` only when an arithmetic or comparison op reads it beside an explicit variable of the same metatype, so kuna prints `((long *)a0)[1] + (long)a1`, `v2 % (long)a1` over a structure field, `(long)i * 0xc + 7`, and `v = (unsigned long)i;` into an `unsigned long v`. With `on`, `kuna_castwiden` decides at print time, with the IR unchanged: the widening of an operand of `+ - * / % & | ^` goes when, for every type the other operand may have as printed (a declared variable, a cast that stays, a load through a pointer printed as a declared variable, a cast, a structure field or an element, a literal, or an arithmetic expression over those), the usual arithmetic conversions (C11 6.3.1.8) give the operation the type it had and that type is the cast's own or the cast keeps the operand's value (an integer conversion depends only on the value converted, 6.3.1.3); and the extension is the one C performs on the operand's printed type, a sign-extension of a signed type and a zero-extension of an unsigned one. Of two widened operands only the right one's cast goes, so the survivor keeps the operation 64-bit; one widened value read by both operands (`(long)i * (long)i`) keeps both casts. The bare operand keeps the parentheses the cast gave it (`p[1] + (a1 + a2)`), and beside a chain of its own operator, which the printer writes without parentheses and C regroups (`x + (y + z)` prints `x + y + z`), the left operand's cast goes only when the chain's first leaf would let it go. `castimplied`'s destinations widen too, for a widening to eight bytes of an operand printed as a C integer: a widening that does not keep the value (`(unsigned long)i` of an `int`) goes into a destination declared with exactly its spelling, where the assignment, argument or return conversion is that very conversion (6.5.16.1p2, 6.5.2.2p7, 6.8.6.4p3); a value-keeping one also goes into an 8-byte integer of the other signedness (`memchr(p,c,n)` for an `int n`); and a store through a pointer printed as a declared variable, a cast, a field or an element is a destination like an assignment (`((long *)a0)[1] = a1;`). With `literal`, an operand beside an integer literal goes too, and the literal, an 8-byte constant in the IR that C would type `int`, is printed with the suffix of its width (`L`, or `UL` for an unsigned target) so C converts the other operand itself: `a0 * 0xcL + 7`; a literal whose value the suffix would change (a negated unsigned literal such as `-0x80000000`) keeps the cast. Never touched: comparisons (castsign's domain), a shift's operands, unary minus, a widening beside a signed operand of the other signedness that would change the operation's type (`(unsigned long)c + l` for a `long l`), narrowings, widenings to fewer than eight bytes, float, pointer and bool conversions, varargs positions and untrusted prototypes, and an operand whose printed type is unknown or not the IR's. Only where `int` is 4 bytes, and C output only. On the 45-binary cast corpus casts on the 4,815 functions kuna and IDA both emit go 35,588 -> 34,061 with `literal` (0.941x -> 0.901x IDA; 29.9 -> 28.7 per 100 statements against IDA's 27.0), 481 functions fewer and 0 more; every changed line over 64 binaries (2,341 functions) parses to the same C tree with the removed casts typed from the declarations and each conversion shown to give the same type and value (semhunks.py), and the 444-slice typesweep is identical on all 10,748 functions.
- **When to flip:** `literal` by default: a widening C's usual arithmetic and assignment conversions perform prints no cast (`((long *)a0)[1] + a1`, `v1 = a0;` into an `unsigned long v1`, `((long *)a0)[1] = a1;`), and a widened index or offset beside an 8-byte literal reads `i * 8L + base`, as IDA's `8LL * i + base` does. `on` keeps every literal unsuffixed and only drops the casts that need no literal typed. Set it off to get every widening upstream prints, for example when diffing against Ghidra; the value computed is the same in all three.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/cast-policy · ida · presentation-default · kuna-castwiden
- **Example:** `option castwiden literal`

### `castnarrow` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a truncation assigned to a variable already declared that type, v1 = (unsigned int)a0; with unsigned int v1; return (int)x; from a function declared int; a long passed to a declared int parameter as toupper((int)a0); a byte store through a char pointer written *a1 = (char)a0;; kuna prints a narrowing cast IDA leaves to C's assignment conversion.
- **What it does:** Leave out a narrowing cast that C's own conversion performs where the value lands. `castimplied` leaves out widenings and keeps every truncation and sign change, so kuna prints `v1 = (unsigned int)a0;` into an `unsigned int v1` from a `long a0`, `*a1 = (char)a0;` through a `char *a1`, `toupper((int)a0)`, and `return (int)x;` from a function declared `int`. C converts the right operand of `=` to the type of the left (C11 6.5.16.1p2), an argument to its parameter's type under a prototype (6.5.2.2p7) and a returned value to the return type (6.8.6.4p3), and an integer conversion depends only on the value converted and the type converted to (6.3.1.3), so `T v = (T)e;` stores what `T v = e;` stores for any integer `e`. When on, `kuna_castnarrow` decides at print time, with the IR unchanged, for a low `SUBPIECE` printed as a cast, a `CPUI_CAST` between integer types, and the `(T)name` the printer writes for the low piece of a wider variable: the cast goes when its value lands whole in a plain `lhs = (T)e;` statement whose local or parameter is declared with exactly `T`'s spelling (not an arm of `c ? a : b`, not a stack-view compound literal), a store through a pointer printed with pointee `T` (a declared `T *`, a cast, a field or an element; not a bitfield or stack-view store), a direct call argument whose type-locked parameter is spelled `T` (never a trial prototype, a varargs position, a per-call-site override or an argument `truncarg` narrowed), or `return` from a function declared `T`; and `T` is a plain integer while the operand prints as an integer: a declared variable (an unknown type the printer spells as an integer counts), a cast, a load through a typed pointer, integer arithmetic over those, or a shift of one; a piece of a variable needs that variable declared with exactly its own type. A constant, a call, `bool`, an enum, a float or a pointer on either side keeps the cast, and so does a narrowing read by arithmetic, by a comparison, under another conversion, or into a destination of another spelling (`*a1 = (int)a0;` through an `unsigned int *a1` stays). Only where `int` is 4 bytes, and C output only: Rust has no implicit integer conversions. Over 10 stripped decbench binaries (O0 ls, bzip2, dash, gzip, xmlwf; O2 sort, grep, diff, find, kmod) under `--mode aggressive`, 218 casts go (19,784 -> 19,566, 169.3 -> 167.4 per 1,000 lines) in 115 of 3,809 functions and no function gains one; every changed line is the old line with integer casts removed, each into an assignment, a store or a call argument of exactly its type; 0/675 datatest assertions move.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a narrowing C performs at an assignment, a store, a prototyped argument or a return prints no cast -- `v1 = a0;` into an `unsigned int v1`, `*a1 = a0;` through a `char *`, `toupper(a0)`, `return x;` from an `int` function. Set it off to see every truncation and sign change ActionSetCasts and the partial-variable printer write, as upstream prints them.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/cast-policy · ida · presentation-default · kuna-castnarrow
- **Example:** `option castnarrow on`

### `ptrdepthcap` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a local is declared with three or more levels of pointer indirection; unsigned long long ***** or char ***** appears in the output; C++ std::string / ostringstream locals get absurd pointer types; the type of a stack object grows one pointer level per decompilation pass.
- **What it does:** Refuse to deepen an already unsatisfiable pointer equation while `ActionInferTypes` propagates types. A small-string-optimized C++ object (MSVC `std::basic_string`, an `ostringstream` buffer) writes `T == ptr(T)` into the type lattice: one MULTIEQUAL edge carries `p = &obj` (a `PTRSUB(spacebase,-0xN)`, typed pointer-to-the-mapped-local) and the other carries `p = obj.ptr` (a LOAD from that same address, typed as the local itself), because the SSO union stores either the characters or a pointer to them in the same 8 bytes. No finite type satisfies that, so `propagateOneType` adds exactly ONE pointer level per pass and only stops at the empirical seven-pass settle ceiling -- the object, and every temporary that touches it, is then declared `unsigned long long *****` / `char *****`. Upstream Ghidra already refuses to build such a chain at the one seam it noticed, `TypeFactory::getTypePointerNoDepth` (`type.cc:1509`, used by `TypeOpLoad`/`TypeOpStore::propagateType`), but the spacebase-PTRSUB arm that actually drives this escalation never routes through it. When on, `kuna_ptrdepth::cap_pointer_depth` applies that same rule at the single propagation funnel: a candidate whose target is itself a pointer-to-pointer collapses to `ptr(undefined<N>)`, and `ptr(ptr(undefined<N>))` collapses one more level when `N` is the pointer width. `ptr(undefined<N>)` is a fixed point, so the lattice settles instead of running to the ceiling. Depth 1 and depth 2 over a concrete base are untouched, so `char **argv`, `char **envp` and a real pointer-to-pointer parameter keep their spelling.
- **When to flip:** The emitted C declares locals with three or more levels of indirection that the binary plainly does not have -- most visibly `unsigned long long *****` / `char *****` around C++ std::string / ostringstream objects in MSVC binaries, where the false types dominate the listing and hide which buffer holds which string. Default OFF in the catalog (it changes inferred types, and the datatest corpus pins the upstream spellings) but ON in the `aggressive` preset, which `auto` selects for anything under 500 KiB -- so it is the default rendering of `kuna decompile`, `decompile-all`, `decompile-project` and the web front-end. Flip OFF to restore upstream Ghidra's unbounded escalation. Measured over 90 binaries / 22,307 functions (RE dataset, ELF + PE, `decompile-all` both arms): 103 functions change (0.46%), three-or-more-star occurrences fall 1,617 -> 28 and the functions carrying one 80 -> 17, and ZERO call sites are lost or gained. Every residual difference is an addressing SPELLING -- `*(char *)((long long)v + N)` becomes `v[N]`, `v = (T ****)((long long)v + N)` becomes `v = &v[N]` -- except one named cost: where the object really is an array of 8-byte pointers, an 8-byte zero store re-renders as eight one-byte stores (12 such lines across the whole sweep, in 2 functions). Speed -0.12% on a 1,027-function binary where the option is inert, +5.3% whole-binary on the witness where 1 of 144 functions changes (~40 ms, all of it in that one function).
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · kuna · type-inference · kuna-ptrdepthcap
- **Example:** `option ptrdepthcap on`

### `calltargettype` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** an indirect call through a table entry prints (**(void **)p)(), which does not compile; a local holding a function pointer is declared void * and called as (*v1)(a1,7); a parameter, global or struct field holding a function pointer is declared void * and its call does not compile; a DWARF function-pointer parameter or field prints void *; called object is not a function or function pointer when the output is compiled.
- **What it does:** Give the target of an indirect call the function-pointer type the call itself states. Type recovery types a call target `code *`, a pointer to a function of unknown signature, which C cannot spell: under `ctypes` kuna prints it `void *`, so every call through one -- a dispatch table entry, a callback held in a local, a parameter, a global, an `ops->fn` field -- is a call of a `void *` that no C compiler accepts (`(**(void **)&tbl[a0 * 8UL])();`). With `on` (and `ctypes` on; without it the upstream `code *` spelling is left alone), `kuna_calltargettype` runs once every variable has its final type, just before casts are decided: for each indirect call it builds `R (*)(A1,..,An)` from the type of the call's output (`void` when it has none) and the type of each argument it passes (`void *` for an argument printed as an address computed from a base, `&v4` or `&a1[2]`), and keeps it only when the default model lays every parameter and the result out in the storage the call uses -- a `float` held as an `unsigned int` in `xmm0` or `s0`, or a `double`'s bits in `rdi`, would compile to a call that passes something else -- and no value the call overwrites is read after it. The storage the call goes through takes that type when every call through it states the same one and nothing it meets fixes another: a local; in C output also a parameter, whose prototype is declared with it (`int viaparam(int (*a0)(unsigned int,unsigned long),unsigned int a1)`), and a global; a local that receives a function's address only when that function's declared prototype is exactly the call's type; and a field of a synthesized record, which the project header declares with the type every call through it in the export agrees on (`void (*field_0x10)(void);`). In C output a target that still cannot be called -- its calls disagree, it is also used as data, or a declaration says `void *` -- is cast to its call's type at each call instead, and with the option on the C cast strategy treats a record's declaration and its completed definition as one type, so the casts between them go. The DWARF mapper, at load, maps a pointer to a prototyped `DW_TAG_subroutine_type` to a function pointer of that prototype, so DWARF parameters, fields and locals that hold a function pointer are declared as one (`unsigned long (*hasher)(void *,unsigned long);`). Rust output, which spells every pointer to code `*const ()`, is unchanged. On decbench -O2 gzip, dash, diff and bash under `decompile-project --mode aggressive` and gcc 11, the `called object is not a function` errors fall from 63 to 0 and the casts of `decompile-all` from 17,288 to 16,687; gcc's incompatible-pointer-type warnings rise from 247 to 312, where a function whose recovered prototype differs from the DWARF slot it is passed to was passed to a `void *` before.
- **When to flip:** On by default: an indirect call's target takes the function-pointer type the call states, so a call through a table entry, a local, a parameter, a global or a record field compiles as C. It acts only with `ctypes` on, as `auto` at every size, `aggressive` and `fast` run (without it, as under an explicit `--mode reliable`, the upstream `code *` spelling is left alone), and never on Rust output. Set it off to get the upstream spelling of every call target back, for example when diffing against Ghidra.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · kuna · type-inference · GH-869
- **Example:** `option calltargettype off`

### `ptrfromuse` -- off | byte | void, default `void`

- **Symptoms:** a parameter is declared long or unsigned long and is only ever dereferenced; every use of an argument is *(T *)(a0 + k) but the argument is not a pointer; one function takes T *a0 and its sibling takes long a0 for the same kind of argument; an argument dereferenced at offset 0 gets a pointer type but one dereferenced at +8 does not.
- **What it does:** Type a function parameter that is only ever used as a memory base as a pointer. `ActionInferTypes` seeds every Varnode from local op semantics and then pushes the seeds along the def-use graph, and neither half can reach a parameter the function dereferences at a constant offset. `TypeOpIntAdd::getInputLocal` votes `int<N>` for each `p + k` reader, so the seed fold has no pointer candidate at all; the pointer that DOES exist -- `TypeOp::propagateToPointer` types the `p + 8` result `undefined8 *` -- never travels back, because `TypeOpIntAdd::propagateType` (typeop.cc:1217) refuses to carry a pointer from an output to an input. coreutils fmt -O2 with `libctypes off` shows both halves at once: `put_word`, which dereferences its argument at offset 0, is `void sub_3000(unsigned long *a0)`, while `get_line`, which dereferences the same kind of argument at +8 and +0x10, is `void sub_3420(long a0, unsigned int a1)`. When on, `kuna_ptrfromuse::pointer_from_use` walks each function input's transitive descendants through COPY/MULTIEQUAL/INDIRECT identity, the base slot of PTRADD/PTRSUB and constant-offset INT_ADD (breadth-first bounded worklist, visited set, ten hops, so the cap is a property of the graph rather than of the pop order) and offers a pointer candidate when at least one terminal use is the address operand of a LOAD or STORE. The candidate is FOLDED into the same `getLocalType` fold by `Datatype::type_order`, not installed as a replacement seed, so a more specific vote still wins: a `FILE *` arriving from a callee's locked prototype is `SUB_PTR_STRUCT` and outranks this rule's `SUB_PTR`. The walk refuses on any use no pointer survives -- INT_MULT, INT_DIV/SDIV/REM/SREM, INT_2COMP/NEGATE, a shift, a PIECE that assembles the value from halves, any float op, a comparison against a non-zero literal, and a CALL whose callee prototype has already committed that argument to a non-pointer -- and a variable-offset addition is neutral, carrying neither acceptance nor refusal, because either operand of `x + y` could be the base. A *literal* addend is the one ambiguous shape: `p->field` and `table[i]` lower to the same INT_ADD of a value and a constant, and only the constant says which operand is the base, so the walk asks `ActionConstantPtr::isPointer`'s own question of it -- the default data space's pointer bounds, `resolveConstant` into that space, then the global scope -- and grades the answer. A constant that resolves to a global object kuna knows about IS the base, so the walked value is a subscript and the candidate is refused. A constant that is address-like but names nothing settles nothing and is neutral, exactly like a variable addend: that is what a stripped image's .bss table looks like, and also what a genuinely large struct looks like (bzip2's 0x13f0-byte bzFile is read at +0x1394). Anything below the bound is an ordinary field offset and the walk carries on. Only inputs whose width is the default data space's address size are considered (eight bytes on the 64-bit images the option is named for, four on a 32-bit image), and only storage the prototype model says could carry a parameter, which keeps a segment-base register such as x86-64's FS_OFFSET out of it. `byte` points at one unknown byte, which `realtypes` renders `char *`; `void` points at nothing and renders `void *`. Only function inputs are considered: a parameter is one declaration per function rather than one per local, and it is the argument-position match that a metric or a reader sees first.
- **When to flip:** On by default (`void`): a pointer-width parameter whose every memory use is `*(T *)(a0 + k)` -- a struct or buffer pointer once the compiler has folded the field offsets in -- is declared `void *a0`, and its field accesses keep their byte arithmetic with a cast on the base (`*(long *)((long)a0 + 0x28)`). With `protoorder` at its default the callee's `void *` also types the matching argument at each call site, which is how a wrapper that only forwards its arguments (the `qsort` comparators and hash-table callbacks whose declared parameters are `void const *`) is declared with `void *` parameters: over the 444-slice decbench sweep the default moves 204 functions onto a perfect type_match and 85 more up, none down. `byte` declares `char *a0` instead and rewrites the arithmetic into indexing (`*(long *)&a0[0x28]`, `RulePtrArith`); it moves 7 functions onto perfect. Turn it off to get upstream's integer declaration and uncast arithmetic back, when a script matches body text an older run printed (the `(long)a0 + k` casts, and the local renumbering where a retyped value merges differently), or when a parameter really is an integer the function also uses as an address -- committing it to a pointer is a claim the width-only integer spelling did not make. Prefer `libctypes` where the argument reaches a libc call: a named `FILE *` outranks this rule's candidate and is kept. KNOWN AMBIGUITY: an index into a global array is the same shape as a base at a constant offset -- both are `INT_ADD(value, constant)` -- so the rule grades the constant. A named global object refuses the candidate (`char table[256]; int lookup(long i){return table[i];}` keeps `long a0` and its named global; typing it would also replace `table` in the body with its raw address). An address-like constant that names nothing is neutral, so a parameter used ONLY that way is still declined, but one that is also dereferenced at an ordinary field offset is typed on the strength of that other use -- which is right for a large struct and wrong for a subscript into an unnamed table that the function also uses as a base. A constant below the space's pointer lower bound is always read as a field offset.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · angr · opt-in-tool · kuna-ptrfromuse
- **Example:** `option ptrfromuse off`

### `charptr` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a string parameter is declared unsigned long and every call site passes it to strlen or printf; a buffer indexed one byte at a time is declared void *; two functions take the same string and one says char * and the other unsigned long; a -O0 parameter is an integer although the callee's prototype declares char *; void * sub_e680(uint1 *a0) for a function that passes its argument to strlen.
- **What it does:** Commit a pointer-width parameter or stack local the program only ever uses on characters to `char *`. `ptrfromuse` decides that a value IS a pointer; nothing says what is on the other end, and its shipped `void` says so honestly. The element type is often already on the table -- `strlen`'s declared `char *`, a `%s` conversion `formatstring` resolved, a walk that indexes the object one byte at a time -- and it is lost for the same structural reason the pointer was: `TypeOpCall::getInputLocal` (typeop.cc:689) states the callee's declared parameter type about the Varnode that IS the call's operand, and `propagateTypeEdge` will not carry a pointer back over an INT_ADD, a MULTIEQUAL, or the store/load pair an -O0 spill puts in between. GNU tar -O0 shows it: `void * sub_e680(uint1 *a0)` for `drop_volume_label_suffix(char const *label)`, which passes `label` to `strlen`. When on, `kuna_charptr::char_pointer_from_evidence` collects that evidence with the bounded breadth-first walk `ptrfromuse` uses -- COPY/MULTIEQUAL/INDIRECT/CAST identity, the base slot of PTRADD/PTRSUB, a literal-addend INT_ADD graded by `ActionConstantPtr::isPointer`'s own three-way question, ten hops, visited set -- and asks of every use whether it is about CHARACTERS rather than whether it is a dereference at all. Three uses say yes: the value reaches argument i of a call whose callee DECLARES `char *` there AT THE BASE (declared meaning stated from outside the decompile -- a `libproto`/`libcsigs` signature, a `libctypes` shell, DWARF, a demangled name, `--assert prototype`, or the per-call-site override `formatstring` installs for a resolved `%s` -- read through `declared_input_type_local`, so `protoorder`'s recovered callee vote is deliberately NOT evidence: counting it was measured on the 444-slice sweep and scored lower); every dereference AT THE BASE is one byte wide, or the value is indexed one byte at a time by an index the program COMPUTES (a PTRADD of element size one whose index is not a constant); and the value is defined by or compared against a constant that resolves to a character array in the image. Nothing at a FIXED non-zero offset is evidence, in any of the three -- that is a field, not the object. The walk marks a value offset when it passes a non-zero literal INT_ADD, a non-zero PTRSUB, or a PTRADD whose index is a non-zero constant, and a byte access, a declared parameter and a further one-byte step there are all neutral. A byte read there is a one-byte struct field (coreutils `ginstall`'s `announce_mkdir(char *dir, void *options)` reads the `bool` at `options + 0x3c`); a declared `char *` there is a string FIELD (cronie `crond` -O0 `sub_6715` calls `strcmp(base + 0x13, ".cron.hostname")` on a `struct dirent *`); and the PTRADD spelling matters because the same displacement is an INT_ADD while the base is an integer and `PTRADD(d, 0x13, 1)` once an earlier fold typed it `void *`, which is how dpkg's `dpkg-trigger` -O2 `sub_58d0` and `dpkg-statoverride` -O0 `sub_9aaf`, walking `d_name` to its NUL, became `char *`. The price is two correct idioms with the shape of a field: skipping a string's first character (`p + 1`), so coreutils `realpath`'s `path_prefix`, `env`'s `scan_varname` and `printf`'s `print_esc` stay `void *`, and writing a number backwards from `buf + 20` (gnulib `umaxtostr`), whose `buf` stays `void *` too. A VARIABLE index is not an offset: `strlen(p + i)` and `p[i]` still count. The candidate is one more vote in the same `getLocalType` fold, folded by `Datatype::type_order`, and it may additionally REFINE a pointer VOTE that points at nothing (`void *`, `undefined1 *`) while a pointer vote at a NAMED, aggregate or WIDER pointee -- `FILE *`, `stat *`, `long *`, a synthesized `struct_3 *` -- is left as it was. The guard reads the vote IN FLIGHT, not the type the function will finally print, so a pointee that would only have arrived by LATER propagation is not there to protect. `unsigned char *` is the common case and is deliberately accepted -- the element width agrees and only its signedness moves, the same call `charbyte` makes one level down (`protoorder_x86_64`: `int callee(unsigned char *a0,int a1)` -> `char *`). It is not only signedness: measured over 8 whole binaries, 3 declarations move from a WIDER pointee, all of them e2fsprogs e2fsck's `ext2fs_bitcount(unsigned int *a0,uint4 a1)` and its two stack copies (upstream declares it `int ext2fs_bitcount(const void *addr, int nbytes)`). No synthesized `struct_N *` declaration moves at all in that run (1,286 in both arms), and wide field reads rendered through an indexed character pointer go 1,202 -> 1,204 -- see `docs/features/charptr/analysis.md`. The refusals are a dereference or element step wider than a byte, a call argument the callee declared as some other pointer or as a scalar, integer multiplication/division/shift/PIECE, a float op, a comparison against a non-zero literal that is not a string, and an INT_ADD whose constant addend resolves to a global object. A refusal withdraws the VARNODE it was collected for and nothing else: the walk runs once per Varnode, the vote is folded per Varnode, and the type a reader sees belongs to the MERGED VARIABLE, so a slot walked with byte evidence in one flow and refused in another prints the commitment (grep -O0 `sub_6fdd`'s stack slot at -0x20: eight `byte` walks, four refusals, visible under `KUNA_CHARPTR_CENSUS=1`). They are about element WIDTH and contradicting declarations, not about arithmetic shape -- a constant-stride walk is never refused, because a literal displacement only marks the value as offset from its base. Only storage a reader sees declared is considered: a function input the prototype model could place a parameter in, or a Varnode in the stack space; a type-locked Varnode and one seeded from a type-locked symbol are never touched.
- **When to flip:** Off by default, and the measurement says to keep it off. Turn it on when a string parameter or stack local reads as `void *` or `unsigned char *` and a callee's declared `char *` or a computed byte index says what it is -- most visibly at -O0, where every value is spilled to the frame and reloaded, which is exactly the hop the ordinary propagation cannot cross. Measured on the 444-slice decbench type sweep (10,748 functions): no function moves onto or off a perfect `type_match`, 2 move up and 4 down, aggregate -0.57. Before the offset rule covered a constant PTRADD index the same sweep read +4 onto perfect, 14 up, 6 down, aggregate +4.93, and nearly all of that gain was the skip-the-first-character idiom that is now declined because it is indistinguishable from a struct field. The reason the ceiling is small is measured and published in `docs/features/charptr/analysis.md`: ground-truth `char *` is the largest class in the corpus (14,645 of 65,715 scored variables) but half of it lives in registers, which kuna does not export at all, kuna's ARGUMENT recovery is already within 6.6 points of Binary Ninja's, and 932 of the 1,648 stack misses are frame slots reported as `undefined8` because the value that lived there was copy-propagated into a register -- a chapter-06 gap, not a chapter-05 one. KNOWN COST: committing a pointer forfeits the width-only free pass an 8-byte scalar gets, and `char *` changes how the body reads -- `*(long *)((long)a0 + 8)` becomes `*(long *)&a0[8]` (`RulePtrArith`), and a byte compared through it prints as a character constant. The four measured regressions are two functions: an `__off_t` the body also uses as an address (coreutils `head::elide_tail_bytes_pipe`), and a GT `_Bool` byte kuna reported as `undefined1` -- credited on width alone -- knocked on to `char` by the pointer it is read through (`tar::check_compressed_archive`, three builds). A byte-sized STORE is evidence too, so a `bool *` out-parameter that is only ever written (tar -O0 `mode_from_header`'s `hbits`) becomes `char *`. The signedness can also move the OTHER way as a knock-on, and a correct `char *` becomes `unsigned char *`. Measured on dash -O0 (not a sweep project): 13 lines in 7 functions, 4 of them signatures (`sub_68c3`, `sub_128e1`, `sub_1295d`, `sub_155e7`), and two of those bodies lose a character literal (`*a0 != '_'` becomes `*a0 != 0x5f`). Against it, 23 lines move forward to `char *` in the same binary and four `strcmp` casts disappear.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · binja · type-inference · kuna-charptr
- **Example:** `option charptr on`

### `elemptr` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a buffer indexed one byte at a time prints as *(char *)((long)v6 + (long)v8); a parameter only ever indexed is declared long; malloc's result is declared void * and every store through it casts; a table in .data read with a computed index prints as *(unsigned char *)((long)v1 + 0x4020); argv-like parameters are declared long and each element is cast to char *.
- **What it does:** Declare a pointer-width value the program uses only as an array of one element type as a pointer to that element. `TypeOpIntAdd` votes an integer for both operands of `p + i`, and nothing carries the element type a load through the sum implies back over the add (`typeop.cc:1217`, the refusal `ptrfromuse` documents), so a byte buffer indexed by a computed value reaches the reader as `long` (a parameter, a global read before it is written) or `void *` (what `malloc` returns), and every access prints as `*(char *)((long)v6 + (long)v8)`. When on, `kuna_elemptr::element_pointer` supplies a `T *` vote in the `getLocalType` fold for four kinds of value: a function input the prototype model could place a parameter in; the value a call returns when its callee left the pointee open (`void *`, an allocator), when no phi joins it with anything but a copy of itself or a null; a global the image names nothing at (`dat_<addr>`), decided from every Varnode of the function that holds it; and a constant address inside a section of program data that is the base of an indexed access, which `globalref` then prints as the array it names (`dat_4020[v1]`) and the `decompile-project` header declares `T dat_4020[]`. A bounded breadth-first walk follows the value through COPY/CAST/MULTIEQUAL/INDIRECT and literal offsets and accepts only when every access through it, at any literal offset, is one width W (1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes) landing on a whole element, and at least one index is a value the program computes: scaled by W (`x * W`, `x << log2 W`), or, for W = 1, an unscaled integer. An index is recognised by how it was made -- a scaling, an extension from a narrower integer, a small mask, a shift, a division, a loop counter that starts at a literal and steps by one, a value the program also multiplies, divides, shifts or orders against a literal (not one it masks: `p & 7` tests a pointer's alignment) -- or because the other operand is already a pointer (C adds no two); an operand already typed as a pointer is the base, and an add whose operands could each be the base says nothing. Constant offsets alone never commit: a record's fields stay with `ptrfromuse` and `structsynth`. The element's sign comes only from evidence, since a function that returns the element returns it at that type: the recovered return type, then the extensions, orderings, shifts and divisions of a loaded element when they agree, then (a byte compared against a character literal is plain `char`) the type the load has without the rule; a wider element nothing votes for is unsigned, as an undefined word prints, and a byte plain `char`. An element as wide as a pointer commits only to a pointer type something else names (a loaded value already typed `char *`, a stored `FILE *`, a callee's declared pointee), or to an integer when its uses are only arithmetic: an unnamed `void **` would pre-empt the `char **` argv `calleevote` states on a later decompile. The walk refuses a second width (a record, not an array), an index scaled by something other than the element or itself a multiple of elements (`p[2 * i]`, `p[2 * i + 1]` walk 16-byte records), a non-zero field (`PTRSUB`), integer arithmetic on the pointer, a float, a comparison against a non-zero literal, a call argument declared as a scalar or as a pointer to something of another width, a comparison or difference with a pointer to something of another width, a use as the index of another base (a `PTRADD` index, an add to a constant already typed a pointer; an add that subtracts one more pointer than it adds is a difference, not an element), and a global copied into a register the function returns another value in; it never replaces a type-locked, symbol-seeded or already-named pointer vote. A global, and a constant table, is typed only where every function of a batch agrees on the element, sign included: `decompile-all` and `decompile-project` record what each function said about each (an array of which element, whether evidence or the default chose its sign, or for a global a refusal), block an object two functions' evidence types differently for every function that typed it, and decide again at the evidenced sign a function whose sign was only the default (a function that returns the element keeps its own); the header declares no array two functions index at different elements. A function that holds a global and leaves it untyped refuses it unless nothing it prints depends on the pointee (copied, dereferenced at its own address, stored, passed, returned, compared): `gp++` prints `dat_4018 += 4`, which one `int *dat_4018` declaration would make four elements. A global whose vote already names a pointee (a callee's `char *`) files that pointee as evidence, never as a function to decide again. A function that reads or writes a table's first element by name (`dat_4040 + 1`) blocks every function that named the table an array; one that names it and indexes the table too prints `(&dat_4040)[i]` and keeps its type. A narrow load through a pointee this option supplies keeps its own width in both arms (`*(unsigned short *)&a0[1]`, never the 4-byte `(unsigned short)a0[1]`; chapter 03's `RuleExpandLoad`). Only such a batch -- the callee-first driver, or a single function -- types a global or a table: a `--jobs` worker, the streamed export and a serial run of several functions that is not callee-first type neither, and leave untyped a parameter or call return they store into a global, so a pool prints what `--jobs 1 --option protoorder off` prints. The printer declines a string literal for a table indexed by a computed value unless the index provably stays inside the literal (a zero-extended byte, a mask, an unsigned remainder), because `""[x]` reads bytes the literal does not have; and a character-pointer constant whose type comes from the rule alone -- it reaches a pointer the rule typed, or a callee's parameter the rule typed and stated for its callers, and nothing reads it as a C string, through it a byte at a time directly, or as a declared `char *` argument -- prints as its address, since an index says nothing about where the bytes end (a 15-byte DigestInfo prefix compared by `timingsafe_bcmp` printed as a literal that stopped at its zero byte).
- **When to flip:** On by default. Turn it off to see the integer spelling upstream prints -- `*(char *)((long)v6 + (long)v8)`, `*(unsigned char *)((long)v1 + 0x4020)` -- or when a consumer matches the older declarations (`long a0` for a byte buffer, `void *` for an allocator's result). Measured with the default on against `--option elemptr off` on one build: 0 of 675 datatest assertions move; 8 stage assertions of other options and 2 `tests/cli` probes pinned the integer spelling and now read the subscript, each the same access, and 3 stage assertions pinned upstream's widened read of a 4-byte field and now read it 4 bytes wide; the 444-slice decbench type sweep goes 1,631 -> 1,674 perfect functions (15.17% -> 15.57%), mean .3717 -> .3752, 189 functions better and none worse, 243 scored variables gained and none lost, no function's variable or argument count moved; over the 45-binary castbench corpus casts fall 33,289 -> 32,073 on the 4,815 functions kuna and IDA both emit, measured on a main that already has `castindex`, `castternary`, `callrettype`, `castobject` and `castwiden` (0.880x -> 0.848x IDA, 176.0 -> 169.6 per 1,000 lines), 301 functions with fewer and 18 with more (+26, a callee now declaring `char *` making a caller's integer argument print its conversion, a constant used at two pointee types, or a narrow read respelled); the `off` arm is byte-identical to main. Speed, interleaved min-of-15 whole-binary on main `f96e80805`: fmt +0.03%, ls +0.25%, sort +0.36%, bash +1.81%. A global or a table is typed only by a batch that agrees on it (a callee-first `decompile-all` or `decompile-project`, or one function); `--jobs N`, `--stream` and a serial run of several functions without the callee-first order type neither, which keeps `--jobs N` byte-identical to `--jobs 1` under `--option protoorder off`.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · ida · type-inference · castcampaign-elemptr
- **Example:** `option elemptr on`

### `pebnames` -- off | auto | on, default `auto`

- **Symptoms:** a local commented // gs_offset or // fs_offset is read through constant offsets; an anti-debug check reads *(char *)(*(long long *)(v1 + 0x60) + 2); PEB fields such as BeingDebugged or NtGlobalFlag render as magic offsets; a thread-local or stack-limit read renders as *(long long *)(v1 + 0x58) or (v1 + 0x10).
- **What it does:** Type the Windows thread-environment segment base as `TEB *teb`, so reads through it render as the TEB and PEB fields a reverser recognises. A Windows user-mode thread keeps its Thread Environment Block at the base of `GS` (x86-64) or `FS` (x86), and x86 SLEIGH lowers a segment-prefixed operand to `GS_OFFSET + disp` / `FS_OFFSET + disp` over a register input nothing in the function writes. With no type on that register the anti-debug probe `MOV RAX,GS:[0x60]; MOVZX ECX,byte [RAX+2]; MOV EAX,[RAX+0xBC]` renders as `long long v1; // gs_offset` and `*(char *)(*(long long *)(v1 + 0x60) + 2)`: magic offsets into nothing, with `gs_offset` being only the lowercased register name. Before heritage, when the raw p-code reads the segment-base register and never stores through it, a type-locked and name-locked local Symbol `TEB *teb` is mapped over its input storage, and ordinary pointer-arithmetic and field rendering does the rest: `teb->ProcessEnvironmentBlock->BeingDebugged`, `teb->ProcessEnvironmentBlock->NtGlobalFlag`, `teb->Self->ProcessEnvironmentBlock`, `teb->ThreadLocalStoragePointer`, `teb->StackLimit`. A field is named only when its offset, name and size agree in every PDB-derived layout the Vergilius Project publishes (x64 XP SP2 to Windows 11 25H2; x86 XP SP3 to Windows 10 22H2 plus every WOW64 TEB32/PEB32), so a release-dependent name such as `ApiSetMap` or `CrossProcessFlags` stays `field_0x<off>`. Both structures are variable-length at the largest published size, so an offset past the end stays an integer addition instead of naming a field of a phantom neighbouring TEB. A function that writes through the base (on x86, every function linking an SEH registration record through `fs:[0]`) is left untyped, because that record's stack layout is inferred from how the untyped base is used. The base is only a TEB in user mode -- kernel code keeps its KPCR there and firmware nothing -- so `auto` acts only on an image the loader proved is a Windows GUI or console PE (optional-header subsystem 2 or 3); `on` trusts a Windows compiler spec alone. The register is GS on x86-64 and FS on x86, so the x86-64 ELF canary at `fs:0x28` and the x86 one at `gs:0x14` never reach the pass; both modes also require a Windows compiler spec, which keeps a non-Windows image that does read that register untyped.
- **When to flip:** On (`auto`) by default: a Windows PE whose C reads a `// gs_offset` or `// fs_offset` local through constant offsets -- anti-debug `BeingDebugged`/`NtGlobalFlag` probes, MSVC `thread_local` access through `gs:[0x58]`, `__chkstk` stack-limit checks -- gets the field names. Besides the names, a reader's types can move: a stub that returns the TEB or PEB pointer is declared `_TEB *` or `PEB *`, a `BeingDebugged` read is `uint1` rather than `char`, a local that keeps the PEB pointer is declared `PEB *`, and an opaque field compared with a pointer gains a cast. A variable that holds `teb->Self` or `teb->ProcessEnvironmentBlock` on one path and an unrelated value on another takes the pointer type, so the unrelated value gains a cast (seen once, in an obfuscated binary); a parameter merged with such a value can take it too. Set `on` for code with no PE container that still runs as a Windows user-mode thread: shellcode or a raw `.text` blob loaded under a `windows` compiler spec, a stage bytechunk, or the Ghidra front-end, which never supplies the loader fact `auto` needs. Set `off` to restore the untyped register. It never fires on a kernel driver, an EFI image, a COFF object or anything loaded under a non-Windows compiler spec; a Symbol the user already mapped over the register, a program type already named `TEB`/`PEB` with a different layout, or a function whose segment-override instructions store through the base (an x86 SEH frame) makes it decline. A store through a pointer loaded from the TEB (`mov eax,fs:[0x18]; mov [eax],esp`) is not seen by that check and is typed. Measured in DIV-175: every function that changes is a segment-base reader, no call is added or removed, and 0/675 datatests move even with `on` forced as the default.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · kuna · type-inference · GH-468
- **Example:** `option pebnames on`

### `structsynth` -- off | param | locals | nest | all, default `locals`

- **Symptoms:** a parameter is declared `unsigned long *` or `void *` and read at two or more fixed offsets; a local assigned from `xmalloc` or another call is written as `*(char *)((long)v1 + 0x14) = 0x6e`; the body is a wall of `*(int *)(p + 0x18)` casts over one pointer; `*(unsigned int *)&a0[1]` appears where a record field is meant; two functions read the same object and neither names its fields; a local loaded from a `struct_N` field is read as `*(int *)((long)v1 + 0xc)`; a synthesized struct's link fields are `long *` or `unsigned long` where the nodes they point at are the same record.
- **What it does:** Synthesize a structure type from the constant-offset dereferences of a pointer parameter, or of a pointer a call returned, so the reads render as named fields instead of raw offset arithmetic. A stripped binary keeps no record of the aggregate a pointer points at, so `put_word` in a `-O2` coreutils `fmt` renders as `void sub_3000(unsigned long *a0)` with `v2 = *(unsigned int *)&a0[1]` and `v3 = (unsigned char *)*a0` -- the reader carries `offset 0 is a character pointer, offset 8 is a 4-byte count` in their head across every function that touches the same object. With `param`, once type propagation has reached its fixpoint, every live LOAD/STORE whose address peels to `(parameter, constant)` is bucketed by offset, a `struct_N` is completed with one field per observed offset, and the parameter varnode is type-locked to `struct_N *`; the existing pointer-arithmetic and field rendering does the rest, giving `void sub_3000(struct_0 *a0)` with `v2 = a0->field_0x8` and `v3 = a0->field_0x0` over `struct struct_0 { unsigned char *field_0x0; int field_0x8; }` -- offsets 0 and 8 of the real `WORD { char const *text; int length; ... }`. The pass invents a layout, never pointer-ness: the base must ALREADY carry a pointer type, so `fmt`'s `get_line`, whose first parameter is the real `FILE *` but is still typed `long`, is left alone, and a pointee that is a named composite (DWARF, a parsed declaration, a libc shell, an earlier synthesized structure) always wins. The evidence is deliberately narrow. Only `COPY`/`CAST` and constant pointer arithmetic are peeled, never a phi, because chasing a loop-carried MULTIEQUAL to its root turns `while (*p) p = &p[1]` into offsets `{0,1}` and would synthesize a two-field structure over a string; a base that reaches a phi at all declines, as does one used as an integer, one with a non-constant offset term (that is an array, not a structure) whether or not this function dereferences the result, one with fewer than two distinct offsets or no access at offset 0, a negative or >= 0x8000 offset, a run of equal-width offsets on a regular grid, which reads as an array rather than a layout (Howard NDSS 2011 section 4.5: three or more outright, two when the element is narrower than a pointer, so `int pipefds[2]` and `arg[0]`/`arg[1]` over a `char *` decline while a pair of pointer-sized fields does not; a gap does not break the run below pointer width, because a function that writes ten of a buffer's twelve bytes is ordinary, but it does break it at pointer width, where a record with an untouched member between two observed ones is the common case; an optimized `int fd[2]` that is also saved and restored as one 8-byte word has mixed widths and reaches the same decline through the layout rule instead, because both elements sit inside the wide access and nothing but a single field is left), a stack- or spacebase-rooted base, a type-locked base, and a function whose lattice never settled. At a conflicting offset the WIDEST access wins: a field wider than an access renders as a cast of the field, while a narrower one loses the field name entirely. A field commits to a signedness only when every access of its width does; a signed read and an unsigned or undefined one leave it `undefined<N>`, because a signed field makes C sign-extend a read the binary zero-extends into a call argument. The layout is then pruned so that a C compiler reading the exported header back puts `field_0xK` at offset K: an access whose width the header cannot spell at that width (`undefined3` is a 4-byte `unsigned int` there), one at an offset its own alignment does not divide, and one inside the bytes a wider access already claimed each become a hole instead of a field. What survives is naturally aligned and 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes wide, and two such ranges either nest or are disjoint, so the declaration cannot overlap at all. The layout is then made dense and C-sized, which is about the body rather than the declaration: every byte from 0 to the end belongs to a member, a gap becoming an `undefined1 field_0x<hex>[N]` of alignment 1 at its own offset, because the printer names an in-range offset no field covers `field_0x<hex>` anyway while the exported header would render that gap as `undefined1 _pad<hex>[N]`, and address arithmetic reaches those offsets without a dereference; and the size is the end of the last surviving field rounded up to the widest surviving field's width, with that rounding covered by `undefined1` filler like any other gap, because a structure the decompiler sizes 0x15 and a compiler sizes 0x18 puts `a0[1]` at two different addresses. Past that end there is no member and no invented name: the printer spells the address as an element of the structure array plus a byte offset, which is still the address the access meant. Names are program-wide `struct_N`, handed out by a layout ledger that reads back every `struct_N` the program's type factory already holds. A measured layout is answered with a minted structure that CONTAINS it -- every claimed field at the same offset, the same width and the same type, and the structure at least as large -- and not only with one whose signature matches exactly, so two functions that read overlapping but unequal subsets of one record share a definition instead of getting a name each (`ls`'s two `fileinfo` comparators, and a stage test's `{0, 8}` and `{0, 8, 0xc}` readers; over twelve binaries it is 471 names where exact-signature dedup minted 515). Agreement on a shared field is exact: two types at one offset are a conflict rather than a refinement, and a field a reader could not type is its own answer, not a wildcard the other may fill in -- a wildcard rule was measured and it unifies records that merely share a shape. Containment stops being evidence once the container dwarfs the measurement or the measurement is too generic to name a record, so a structure that says strictly MORE than the reader measured must also claim at most twice as many fields and be at most four times its size, and the reader must claim two fields of which one is a typed pointer, or three without one: unbounded, an `ls` reader that measured the two words of a `hash_entry` is declared to hold a 200-byte record, and two integer words are how `struct stat`, gnulib's `cycle_check_state` and a list node all begin, so without the pointer rule `cycle_check`'s `struct stat *` is declared as its `cycle_check_state`. A pointer to code, `void` or an undefined type is not a typed pointer. A reader whose every claim past offset 0 is such a pointer is a table (an interface, an ops vector, a vtable) and is answered only by its own shape, since distinct tables differ only in how many slots they have: without that, `rsyslogd`'s seven `*_if_s` interface records all took one 144-byte layout. A reader with no typed pointer is answered only by a structure of its own size that claims nothing past the reader's last field, which may fill in the holes between its fields but not the bytes after them, because records that begin alike part ways after the last field a reader touched (every `ip` netlink reader measures the same `nlmsghdr` words ahead of a payload of its own, and dpkg's `pkg_queue` ends in the padding where `pkg_spec` keeps two flag bytes). No structure answers with a member inside the alignment padding a reader's claims leave between two of them, because records part ways in their first words too: every `bash` command record begins with an `int flags`, and `for_com` puts an `int line` at 4 where `if_com` pads before its first pointer. And a structure answers for a reader only if it lays exactly the reader's own members over every byte range the reader accessed without claiming a field (an unaligned word, a 16-byte copy): the engine's load/store ordering test compares two addresses without their widths, so a container that started a member inside such an access printed a four-byte load at offset 7 after the byte store at 8 that overwrites part of it. When containment runs the other way the minted structure cannot be widened -- `find_add` refuses a second definition of a held name and the completed structure is already shared by every function that took a pointer to it -- so the larger layout mints beside it and the smaller is SUPERSEDED: still defined, and handed out again only to a layout no live structure answers for. Because `decompile-all` decompiles in address order, the function that minted the smaller layout still names it, so after the batch exactly the results that spell a superseded name are decompiled again and each moves to the survivor where the survivor is in its reach; a redo that fails where the first pass succeeded keeps the first body. The bounds are not transitive, so a record can keep two names, but the sweep never mints a third, and the exported header declares one definition per name still in use. None of that happens under `kuna decompile`, which spawns one engine per function, and the streaming project export (`--stream`) has written a body before a name can be superseded, so it converges only as far as its write order allows. With `nest` the values loaded from one pointer-sized field of an accepted record are measured as one base under the same conditions -- already pointers, not type-locked, no phi, index or integer use, two offsets including 0, not an array run -- and the field becomes a pointer to the completed record the ledger answers for them; at most two records below the parameter. When a loaded record claims nothing the enclosing record does not hold at the same offset, width and type, the field points at the enclosing record itself: the structure is minted around its incomplete shell, its self pointer is keyed `SELF` in the ledger, and a LOAD or STORE value typed as a pointer to that shell takes the pointer to the completed structure, so `v3->field_0x18` prints three links down. Under `nest` the convergence sweep can mint (a redone reader's outer layout names the surviving inner record), and a `--jobs` run names a structure with a nested or self field in its one ordered worker. With `locals` the value a CALL or CALLIND returns is a base too: single assignment makes it the local's only definition, so an allocation a function fills in (`v1 = (unsigned long *)xmalloc(0x18); *(char *)((long)v1 + 0x14) = 0x6e`) or a pointer a lookup returns is measured under every condition a parameter is, and five more about the value. A callee declared to return a pointer to something (`char *`, `struct stat *`) has said what it is, so only a `void *` or unlocked return is measured. The value must not share a variable with anything else: a copy is merged with what it copies, a phi input with the other inputs and a value in address-tied storage with everything stored there, so it declines when it or a COPY/CAST of it reaches a MULTIEQUAL or INDIRECT, lands in tied storage, or overlaps the storage any RETURN reads where a phi writes that return register (tied as a whole-function local once merging starts; `kmod` kept a name, its length and a `calloc` record in the one `rax` its `int` function returns through `eax`) -- a locked member decides the merged variable's type. A function has one return type, so a record returned on one path while another RETURN returns a different value (a name, a count, an error code) declines; a constant zero may be returned beside it. A base whose every access stores text is a string buffer: a constant whose bytes are characters (`tar` builds `SCHILY.xattr.` in a fresh allocation as an 8-, a 4- and a 1-byte store) or bytes loaded from a read-only string literal (`cp` fills a `mempcpy` tail from `CuXXXXXX`). And a base declines when a copy of it forms an address at or past the end of every access, because the record is wider than this function shows (`sortlines` passes `&node->lock` just past the fields it reads, and typed on those fields the mutex would print as `&v1[1]` and take the record's type). `all` is `locals` and `nest` together. Globals are not bases: over eight builds each of the thirteen global pointers dereferenced at two or more offsets reaches a phi or an INDIRECT, and a global record is not one base in the IR at all.
- **When to flip:** On (`locals`) by default: any stripped function that reads the same object at fixed offsets -- a linked-list or record walker, a parser state block, a callback context, a record it has just allocated and fills in, anything whose listing would be a wall of `*(int *)(p + 0x18)` -- gets a `struct_N *` parameter or local whose accesses render as `p->field_0x18`. It acts only on a parameter or a call's returned value the engine already believes is a pointer, never on a stack slot, a global, or anything a declared, DWARF or libc type already names. `locals` was made the default on measured evidence against `param` on the same build: 0 of 675 datatest assertions and no stage assertion of another feature move, `make test-cli` is unchanged, the 444-slice typesweep is 1,472 perfect in both arms with every function's scored variable count unchanged, and of its 65,377 scored decisions 95 change type, each a -O0 stack slot a returned record is stored to (`slotptr` types it from the stored value) going from `undefined8`, `long *` or `int8 *` to `struct_N *` where DWARF names a struct pointer (`hash_entry *`, `predicate *`, `group *`, `passwd *`, ...), none replacing a correct pointer, and the rest the same type up to `struct_N` numbering (at -O2 a returned pointer lives in a register, which `variables[]` never exports); over 29 binaries and 12,939 functions 872 change, 769 only in `struct_N` numbering, 83 the same statements respelled through the returned record with clean declarations and casts (checked by a declaration- and cast-aware classifier), and 20 read by hand (15 where the record gets a register variable of its own instead of sharing one with an unrelated value of the same primitive type, 4 `find` predicate records whose name field holds a string literal, 1 local typed `void *` from the record's field), with no control-flow, call or arity change, and 24 of the 27 return types that move are struct pointers in DWARF (the other three return a record behind a `void *` handle or through an inlined constructor); over 14 builds the call-defined locals declared a record pointer go from 40 to 116, 103 of them struct pointers in DWARF and none anything else, with the new records' claimed fields 0.852 exact and parameter layouts unchanged; serial whole-binary `decompile-all` time on fmt/ls/sort/bash O2 stays inside the +5% budget (interleaved min-of-15, `docs/features/structlocals/record.json`), and a `--jobs` run renames the returned records in place with output identical to the serial `protoorder off` run. Set `param` to measure parameters only, the first default: 0 of 675 datatest assertions move; over a 14-binary, 5,610-function `decompile-all` sweep (x86-64 coreutils/findutils/grep/gzip/bzip2/diffutils/tar at O0/O2 plus two ARM32 firmwares) 483 functions change: 350 are verified mechanically as the same statements with each parameter access respelled from its byte offset to a field, and the other 133 were read by hand as the same memory accesses spelled through the new pointee (an index rescaled to the structure's size, a filler array decaying to its address, constant byte stores merged into one store of the field, a load folded into its use, one more duplicated return block); no function in either arm has a `goto` whose label is missing, and every exported `offsetof(struct_N, field_0xK)` equals K. The known cost is decbench `type_match`, which compares pointee spellings by name and so cannot credit an anonymous `struct_0 *` against a ground-truth `WORD *`: over 444 slices the flip is worth -1 perfect function (959 -> 958, aggregate -0.05%). Its measured false positives are buffers of primitive elements that the array rule does not recognise -- a GMP limb array read at offsets 0 and 8 (coreutils `factor` `powm2`/`millerrabin2`), and character buffers whose writes are not all one width (`ls` `strmode`, `shred` `passname`). Functions that read overlapping parts of one record share one `struct_N`: the smallest minted structure that contains every field a function measured, under growth bounds and evidence rules. Against DWARF that is a trade rather than a free win: pooled claimed-field precision over 169 held-out builds is 0.8908 against 0.8902 for naming every reader's subset separately (0.8852 against 0.8855 on the last 34, chosen before any result under the padding rule was seen), recall is higher on every set, 6 of 177 builds lose precision (`kmod` and `grep` O2 under a point each), and 4 of the 258 parameters answered by a larger structure are given one measured from a different record (all `e2fsck` readers without a typed pointer, filled in between their own fields; two take `ext2_inode_large` for `ext2_inode`, the same record for its first 128 bytes). Set `off` for anything that depends on the exact spelling of a parameter type (a type-name matcher, a diff against another decompiler) or to restore the raw offset arithmetic. `struct_N` names are program-wide only where one process decompiles the whole program (`decompile-all`, a serial `decompile-project`); a sharded `decompile-project --jobs N` runs its workers with `structsynth off` because per-process numbering cannot give one header one layout per name. The layouts themselves are printed above each function by `structdefs` and live in the `decompile-project` header. Set `nest` to go one step further: a pointer field whose loaded values are already pointers and are themselves read at two or more constant offsets including 0 is declared `struct_M *`, so `v1 = a0->field_0x0; ... *(int *)((long)v1 + 0xc)` reads `v1->field_0xc`, and a tree or list node whose link reads the same fields as the node itself points at its own `struct_N`. Measured against `param` on the same build: no datatest assertion (675/675) and no stage assertion of another feature moves; over 15 binaries and 7,819 functions (x86-64 coreutils/findutils/grep/gzip/bzip2/diffutils/tar and three ARM32 firmwares) 93 functions change, 86 of them only in `struct_N` numbering and 7 in reads respelled through the nested record, with no control flow moved; the 444-slice typesweep is 1,349 perfect in both arms with no function better or worse; against DWARF it adds 2 nested fields on 10 builds, both real struct pointers, and every exported `offsetof` stays exact. `nest` is not the default because a sharded run pays for it: a structure with a nested or self field has no portable recipe, so `--jobs` decompiles every function with a synthesized structure in its one ordered worker, and `decompile-all --jobs 8` on tar O2 takes 26.0 s against 15.9 s under `param` (the output is identical to the serial run either way).
- **Where / provenance:** P5/aggregate-union · angr · structure-recovery · kuna-structsynth
- **Example:** `option structsynth param`

### `structmerge` -- off | siblings, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** one object has two or more struct_N names whose fields agree as far as both go; a synthesized record declares fewer fields than the program's own accesses show; two functions take a pointer to the same thing and their parameter types differ; the exported header defines struct_2 and struct_7 with the same first members.
- **What it does:** Give a synthesized record the fields a sibling reader of the same record proved. `structsynth` measures one function's accesses at a time and the layout ledger shares one `struct_N` between two functions only when one reader's claims are a SUBSET of the other's. Two readers that measured overlapping-but-different parts of one object -- the common case -- therefore get a name each, and each is declared to have only the fields its own function happened to touch: two readers of a `{char *name; long n; int flags; long tail;}` that each skip one member are given a record with a hole where `flags` is and a record that stops before `tail`. Over the eight layout builds 23 of the 77 ground-truth records kuna types at all are given more than one name this way. With the option on, a layout that nothing held answers for is merged with a held structure it was measured to agree with, and the UNION is minted in its place; the union strictly contains the held structure, so the convergence sweep (`decompile-all` and a serial `decompile-project`) decompiles that structure's readers again and moves them onto it. Two layouts are merged only where neither contradicts the other -- every offset both claim carries the same field, width, type and pointee spelled exactly as the ledger spells them, and no claim of one covers bytes the other claims at a different offset -- and only where the agreement is itself evidence: three shared claims, or two of which one is a pointer with a pointee, since two integer words at 0 and 8 are what `struct stat`, a `timespec` and a list node all begin with. The union is then held to the containment rule against each side separately, so a reader is still never declared to hold more than twice the fields it measured or four times its bytes, a table of opaque slots is still answered only by its own shape, no member lands in the alignment padding a reader's own claims leave, and the union still lays the reader's own members over every byte it dereferenced without claiming. Measured against DWARF on the eight layout builds (`fmt`/`ls`/`sort`/`du` at -O0 and -O2, 835 pointer-to-struct parameters, 9,443 fields): per-parameter claimed-field precision 0.8713 -> 0.8730 and recall 0.0932 -> 0.0960, F1 0.1684 -> 0.1731, with seven fewer `struct_N` names for the same records; no ground-truth record is newly given two names either, but that counts how many names a record has and says nothing about the opposite error. The agreement floor does fuse two records: two readers of two DIFFERENT objects that begin alike -- `{char *name; long n;}` is a job record and a connection record both -- clear the floor, are answered by one union, and each then declares a field its own object does not have. 19 of the 63 merges traced over sixteen builds sit exactly at that floor, and over 177 builds 189 of the 1,105 fields the merge adds are not fields of the DWARF record (916 are), so pooled claimed-field precision over those builds falls 0.9330 -> 0.9312 while it rises on the eight layout builds. That trade is why the option ships off.
- **When to flip:** Default OFF, and only ever acts where `structsynth` already synthesized something. Flip it on when a whole-binary run gives one object two or more `struct_N` names -- the give-away is two functions whose parameters have different record types that agree field for field as far as both go -- or when a record's declaration is visibly shorter than the program's own use of it. A parameter's type name can change (`struct_2 *` to `struct_7 *`) and its record gains the fields a second function measured, which moves the exported header's definitions and can change how address arithmetic past the reader's own last field is spelled. It can also leave a function WORSE typed than `off` does. The union is minted under a fresh name and supersedes the thinner record it contains, so the convergence sweep decompiles that record's readers again; the containment bounds that keep a thin reader off a record far larger than it measured can put the union out of its reach, and the redo's answer is not always as good as the one it replaces. On e2fsprogs `e2fsck` -O0 (1,908 functions, outside the layout set) three variables fall from `struct_35 */struct_87 *` to `void *` and two `char *` parameters of `reconfigure_bool` become `unsigned long`, costing that function type_match 0.67 -> 0.33, while one function gains a five-field record; with the sweep disabled (`--option protoorder lock`) not one variable on that binary changes type. Leave it off when a field that is not there costs more than a field that is missing: the merge can fuse two records. The agreement floor -- three shared claims, or two of which one is a typed pointer -- is cleared by two readers of two different objects that merely begin alike, and the union then gives each reader a field its object does not have; 19 of the 63 merges traced over sixteen builds clear the bar exactly there, 189 of the 1,105 fields the merge adds over 177 builds are not fields of the DWARF record, and pooled claimed-field precision over those builds falls 0.9330 -> 0.9312 (it rises, 0.8713 -> 0.8730, on the eight builds the layout instrument is published on). Leave it off too when you want each function's record to state exactly what THAT function proved, which is the more conservative reading and what every earlier round measured. The merge is a property of one process's ledger, so it needs a whole-program surface: `kuna decompile` spawns one `decomp_dbg` per function and a `--jobs N` worker answers from the parent's replay, so neither merges and both behave as `off` -- the same divergence `structsynth` already has. The convergence sweep runs one pass, so a union that supersedes a structure whose readers would themselves merge again can still leave two names, which is `structsynth`'s own non-transitivity rather than a new limit.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/aggregate-union · kuna · structure-recovery · typecampaign-layout-recall
- **Example:** `option structmerge siblings`

### `structheadless` -- off | closed, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a parameter is declared `void *` and every read of it is `((T *)a0)[K]` or `*(T *)((long)a0 + K)` with no read at offset 0; a function reads a record's later members and the listing shows a cast per access; `statx_to_stat` or a `fileinfo` accessor renders as casts of an untyped pointer; a record reader keeps `void *` while a sibling that reads the first member gets `struct_N *`.
- **What it does:** Give a record to a parameter a function reads only past the record's start. `structsynth` requires an access at offset 0 before it believes a pointer points at a record, so a function that reads a record's later members and never its first keeps the pointee it had -- `void *` for a pointer known only by its dereferences -- and every access is a cast of it: coreutils `ls` -O0 `sub_53e7` renders `if ((dat_2b358) && (((char *)a0)[0xb9])) v1 = ((unsigned int *)a0)[0x2b]; else v1 = ((unsigned int *)a0)[0xc];` for `struct fileinfo`'s `linkok`, `linkmode` and `stat.st_mode`, and `statx_to_stat` reads eighteen members of a `struct statx` and none of them `stx_mask` at 0. Over the 45 castbench binaries 1,238 parameters are refused for this reason alone, against 1,716 accepted. With `closed`, a parameter read at two or more constant offsets, none of them zero, is a record when every caller of its function is a known direct call (the `calleevote fields` closed set), nothing outside the function gave the parameter its pointee, and the parameter did not take a type its callers state; every other `structsynth` condition still applies, and so does the one `locals` adds for a partial view (no address formed at or past the end of every access, which would print as an element of a record array), and the bytes before the first access are `undefined1` filler like any hole. The closed condition keeps callbacks out: a `qsort` comparator or a hash-table callback reads members of what it was handed exactly like a record reader, and its declared parameter is `void *`. Against DWARF the headless parameters of closed functions are 883 struct pointers, no `void *`, two `char **` and three integers (75 more are -O2 parameters DWARF describes only through an abstract origin); those of functions whose address is stored are 202 struct pointers and 53 `void *`. A function whose main loop ends on the propagation pass that first typed it is never offered to `structsynth`, and a headless record gives the pointer-arithmetic rules nothing to rewrite, so such a function asks for one more pass, as a closed lone field already does. The record never overrides a type from outside the recovery: a headless record is open to `calleevote`'s vote when every caller passes the same `char *`, `char **` or declared record (coreutils `tail`'s `parse_obsolete_option` reads only `argv[1]` and `argv[2]` and keeps the `char **` `main` passes), a callee's synthesized record never replaces a pointer a declared call gives the caller's value (`getgrnam`'s `group *`, `getopt_long`'s `char **argv`), a headless record that types as a word a member the function reads through is refused as a vote, and a headless record the caller's own reads refuse falls back to the `void *` the callee states without it. Measured on main c960fb18d (castimplied, castarith, castsign and globalref on) over the 45 castbench binaries, both arms of one build: casts on the 4,815 functions kuna and IDA share fall 37,477 -> 36,040 (0.991 -> 0.953 times IDA; 219 functions fewer, 57 more, 36 of them where `globalref` stops naming a constant address because the function now passes it as a record and as another pointer, or reads a member of it directly), the 444-slice typesweep keeps 1,615 perfect (1 improved, 2 worse, none lost), the decbench#93 credited replay rises 2,188 -> 2,313 perfect, per-parameter layout recall rises 0.0932 -> 0.1131, and fields-only layout precision falls 0.8713 -> 0.8298 on the published instrument (0.9594 -> 0.9526 with embedded records, arrays of records and unions flattened in the ground truth). That fall, and the two worse rows, are why it ships off.
- **When to flip:** Default OFF. Flip it on when a stripped function reads one pointer at several fixed offsets and the listing is a run of `((unsigned int *)a0)[0x2b]` or `*(unsigned int *)((long)a0 + 0xac)` over a `void *` parameter -- the offsets are all past the start, so `structsynth` never took it -- and you want the reads as `a0->field_0xac`; it removes about 4% of the casts kuna prints on coreutils, grep, gzip, diffutils, tar and findutils. It acts only on a parameter of a function every caller of which is a known direct call in a whole-binary `decompile-all`/`decompile-project` run on x86-64 (the `calleevote fields` closed set), so it is inert under `kuna decompile`, a `--jobs` worker, `calleevote off`, and every other architecture, and only where `structsynth` fires. The record's first bytes are `undefined1` filler, so the exported header declares whatever the program has there as raw bytes. Leave it off when you need one `struct_N` per program object: a function that reads only part of a record mints its own partial view where it used to inherit the record its callers carry or had none, so one object can carry several names, each declaring only the members its reader measured (tar's `tar_stat_info` goes from one name over nine functions to five), and a local that holds a member's address can take the member's type instead of a declared one (gnulib `fts_stat` holds the address of its embedded `struct stat` as `unsigned long *` and casts it to `stat *` at `fstatat`). Leave it off too for an API whose opaque handle is a `void *` the function casts inside: bzip2's `BZ2_bzReadClose` takes `BZFILE *`, which is `void`, and gets a record the metric scores as a miss.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/aggregate-union · kuna · structure-recovery · typecampaign-structdeep
- **Example:** `option structheadless closed`

### `fieldtype` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a synthesized record declares long field_0x0 and every read of it is (char *)a0->field_0x0; free((void *)a0->field_0xb0) on a struct_N field; a function-pointer field prints as (*(void *)a0->field_0x40)(...); a record's buffer field is used in pointer arithmetic that prints as (char *)(a0->field_0x8 + a0->field_0x0).
