- **What it does:** Declare a synthesized record's field as the pointer the program uses it as. `structsynth` types each field from the widest access it measured, and among accesses of one width the first one it meets decides, so at -O0, where a field is reloaded for every use, the load that feeds an integer add decides: coreutils `sort` -O0 `fillbuf` declares `buffer.buf` as `long field_0x0` although the next load hands it to `memmove`, and every read prints a cast back (`memmove((void *)a0->field_0x0,(void *)((a0->field_0x8 - a0->field_0x20) + a0->field_0x0),a0->field_0x20)`); `ls` -O0 `free_ent` declares the security context `long` and prints `free((void *)a0->field_0xb0)` and `freecon((char *)a0->field_0xb0)`; a function-pointer field compared with zero before it is called is declared `unsigned long` and the call prints as `(*(void *)a0->field_0x40)(*v3)`, which is not C. When on, the accesses whose value the program uses as a pointer are the evidence: a value (or a copy or cast of it) that a load or store goes through, that an indirect call jumps to, that a declared pointer parameter takes, or that a function declared to return a pointer returned. The type a value picks up by being merged with another value is not evidence, so a register that carries a number on one path and a string on another does not make the number a `char *`. A field of which such an access carries a pointer, and no access a float, is declared as the most specific pointer they carry -- a record, named aggregate or code pointee outranks a scalar one, which outranks an undefined one, which outranks `void` -- provided that pointer is the only one of its rank or the only one of its rank a declared parameter the value is passed to names, and the first access does not already carry a pointer whose pointee outranks it. A field whose value is loaded and compared with a value loaded from a field so declared takes the same pointer, since C compares a pointer only with a compatible one. A field some access divides, takes a remainder of, shifts, multiplies (other than negates), compares with sign, sign-extends or converts to a float keeps its type: an index or a hash stays a number even where it is once handed to a `void *` parameter. Integer accesses of a re-typed field are unchanged: the printer casts the pointer where an operation needs a number. `free_ent` prints `free(a0->field_0xb0)` and `freecon(a0->field_0xb0)`, and the call prints `(*a0->field_0x40)(*v3)`. Acts only where `structsynth` synthesizes a record.
- **When to flip:** Default OFF. Flip it on when a synthesized record declares a field as an integer and every pointer use of it prints a cast back -- `(char *)a0->field_0x0`, `free((void *)a0->field_0xb0)`, `(*(void *)a0->field_0x40)(...)` -- and you want the field declared as the pointer the program uses it as; on the 4,815 functions kuna and IDA both emit it removes 134 casts in 53 functions and adds 35 in 14 (net -99). It is off because the record a function shares with another is decided by exact field-type agreement, so a field re-typed in one reader moves which record another reader is answered with, and the fields-only layout precision of the eight-build layout census drops (docs/features/fieldtype/default-on-evaluation.md). A field proven only as a pointer to undefined words (`unsigned long *` for a record kuna reads by the word) can make the locals it is read into, which stay `long`, pay a cast per read: sort -O0 `mergelines_node` gains 20. It never turns a field into a number: a field whose first access already carries a pointer keeps it, and an integer that is only ever added and handed to a declared `void *` parameter cannot be told from an address and is declared `void *`.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/aggregate-union · kuna · type-inference · castcampaign-fieldtype
- **Example:** `option fieldtype on`

### `noreturn_known` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** dead code kept after calls to exit/abort/panic when off; call to a known no-return libc function still shows a fall-through path; unreachable epilogue after std::terminate or a rust panic call.
- **What it does:** Run the known-no-return analysis pass: mark exit/abort/_Unwind_Resume/std::terminate-style functions no-return (the kuna analog of Ghidra's NoReturnFunctionAnalyzer, plus the Rust panic/handle_alloc_error list). The same flag covers the flow-time name matches that reach the externs the address-keyed scan cannot (`kuna_noreturn_externmatch.rs`, `kuna_noreturnextern.rs`: an undefined extern of an ET_REL object whose name is on the list) and the error(nonzero,...) value rule inside the no-return propagation (an error(status,...) wrapper whose status is a nonzero literal is no-return). It also ends a call to a `<prefix>__<entry>` proxy stub (`stub___stack_chk_fail`, an empty `__wrap___assert_fail`: a sized one-instruction return or jump named for a multi-word list entry) when that call is the last instruction of its sized caller, so the caller was compiled for the no-return original. On a Go binary the same vendored Go list is also applied to the pclntab-recovered function list (the gonoreturn pass, formerly its own option), so a stripped Go binary whose symbol tables are gone still gets its runtime.panic*/throw/goexit facts.
- **When to flip:** On (default) suppresses dead fall-through after a no-return call; off leaves the call rendering as if it returns (dead code reappears).
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · kuna · analysis-enablement · kuna-analysis-noreturn
- **Example:** `option noreturn_known off`

### `noreturn_disc` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** heavily-called custom die()/fatal() wrapper still treated as returning; dead code after a stripped sub_ wrapper that never falls through at 3+ call sites; caller swallows the next function after a wrapper call.
- **What it does:** Run the discovered-no-return consumer (the first Listing/xref consumer): the evidence-tally fixpoint over the Listing — a call target is no-return when at least 3 of its call sites show no valid fall-through (the instruction after the call is not a valid instruction start / fell into data / is another function's entry), iterated to a fixpoint (a function whose last act is a call to an already-discovered-no-return function is itself no-return). The kuna analog of Ghidra's FindNoReturnFunctionsAnalyzer. Requires the Listing (option listing on) — a no-op when the Listing is absent. On by default (DIV-22, matching Ghidra's default-on analyzer), but gated on the Listing (default-off), so every parity gate is byte-identical (real-ELF Listing path only). Only POSITIVE evidence counts at a call site: the successor is data (outside every executable range) or another function's entry, or the call has no fall-through at all; a successor that merely failed to decode is not evidence, because the Listing walk attempts every call's successor and that arm would be a decode-failure detector forging no-return verdicts on kuna's own spec gaps (GH-312, DIV-92, formerly the noreturn_discstrict option).
- **When to flip:** On by default (DIV-22), but a no-op unless the Listing is built (option listing on) — with the Listing off there is zero behavior change. With listing on it marks heavily-called custom/tail-calling no-return wrappers — that the static name lists do not know — no-return by the >=3-call-site evidence tally, eliminating the post-call dead code on a real-ELF target. Flip OFF (with listing on) to keep the post-call fall-through code.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · kuna · analysis-enablement · kuna-analysis-noreturn-disc
- **Example:** `option listing on --option noreturn_disc on`

### `noreturn_propagate` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** unreachable code after a call to an exit/fatal wrapper; function truncated after calling a cold wrapper; spurious while(true) around a call that never returns; stripped binary's unnamed exit wrapper swallows the functions after it.
- **What it does:** REMOVES CODE: propagates no-return through the call graph, dropping unreachable code after no-return calls. Runs the structural no-return propagation consumer (the second Listing/xref consumer): the kuna analog of angr's CFGFast call-graph no-return propagation. Seed the terminal set from the Known no-return list and conclude a function no-return when its last real instruction (skipping trailing NOP alignment padding) is a CALL (or tail JMP) to an already-no-return callee, with no RETURN path, no computed jump, and no branch escaping the reachable body — iterated to a fixpoint, with NO evidence threshold (unlike noreturn_disc's >=3 call sites). Catches a custom no-return wrapper (e.g. coreutils xalloc_die, which ends in `call abort` followed by padding) that the static name list does not know and the >=3-evidence rule does not reach, so a caller (e.g. tee_O2 x2nrealloc) no longer grows a spurious while(true)/goto from the dead fall-through. Emits the existing NoReturnFact -> the existing set_function_no_return commit seam (no new commit arm, no S7 work). Requires the Listing (option listing on) — a no-op when the Listing is absent. On by default (DIV-14), but gated on the Listing (default-off), so every parity gate is byte-identical (real-ELF Listing path only).
- **When to flip:** On by default (DIV-14), but a no-op unless the Listing is built (option listing on) — with the Listing off there is zero behavior change. With listing on it concludes a custom no-return wrapper (a die()/fatal()/xalloc_die() that unconditionally ends in abort/exit) is no-return where it would otherwise be treated as returning — angr renders the caller cleanly but kuna would emit a spurious while(true) loop + goto + dead stack spills from the post-call fall-through (e.g. tee_O2 x2nrealloc). Broader than noreturn_disc: no >=3 call-site threshold and it seeds from the Known list. Flip OFF (with listing on) to keep the post-call fall-through code in the output.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · angr · structure-recovery · kuna-analysis-noreturn-propagate
- **Example:** `option listing on --option noreturn_propagate on`

### `noreturn_reach` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** wrapper with a mid-body fatal call still treated as returning; unreachable write()/return tail keeps a fatal wrapper looking like it returns; switch whose every arm ends in a no-return call not concluded no-return; caller decodes garbage past an sshpkt_fatal-style wrapper.
- **What it does:** REMOVES CODE: the CFG-reachability no-return rule — the port of Ghidra's FindNoReturnFunctionsAnalyzer.targetOnlyCallsNoReturn ('Non-Returning Functions - Discovered' analyzer). kuna's noreturn_propagate concludes a wrapper no-return only when its LAST real instruction is a terminal call to an already-no-return callee (a tail-call subset). That misses three shapes Ghidra catches by walking the CFG: (1) a no-return call MID-body with a dead tail after it (e.g. openssh sshpkt_fatal, whose FIRST statement is `call sshpkt_vfatal` and whose write()/return tail is unreachable); (2) a RETURN that is present but UNREACHABLE (the path to it dies at a no-return call); (3) a SWITCH (indirect jump) whose every arm ends in a no-return call (openssh sshpkt_vfatal). When on, for each candidate the rule walks the instruction-level reachable CFG from entry, treats a call/jump to an already-no-return callee as terminal (its fall-through is dead), and concludes no-return iff NO RETURN is reachable and at least one path ends at a no-return transfer — iterated to a call-graph fixpoint by the same propagate loop, emitting the same NoReturnFact -> set_function_no_return seam. Conservative: a reachable RETURN, an unresolved indirect jump, a branch escaping the body to a possibly-returning neighbour, or a call with no modelled fall-through that is not itself terminal all reject (a false positive would drop live caller code). Requires the Listing (option listing on) AND noreturn_propagate on — a no-op otherwise. On by default (DIV-19), gated on the Listing (default-off), so every parity gate is byte-identical (real-ELF Listing path only).
- **When to flip:** On by default (DIV-19), a no-op unless the Listing is built (option listing on) and noreturn_propagate is on. With listing on it concludes internal fatal wrappers that kuna's tail-call rule (noreturn_propagate/noreturn_error) misses because the no-return call is mid-body, the return is dead, or the function routes through a switch — where kuna would otherwise decode the cold error path / adjacent function's bytes as live code past the wrapper call, ballooning the caller and inflating GED vs ghidra (openssh sshpkt_fatal/ssh_tun_confirm, shadow oom). This is the general 'Non-Returning Functions - Discovered' reachability that ghidra runs by default. Flip OFF (with listing on) to fall back to the strict tail-call rule (keeps the post-call fall-through code).
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · ghidra · correctness-fix · kuna-analysis-noreturn-reach
- **Example:** `option listing on --option noreturn_reach on`

### `fatstr` -- off | auto | always, default `auto`

- **Symptoms:** rust or go string argument renders as a raw rodata address beside its length instead of the literal text; takes_str(&DAT_00102000, 15) where the 15 bytes at that address are plainly the string; string literals recovered on C binaries but never on rust or go ones.
- **What it does:** Render a length-carried (ptr, len) constant call-argument pair as a bounded string literal. Rust (&str, &[u8]) and Go (string) carry a string's length beside its pointer and never NUL-terminate the bytes, so the classic literal path - which reads the image until a terminator - refuses them and every string argument renders as a raw rodata address beside a magic length: takes_str((char *)&DAT_00102000, 15). The length is right there in the adjacent argument, so the rule reads exactly that many bytes and routes them through the existing bounded literal mechanism (Funcdata::get_internal_string -> the BUILTIN_STRINGDATA user-op, the constseq path, which needs no terminator): takes_str("hello multilang", 15). A pair is rewritten only when both arguments are p-code constants adjacent in the call's inputs, 2 <= len <= 4096, the pointed-at bytes are READ-ONLY in the image (query_global_properties, the msvcstrappend literal test), and the bytes decode as UTF-8 text with no control characters beyond newline/tab/CR and at least one alphanumeric - or the pointer's facing type carries a text language facet (the multilang W3 side table on the type factory), a type provider's statement that outranks the byte heuristic. The length argument is kept: the call really does pass it. At auto (default) the rule acts only when the image's source language is Rust or Go (the sourcelang fact), a structural no-op elsewhere; always drops the language test (stage-test bytechunks); off keeps the raw pointer. The option also gates the ANALYSIS-side recognizer (pass id fatstrrecords, registered for a rustc- or Go-detected image): both languages pack unterminated literals back to back in .rodata, so the NUL-run string scan glues adjacent literals into one wrong row; the static (ptr, len) records that carry every Rust literal's length (a PIE's R_*_RELATIVE slots in .data.rel.ro, absolute pairs on a non-PIE) are re-read as length-BOUNDED string facts, committed ahead of the NUL stream so the glued rows retire and the data symbol at each literal spans exactly the literal. off drops both recognizers; the record facts are dropped at the read-symbols boundary like every analysis gate.
- **When to flip:** Leave auto: on a Rust or Go binary every constant &str/string argument renders as its literal text instead of a raw &DAT_ address beside a magic length. Use always on a carved bytechunk or raw image with no language signal. Flip off when auditing exact rodata addresses, or if a read-only buffer of coincidentally printable bytes is being misread as text at a call site.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/const-pointer · kuna · type-inference · kuna-multilang-fatstr
- **Example:** `option fatstr always`

### `gomorestack` -- off | auto | always, default `auto` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** every function of a Go binary opens with if (condition) { runtime_morestack_noctxt(); } inside a loop to the entry; go function parameters recovered as phi-fed locals or missing because the entry is a loop head; do-while wrapping an entire go function body with a morestack call in its latch.
- **What it does:** Fold the Go stack-growth prologue. Every non-leaf function the Go compiler emits opens with a guard - compare SP against the goroutine's stackguard, and on failure call runtime.morestack(_noctxt) and LOOP BACK TO THE FUNCTION ENTRY to re-run the prologue on the grown stack. The check is pure runtime machinery (the function's own semantics are the fall-through path), but the back-edge makes the entry a loop head, so every live argument register joins its incoming value with its after-growth value and parameter recovery sees phi-fed arguments on every non-leaf Go function. The fold matches the tight guard/grow two-block cycle sitting on the inserted entry block (the shared entry-guard-loop shape, infra/idiom.rs) with the cold arm calling a runtime.morestack* routine - the name is only accepted IN the shape, so a coincidental name in straight-line flow cuts nothing - and removes the guard edge pre-SSA (the cleanupcode window), so the entry phi never forms and the guard's compare and stackguard load die to ordinary dead-code elimination. At auto (default) the fold acts only when the image's source language is Go (the sourcelang fact), making it a structural no-op on every non-Go binary; always drops the language test for corpora with no detection signal (a stage-test bytechunk); off keeps the guard for auditing.
- **When to flip:** Leave auto: on a Go binary the fold turns every function's entry-loop + runtime.morestack_noctxt() noise into straight-line flow and un-breaks parameter recovery; off only to audit the real prologue instructions (e.g. verifying a hand-patched stackguard). Use always on a Go function carved into a bytechunk or a raw image where detection has no buildinfo section to find.
- **Where / provenance:** P2/flow-classification · kuna · structure-recovery · kuna-multilang-gomorestack
- **Example:** `option gomorestack off`

### `gonewtype` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** go newobject results declared long or undefined8 while the call names its type: descriptor; field stores into a fresh go allocation render as offset arithmetic on an integer local; harvested go record types visible at interface conversions but never on allocations; go allocation sites cast their result at every use instead of declaring the named pointer.
- **What it does:** Type a Go allocation result from the descriptor it allocates - the first client of the per-call-site output TYPE LOCK. Go's allocators take the runtime descriptor of the type they allocate: `runtime.newobject(typ *_type) unsafe.Pointer` returns a fresh zeroed object OF that type, and go1.26+ compilers inline the same call into the size-class `runtime.mallocgc*` entries (`mallocgcSmallScanNoHeaderSC4(size, typ, needzero)`, ...), descriptor second. At a site whose descriptor argument resolves to a `type:<name>` data symbol (gotypeglobals) whose `<name>` the gotypes harvest interned as a complete named record, the result's type is a fact stated by the binary's own metadata. A plain vote at the type-inference seam cannot deliver it: `typeOrder` folding and structsynth override the voted type before the declaration prints, and parking a prototype locks EVERY site of the callee to one output (`void *`). The option therefore asserts the fact through the sitetypelock primitive: the lock is recorded in the P0 override store keyed by the CALL op's address (surviving restarts like every per-site override), and `ActionSiteTypeLock` pins it onto the call's output Varnode (`update_type_locked(lock=true, over=false)`) directly before the first `buildLocaltypes`, riding the same Varnode-typelock chain a type-locked Database symbol rides - propagation refuses to enter a locked Varnode, `writeBack` refuses to replace it, structsynth installs with `over=false`, and the HighVariable's type representative prefers the locked member. Refusals leave the site untouched: no output Varnode, output already type-locked (mapped-symbol/DWARF evidence outranks the client), descriptor argument not a constant address (or one COPY away), constant not at the START of a `type:` symbol, `<name>` not held as a complete named record (pointer/array/primitive spellings and empty shells refuse, so the lock never blocks a later structsynth recovery), a mallocgc-family size argument that is not a constant equal to the record's size, or an output-width mismatch. The lock changes downstream pointer-arithmetic restructuring (field reads render as `->field`), which is why the whole-corpus two-leg diff ships with the feature; a wrong descriptor decode would mis-NAME fields but never moves or deletes a statement. Structurally inert off Go images: the callee name, the `type:` symbol and the interned record only exist where the Go harvest ran.
- **When to flip:** On by default: every escaping Go allocation declares its result as a pointer to the program's own named record (`main.Point *p = runtime.newobject(&type:main.Point)`) and downstream field accesses render by name instead of offset arithmetic. Flip off to compare against the untyped rendering (triaging a suspect field layout back to the descriptor walk) or to let structsynth re-derive the layout from accesses alone. Non-Go binaries are byte-identical either way.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · kuna · type-inference · kuna-multilang-gonewtype
- **Example:** `option gonewtype off`

### `gowritebarrier` -- off | auto | always, default `auto` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** every pointer store in a go function wrapped in if (writeBarrier flag) with a gcWriteBarrier call; stores through an undefined local after a gcWriteBarrier call because the thunk's buffer register is not modeled; go output doubled in size by GC bookkeeping diamonds.
- **What it does:** Fold the Go GC write-barrier diamond. Every pointer store the garbage collector must see compiles to a flag test: when runtime.writeBarrier is set, call a runtime.gcWriteBarrier<N> thunk (which hands back the GC pointer buffer, R11 on amd64) and record the old and new pointer values in it; both paths then perform the program's own stores at the join. The cold arm is GC bookkeeping with no bearing on what the function computes, and it actively corrupts the output today: the thunk's buffer register is not a modeled return, so the recording stores read an undefined local and the value split can mangle even the real store's address expression. The fold matches the shared guarded-cold-call shape (infra/idiom.rs): a one-block cold arm holding exactly one call, whose guard rejoins the hot path in one hop - the callee name (runtime.gcWriteBarrier, gcWriteBarrier1..8, the bare assembly thunk gcWriteBarrier; never wbBufFlush, which user code cannot call inline) is only accepted INSIDE that shape, so a coincidental name in ordinary flow cuts nothing. The guard edge is removed pre-SSA (the cleanupcode/gomorestack window, registered directly after gomorestack), so the buffer-feeding loads die to ordinary dead-code elimination and the program's stores at the join are untouched. At auto (default) the fold acts only when the image's source language is Go; always drops the language test (stage-test bytechunks); off keeps the barrier for auditing GC behavior. A second, post-SSA arm of the same option folds the shapes this pre-SSA fold must refuse - an arm SHARED by several guards, and an arm whose call result (the wb buffer pointer) and register effects feed the join's phis - once SSA has made every read explicit: the matcher proves every guard reads a global flag, every arm op is bookkeeping with stores only through the call's own buffer pointer, and no arm-defined value escapes except through the join phis, then cuts one guard edge per pass so the unreachable sweep collapses each phi to the hot-path value the program computes. The post-SSA arm REFUSES a value-returning function whose barrier output or arm INDIRECT effects reach a RETURN or an outside store address - the return-value staging dataflow a fold must never orphan (two miscompiles proved it; a refusal is a kept barrier, never wrong C); a void function keeps the fold, where the same reach is a preserved caller register. Whenever the fold is enabled on a Go image, the jump-only forwarding blocks an unoptimized build places between the flag test and the barrier call are normalized away first (`kuna_gojumpchain.rs`).
- **When to flip:** Leave auto: on a Go binary every guarded pointer store sheds its if (runtime_writeBarrier) { gcWriteBarrierN(); buffer writes } wrapper and renders as the plain store; off only to audit the GC's barrier placement. Use always on a Go function carved into a bytechunk where detection has no buildinfo section to find.
- **Where / provenance:** P2/flow-classification · kuna · structure-recovery · kuna-multilang-gowritebarrier
- **Example:** `option gowritebarrier off`

### `ptrauthtrap` -- on | off, default `on` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** if ((v ^ v << 1) >> 0x3e & 1) before a tail call in an arm64e function; (*SoftwareBreakpoint(0xc471,..))() // jump-as-call; a stack - 0x8 ;  x30 variable declared only for a pointer-auth check.
- **What it does:** Drop the pointer-authentication failure checks an arm64e compiler plants after an aut* instruction. Without FEAT_FPAC a failed aut* does not trap; it leaves an error code in the pointer's top bits, so Apple's clang checks the result inline and branches to brk #0xc470+key when it is bad: before a tail call it tests that bits 62 and 61 of the authenticated x30 agree (eor x16, x30, x30, lsl #1; tbz x16, #62), after a data aut* it compares the result with its xpac-stripped copy. SLEIGH hides the aut* itself (ShowPAC is off), so statically every pointer authenticates and the check is noise; the xpac form folds away on its own, but the bit test reads the incoming return address and renders as if ((x30 ^ x30 << 1) >> 0x3e & 1) { (*SoftwareBreakpoint(0xc471,..))(); return; } before nearly every tail call of an Apple binary. The trap block is the anchor: a block lifted entirely from one brk whose SoftwareBreakpoint immediate is 0xc470-0xc473, the codes LLVM reserves for this trap. A CBRANCH edge into it is removed pre-SSA (the gomorestack window) only when the guard's condition is that bit test of the return address, ((x30 ^ x30 << 1) >> 62) & 1, the edge is the arm taken when the two bits disagree, and x30 was reloaded from the frame (an sp- or x29-based load) or is unwritten anywhere in the function: the brk immediate alone is not evidence, since any AArch64 code can branch to a brk #0xc470 on a condition of its own, and a value the code put in x30 (mov x30, x0; ldr x30, [x0]) is not the authenticated return address. The condition then dies to dead-code elimination.
- **When to flip:** Leave on: an arm64e function's tail call reads as the call alone. Flip off to audit where the compiler checks an authenticated pointer. Inert on any guard other than the return-address bit test before a brk #0xc470-0xc473 trap, whatever the image format.
- **Where / provenance:** P2/flow-classification · kuna · structure-recovery · kuna-apple-ptrauthtrap
- **Example:** `option ptrauthtrap off`

### `gobool` -- off | auto | always, default `auto` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** go function returning bool prints v = CONCAT71((undefined7)(v >> 8), a == b) instead of returning the comparison; return value masked with 0xffffffff around a boolean; undefined7 casts feeding a concatenation at every boolean return.
- **What it does:** Narrow a Go boolean return's stale-high concatenation. Go's ABI materializes a bool result as 0/1 in the LOW BYTE of the return register and leaves the upper bytes unspecified: the compiler emits a bare SETcc with no zeroing XOR, so the lifted value is PIECE(stale7, bool1) feeding the RETURN and the C prints the CONCAT71 artifact (v = CONCAT71((undefined7)(v >> 8), x == y); return v & 0xffffffff). SubvariableFlow's return pull rightly refuses to narrow it - nothing proves the high bytes zero - and rustc never shows the shape because it zeroes first. The rule rewrites such a RETURN to read ZEXT(bool) instead, asserting the ABI fact the way rustabi asserts the ScalarPair: the stale bytes are unspecified, so zeroing them is the declared reading, and the dead concatenation is collected by ordinary dead-code elimination. The low byte must be a genuine boolean definition (a comparison, carry/borrow, boolean logic or float predicate opcode); any other 7+1 concatenation is left alone. At auto (default) the rule acts only when the image's source language is Go; always drops the language test (stage-test bytechunks); off keeps the faithful concatenation.
- **When to flip:** Leave auto: Go functions returning bool stop printing CONCAT71 noise and return their comparison directly. Use always on a Go function carved into a bytechunk where detection has nothing to read; off only to audit the raw register dataflow.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/output-prototype · kuna · correctness-fix · kuna-multilang-gobool
- **Example:** `option gobool off`

### `objcivars` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** an objective-c method reads *(long *)((long)self + dat_<addr>) instead of self->_ivar; self is objc_object * in every -[Class sel] although the class declares ivars; objc_storeStrong((long)self + <Class>::_ivar, x) instead of &self->_ivar.
- **What it does:** Give every Objective-C class of the image an instance struct built from its ivar list and type each of its methods' `self` with it. `class_ro_t.ivars` names each ivar with its type encoding, its size and a pointer to its OFFSET VARIABLE in `__objc_ivar` — the word a compiled method loads and adds to `self` (`ldrsw x8,[x8,#off]; ldr d0,[x19,x8]`), because under the non-fragile ABI the runtime may slide that offset when a superclass from another image grows. Statically the word holds the compile-time layout, so this builds `struct <Class>` with each ivar at that offset (a local superclass embedded as `super` at 0, an imported one left as an anonymous prefix; field types from the encoding, `@"NSString"` an opaque `NSString *`), types `self` as `<Class> *` in the class's instance methods and its categories' instance methods, and reports the offset variables constant (the `dynrelocs` RELRO fold path), so `*(double *)((long)self + Foo::ratio)` renders `self->ratio` and `objc_storeStrong((long)self + Foo::_name, x)` renders `objc_storeStrong(&self->_name, x)`. A class of another image, or one with no field of its own, still types `self` as a pointer to its declared (opaque) record. An ivar, a property getter/setter (its attribute string names the class: `T@"Base"`) and a stub whose declaration names a class of this image are typed with that class's struct too, so `self->inner->count` and `Base * -[Holder inner]` render. Off: no class struct is interned, `self` stays `objc_object *`, the offset variable keeps its `<Class>::<ivar>` name and the load through it stays a load. A class whose name already denotes a complete struct (DWARF) is that struct. Inert unless `objc` is on; a structural no-op on every non-Mach-O image. Load-time, env-bridged (KUNA_OBJCIVARS) as well as commit-time: set it before the `load file` it should apply to.
- **When to flip:** On by default: the layout is the one the compiler emitted and IDA renders the same `self->_ivar`. Flip off when a superclass from another image may have grown since the binary was built (then the runtime slides the offsets and the static layout is stale) or to read the offset-variable loads themselves. Inert unless `objc` is on; `objc` is on for a Mach-O image under 500 KiB, where `auto` selects the `aggressive` preset.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · kuna · analysis-enablement · kuna-analysis-objc
- **Example:** `option objcivars off`

### `paramcopyhoist` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** parameter copy-shadow assignment (v6 = a1;) emitted below an earlier guard instead of at the top of the function; kuna places some parameter spill copies in the entry block and others after a guard in the same function; extra CFG nodes versus the source around a cascade of if (p && !*p) p = NULL; parameter guards; vN = aM; for an unmodified incoming parameter appearing in the middle of a guard cascade.
- **What it does:** Anchor the copy-shadow of an UNMODIFIED INCOMING PARAMETER in the function's entry block instead of at the tail of the MULTIEQUAL slot's predecessor, so a guarded parameter's `vN = aM;` prints where the source's spill is -- with the other parameter spills -- rather than below an earlier guard. gcc -O0 gives every parameter a stack home, and the source idiom `if (p && !*p) p = NULL;` leaves a MULTIEQUAL at the guard's join whose incoming slots are the raw input register. `Merge::mergeOp` cannot merge the input-register HighVariable with the address-tied stack-slot HighVariable, so `Merge::trimOpInput` snips each offending slot into a COPY and places it with `opInsertEnd(copyop, op->getParent()->getIn(slot))` -- the tail of that slot's PREDECESSOR -- and that COPY is what prints as `vN = aM;`. For the FIRST parameter the guard's join predecessors intersect at the entry block, so `Merge::buildDominantCopy`'s `findCommonBlock` lands the copy there and it renders correctly; for every later parameter the intersection is the previous guard's join, so the copy sinks below that guard and splits the source's single entry block in two. Both producing sub-cases are covered: two-or-more trimmed slots (later collapsed by buildDominantCopy) and exactly one trimmed slot (no dominant-copy pass at all, so the single opInsertEnd is final). Implemented as ActionParamCopyHoist, the LAST action in universal_sched: taking the decision inside `Merge::trimOpInput` itself defeats the trim's own purpose (the widened Cover fails mergeOp's test, mergeOp falls through to trimOpOutput, and markInternalCopies then hides both resulting COPYs, so the assignment DISAPPEARS from the emitted C), and running the move any earlier than ActionFinalStructure perturbs the P8 duplication passes. Legality is buildDominantCopy's own Cover test re-run against the hypothetical hoisted placement and the FINAL HighVariable (b_cover over the high's other instances vs an a_cover whose def point is taken at the START of the entry block, rejecting on `intersect > 1`), which over-approximates and errs toward rejecting; only a formal parameter's storage is ever hoisted, only when a MULTIEQUAL reads the copy, and only when the target variable has exactly one candidate.
- **When to flip:** Turn ON when a parameter's copy-shadow assignment (`v6 = a1;`) is emitted below an earlier guard instead of with the other parameter spills at the top of the function, adding CFG nodes the source does not have. Measured on decbench O0 e2fsprogs/e2fsck save_output (0x4eeb6): 53 nodes/77 edges GED 29.0 -> 51 nodes/77 edges GED 17.0 (-12), which is GED-OPTIMAL for the construct (deleting the copies entirely and writing through the parameter, which is literally what the source does, also scores 17.0). Broad on -O0: over four O0 binaries (e2fsprogs/e2fsck, coreutils/ls, gzip/gzip, bzip2/bzip2; 3031 functions) 121 functions (4.0%) emit at least one top-level parameter copy-shadow outside the entry block -- 200 sunk copies against 318 correctly in the entry -- and turning it on moves 92 of them (200 -> 108 sunk, 318 -> 479 in the entry) across 116 changed functions with zero new decompile errors. Every one of those 116 was diffed: 99 are pure re-orderings of `vN = aM;`, 17 have a secondary rendering effect (mostly a comma side-effect inside a short-circuit condition becoming a plain statement, which is an improvement; 2 leave an empty `if (c) { }` then-branch). Default-OFF opt-in: it is a deliberate DIVERGENCE from upstream Ghidra, which sinks the copy to exactly the same place, and although the default-ON ablation is clean on the datatests (0/675, PARITY OK) it regresses one stage assertion (condfold #3) and the decbench aggregate has not been measured, so the flip is left to a follow-up.
- **Where / provenance:** P6/merge-aggressiveness · kuna · structure-recovery · decbench-parameter-copy-shadow-placement
- **Example:** `option paramcopyhoist on`

### `indirectonly` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a value stored into a stack slot is printed into a register local and the slot is never assigned; a struct filled on the frame is passed by address to a call although the emitted C never wrote it; a declared local is never written and never read anywhere in the function; a `vN = slot;` ... `slot = vN;` round-trip copy pair around a loop that only reads the slot; a call result assigned to a temporary that is immediately assigned to a stack slot.
- **What it does:** Set the `indirectonly` Varnode flag on a function input whose value is never really read, so the two merge-phalanx tests that carry an exception for that case can take it. An ILLEGAL INPUT is an input Varnode that ActionDirectWrite never reached -- nothing a formal parameter feeds can be responsible for its value -- which on a normal frame means the leftover contents of a stack slot the function overwrites before it reads. Merge::mergeTestAdjacent refuses every speculative merge involving such a variable, so an uninitialized value is not printed as a real one, and HighVariable::hasName refuses to name an unaffected input whose members are all of that kind. Both refusals end 'unless the illegal input is only used indirectly', and that exception needs a flag that nothing in kuna set: Funcdata::markIndirectOnly and Funcdata::checkIndirectUse (funcdata_varnode.cc:801-858) were unported and ActionMarkIndirectOnly was a documented no-op, so is_indirect_only() answered false everywhere and both tests rejected strictly more than upstream. checkIndirectUse is a worklist over the def-set: a reader that is a plain CPUI_INDIRECT is the accepting case and the walk stops there (an INDIRECT records that some other op MAY have overwritten the storage, it is not a use of the value); an INDIRECT caused by a STORE is accepted but the walk continues through its output, since the value survives the store; a CPUI_MULTIEQUAL is transparent and the walk continues through its output; ANY OTHER READER fails the whole test, so one arithmetic use, one compare or one call argument anywhere in the def-set leaves the input isolated exactly as before. ON runs that scan in the scheduled slot, one action ahead of ActionMergeAdjacent and well ahead of ActionNameVars, which is stock Ghidra behaviour; OFF, the default, restores the inert stub byte-for-byte.
- **When to flip:** OFF by default, although the body is upstream verbatim, because the merge it unlocks can fabricate a store. When the illegal input is the SOURCE of the copy -- the machine loads an escaped frame slot into a register and then mutates the register -- the merge makes the emitted C mutate the slot, and a later call that was handed the enclosing object reads a value the machine never wrote there. The heritage pass cannot catch it: an INDIRECT is only attached where the storage is still live in the SSA, so a slot whose last read is before the loop gets no INDIRECT at any call after it and the cover-intersection test has nothing to intersect. Stock Ghidra 12.1.2 emits the same fabricated store on the same input (docs/features/indirectonly/counterexample.md), so this is an upstream defect the port inherits rather than a porting error; kuna declines to inherit it by default. Turn it ON to reproduce Ghidra variable partitioning exactly, or for the merges that are sound: where the illegal input is the DESTINATION -- the machine really does store to the slot -- the value is computed into the slot instead of into a temporary that is assigned across, and the assignment, now a COPY inside one variable, is hidden by markInternalCopies; on coreutils `ls` -O2 `main` the two 8-byte loads that fill a 16-byte `struct dev_ino` on the frame stop being printed into two register locals that the following `hash_delete(..., &di)` never sees. The blast radius is small and was measured over 34 whole-binary `decompile-all` slices (ls, sort, grep, gzip, diff, bzip2, find, tar at -O0 and -O2, plus kmod, e2fsck, dpkg, dpkg-query, dash and bash at -O0, -O2 and -O2-noinline): 27 functions change and the corpus loses 19 declarations net, but 24 of the 27 write a frame slot inside an object whose address reaches a later call, so nothing in the emitted C certifies a safe subset -- of the six settled against the disassembly, four restore a store the machine really makes (`ls` -O2 `main`, `tar` -O0 `sub_429c6`, `dpkg` -O0 `sub_2019c`, `e2fsck` -O0 `sub_1680a`, three of them -O0 frames where the variable really does live in memory) while two fabricate one (`bzip2` -O2 `sub_3890`, `kmod` -O2-noinline `sub_97b0`, both -O2 where the value lives in a register for its whole lifetime).
- **Where / provenance:** P6/merge-aggressiveness · ghidra · presentation-default · kuna-indirectonly
- **Example:** `option indirectonly on`

### `outline` -- off | <fn>:<head>-<exit>[;...], default `off` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** an inlined callee body is spliced into the caller and should read as a call; want to pull a chosen region out of a function into a named pseudofunction; acting on an almostregion inline-candidate report by hand or with an llm.
- **What it does:** Stage 2 of inline identification: excise a SUPPLIED single-entry region and emit a call to a synthesized pseudofunction in its place. Where almostregion finds candidate inlined regions, this acts on one - and the choice does not have to come from almostregion, so a human reading the code or an LLM agent reading almostregion's report can drive the transform directly. The value names the owning function entry as well as the region, because an option value is global to the run and every function is decompiled under it. The region is a block SET re-derived from the CFG with the same single-entry predicate almostregion uses; the value only names the head and the exit, and is re-verified against the live bblocks every time rather than trusted. Runs in the pre-SSA window immediately before heritage, so the edge surgery needs no MULTIEQUAL patching and ActionFuncLink still materializes the call's argument and return varnodes. v1 declines - leaving the function untouched - unless the head/exit really bound a single-entry region, exactly one edge enters the head from outside it, at most one value is live out, and the region contains no call and no STORE. Liveness is computed over the region's continuation (blocks reachable from the exit) with sub-register aliases merged, because an x86 32-bit write zero-extends and would otherwise count one register twice.
- **When to flip:** Off (default; inert, and inert also when a region is supplied for a different function). Supply a region to pull an inlined callee body back out into a named call - typically taking the head and exit from `--option almostregion report`.
- **Where / provenance:** P8/goto-quality · kuna · opt-in-tool · kuna-inline-identification
- **Example:** `--option outline 0x401000:0x40100a-0x401018`

### `stackaddrargtrial` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** an unprototyped call loses a local output pointer; a post-call word or halfword output folds to its initializer.
- **What it does:** Retain an existing register argument trial when its value is a same-width copy or constant displacement of a particular stack-pointer value. The provenance walk is bounded to 64 steps and declines phi nodes, unknown bases, width changes, and call-clobbered values. Known dead callee inputs retain their veto. Keeping the pointer lets ordinary call alias handling preserve the local object's output value.
- **When to flip:** Enable when an unprototyped call loses a local output pointer and subsequent loads incorrectly fold to the pre-call initializer. This is evidence of intent, not a declared prototype: a live stack address can also be incidental, so the option is off by default. Supply a prototype when the interface is known.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/active-input-trial-scoring · kuna · opt-in-tool · kuna-stack-address-argument
- **Example:** `option stackaddrargtrial on`

### `callarrayextent` -- on | off, default `off` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** a helper's stack output array is shorter than the helper writes; a post-call stack read is emitted as an independent uninitialized scalar; a stack array passed to a helper loses aliases with neighboring frame slots.
- **What it does:** Represent unlocked integer storage passed directly to declared integer-pointer parameters as one array when a later slot is read after being clobbered by the same call. Preserve a compatible multi-element parent that crosses or ends at the output base. Reserve through the next address-taken frame base or the local frame end, never crossing offset zero, and decline regions larger than 4096 bytes. Decline conflicting parameter types, type locks, incompatible hints, and caller-defined values in newly added storage. This preserves aliases across the call but estimates storage capacity, not the source array's exact length.
- **When to flip:** A helper writes through a stack pointer, but the caller declares a short array followed by independent uninitialized scalars for the helper's output, or splits adjacent input and output storage used by one call. Opt in only when the frame region is intended to be shared storage: caller-defined neighboring values are excluded, but a pointer prototype still does not establish the exact array length. Explicit local types remain authoritative.
- **Where / provenance:** P6/stack-frame-layout · kuna · feature · kuna-callarrayextent
- **Example:** `option callarrayextent on`

### `stackstruct` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a local passed by address to a callee is declared unsigned long and read as v1._4_2_ or v1._6_1_; byte and short fields of a local header print as partial accesses; a struct the source zero-initializes or memsets prints as several unrelated stack scalars; memcpy copies 0x40 bytes into a local declared char v13[12].
- **What it does:** Lay out an address-taken frame object that the function accesses at several offsets with different widths as one synthesized `struct_N`. A local record whose address is handed to a callee (`read(fd,&hdr,8)`) keeps no type in a stripped binary, so the frame layout makes one scalar per slot it finds: the byte and short members inside a slot print as partial accesses of an `unsigned long` (`v1._4_2_`) and the slots after the first become unrelated locals. With the option on, `restructure_varnode` recognizes the object before it merges the hints: it starts at a frame address that reaches a call as an argument with no index added; it extends over what single accesses prove belongs to it -- an access that starts inside and ends past the current end, the contiguous writes one instruction made (a vector zero store the lane split cut into words), and the byte count a buffer call states for that address (`memset`, `memcpy`, `memmove`, `memcmp`, `bzero`, `read`, `write`, `recv`, `send`, `fread`, `fwrite` and the `_chk` object size); and its members are the accesses inside that extent, an access that strictly contains another being an initializer that claims nothing. Slots that merely sit next to the object stay separate locals, and no single access joins two addresses that each reach a call at their own start: a compiler zeroes or reloads two adjacent locals with one access (an AArch64 `stp` of `xzr`). The object is a record only when at least two members of different widths remain, each naturally aligned and 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes wide, and its size is a multiple of the widest. It declines when an access crosses its start, a hint over it is type-locked, shared storage, indexed or already a composite some other evidence typed, a write stores the bytes of text (a string built in place), a wide access copies a non-constant value over its members, or a whole-object read uses the bytes as one value (a register-shared slot). A member's type is the one every access of it agrees on, else the unknown of its width (a float when an access carries one); alignment padding becomes unknown members of the widest width each offset allows and a longer gap one `undefined1[N]`. The structure is minted through the `structsynth` layout ledger and is used only when the answer is exactly the object's size; the object's hints are replaced by one fixed hint of it, and the existing member rendering prints `v1.field_0x4`, splits an initializer into member stores, and `structdefs` prints the definition. The first layout waits until type propagation has settled; later passes keep it while no access crosses its bounds. Flipping it on in default mode moves 0/675 datatest assertions and no other stage file's assertion.
- **When to flip:** ON in the `aggressive` preset (which `auto` picks under 500 KiB, and which the web decompiler uses). Shipped OFF: the structure is a layout hypothesis over a frame object, and a program-wide `struct_N` minted for one function renumbers the synthesized structures of every later function in a `decompile-all` run. Flip ON when a function reads byte or short fields out of a local it passed to a callee by address, or a local filled by `memset`/`memcpy` prints as several unrelated scalars; flip OFF to get one variable per slot back.
- **Where / provenance:** P6/stack-frame-layout · kuna · type-inference · kuna-stackstruct
- **Example:** `option stackstruct on`

### `globalarrayanchor` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** negative index displacement hides a declared global array; indexed stores use an address immediately before an array.
- **What it does:** Keep an exact mapped global array base visible when a scaled memory index carries a negative element displacement.
- **When to flip:** Enable when an indexed access is rendered with a literal address before the declared array or with a synthetic symbol instead of its declared array.
- **Where / provenance:** P3/simplification-quiescence · kuna · opt-in-tool · mapped-array-negative-index-bias
- **Example:** `option globalarrayanchor on`

### `gobounds` -- on | off, default `on` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** Go array accesses surrounded by runtime.panicIndex or runtime.panicBounds calls; Go division retains compiler-generated runtime.panicdivide branches.
- **What it does:** REMOVES CODE: fold compiler-generated Go bounds, slice, division, shift and unsafe string/slice checks. On Go images only, remove a conditional edge to a terminal block whose sole call is an exact compiler panic helper. Preserve explicit panic calls, type assertions, arms containing stores or other calls, and branches whose two successors are both panic handlers. The surviving access or arithmetic is unchanged; arguments used only by the removed check can disappear from inferred signatures.
- **When to flip:** Leave on for source-oriented Go decompilation; turn off to audit the actual checks and panic paths. Non-Go images are unchanged. Use sourcelang go for a bytechunk or image whose language metadata was removed.
- **Where / provenance:** P7/edge-virtualization · angr · opt-in-tool · angr-go-check-remover
- **Example:** `option gobounds off`

### `ppc32picimports` -- off | on | abi, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** PPC32 PIC calls retain local linker stub names; a PPC32 PIC no-return call flows into padding; PPC32 PIC imports are missing from named cross-reference queries; every import call in a PPC32 shared library linked with the start files prints as sub_.
- **What it does:** Recover PPC32 secure-PLT imports. on proves terminal calls in the selected caller without global stub names; abi additionally names stubs across compiled functions under explicit compiler and ABI assumptions.
- **When to flip:** Use on for terminal PPC32 helpers: returning paths, unknown calls and unproved writes withhold recovery. Use abi for ordinary compiler-linked libraries or PIEs only when imports preserve SysV nonvolatiles, callbacks target function entries, computed gotos stay within their function, and application code does not overwrite GOT entries or saved registers. abi walks every function and can cost 1.1-1.8x a function listing and up to 3x a single-function decompile. Entering or leaving abi requires reloading the image; the CLI loads with the selected mode. on and off can be toggled live on an image loaded without abi. Default off leaves PIC calls unresolved. BSS-PLT and absolute imports are unchanged.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · kuna · correctness-fix · PPC32 secure-PLT caller bases
- **Example:** `option ppc32picimports on`

### `rustfmt` -- off | on | all, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** Rust printing exposes std::io::stdio::_print with a pointer and odd integer; Rust print calls retain a runtime template pointer and stack formatter descriptor arrays; Rust integer or string String construction retains format_inner with an output pointer; Rust panic messages remain core::panicking::panic_fmt calls with opaque pointers; older Rust print calls retain a piece-array fmt::Arguments descriptor; Rust String or Stdout writes remain opaque core::fmt::write or write_fmt calls (set all).
- **What it does:** On a rustc-built little-endian 64-bit image, render the standard library's formatting runtime calls as the source macros that produced them. `on` recovers print!, println!, eprint! and eprintln! at the exact std::io::stdio sinks, format! at alloc::fmt::format::format_inner (the hidden String destination is kept as std::ptr::write) and panic! at a non-returning core::panicking::panic_fmt with a constant caller location, for stable Rust 1.93.0/1.93.1 templates and for the piece-array fmt::Arguments layout of x86-64 ELF images built by stable Rust 1.89.0/1.90.0 or nightly 1.89.0 bf64d66bd. Arguments are literal-only messages (format braces escaped, exactly one final newline removed for the ln macros), primitive 8/16/32/64-bit integers under exact Display, Debug, hexadecimal, octal, binary and exponent formatter identities with static width, precision, alignment, Unicode fill, sign, alternate and zero-padding specifications, and string Display arguments proven by an exact forwarding body to core::fmt::Formatter::pad and two live stack words. `all` adds write!/writeln! into a verified String writer (exact core::fmt::write, a complete immutable String fmt::Write vtable; the one-byte result is kept as is_err()) and into Stdout (exact Rust 1.93.1 x86-64 ELF writer bodies and adapter callbacks; the reference-cell or promoted-inner receiver and the owned eight-byte io::Result word are kept). `off` keeps every runtime call. Template bytes must be readonly UTF-8 and descriptor cells complete; unknown compiler builds, sinks, callbacks and writers, dynamic counts, conflicting formatter aliases and unsupported layouts stay explicit. Descriptor setup, typed reads and surrounding IR are preserved. C and Go output are unchanged.
- **When to flip:** Leave `on` (default) to read verified Rust printing, format! and panic! as source macros. Set `off` to inspect the runtime sinks, encoded fmt::Arguments templates and stack descriptor arrays. Set `all` to also recover write!/writeln! into String and Stdout writers; it is not the default for speed: the String writer's study did not clear the small-C wall-time confidence bound and the Stdout writer's did not clear the Go-control CPU and wall-time confidence bounds. The scoped fmt::Write/io::Write imports and result bridges keep the writer contracts without changing function prototypes. Recompiled panic! uses the recovered source location, not the original binary's file and line; a recovered string argument assumes valid UTF-8 storage for its recorded length. Generic reference callbacks, floating-point and pointer formatting, and custom writers are not recovered.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/literal-format · angr · opt-in-tool · angr-rust-format-macros
- **Example:** `option rustfmt all`

### `outlang` -- c | rust | go, default `c`

- **Symptoms:** Go output language is unavailable; Go functions retain C declarations and control-flow syntax.
- **What it does:** Select the C, Rust or Go output-language profile. Go renders recovered types, conversions, operator precedence, declarations and structured statements through the shared printer. Selection preserves the recovered IR and does not infer missing Go ABIs, receiver types or runtime idioms. This is the catalog alias for option setlanguage; the engine default remains C and frontend auto-selection remains independent.
- **When to flip:** Use go to inspect a function in Go syntax, including a Go binary whose source metadata is incomplete. Use c or rust to compare another spelling of the recovered function. A language selection does not prove source-language semantics that analysis has not recovered.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/output-language · angr · opt-in-tool · angr-go-output
- **Example:** `option outlang go`

### `rustprobestack` -- off | auto | always, default `off` (destructive opt-in)

- **Symptoms:** Rust large-frame functions retain __rust_probestack calls; live stack-probe R11 residual renders as an undefined local; stack-probe calls obscure a known constant frame allocation.
- **What it does:** Off in every preset because the predeclared default comparison exceeded its 5% wall-time confidence bound. Explicit auto/always summarize the verified 57-byte AMD64 Rust stack-probe helper before SSA and call recovery. Require a direct relative call, a full RAX constant of at most 16 MiB reaching it within 48 raw ops in one block, canonical call push/store p-code, and an immediate SUB RSP,RAX that kills the helper flags. Preserve the caller return-address store, saved RBP store, restored stack pointer and exact R11 residual; ordinary dead-store analysis removes unused scratch writes. Mark the saved-RBP store as a transient callee spill so P6 permits caller buffers to reuse its bytes. Require the live shared image to prove complete mapped coverage, then read it directly without disturbing loader prefetch state. Match complete helper bytes and x86-64 register storage, never the symbol name. Decline missing bytes, modified bodies, unknown frames, intervening flag use, inline/injected/nonreturning call facts and the stackviews/stackalias memory policies. Page-touch reads and their faults are intentionally abstracted. Auto applies only to Rust images; always removes the language gate; off retains the original probe.
- **When to flip:** Enable auto explicitly to summarize verified Rust compiler stack instrumentation while preserving live R11 and stack writes. Use off to audit page-touch and fault behavior; always accepts matching raw or non-Rust images with the same proof obligations.
- **Where / provenance:** P2/flow-classification · angr · structure-recovery · angr-rust-probestack
- **Example:** `option rustprobestack off`

## Analysis & loader passes

Program-prep enablement: what is discovered, decoded, and named before any function is decompiled.

### `libctypes` -- off | opaque | glibc, default `opaque`

- **Symptoms:** a function that only ever passes its argument to a libc stdio call still declares it long or unsigned long; a fopen or fdopen result is a void * that nothing can name; a stat or lstat call fills an untyped void * buffer; getopt_long takes a bare (void *)0x... long-option table; readdir returns a void * whose fields are casts and offsets; a stream parameter is void * where the ground truth is FILE *; a FILE * or stat * renders its members as field_0x8 / field_0x30 instead of _IO_read_ptr / st_size; a value loaded out of a named libc struct keeps the cast's type instead of the field's; stdin/stdout/stderr render as an untyped word and their fields as raw offsets ((long)stdout + 0x28); a shared object's stream slot has no name at all (*(long *)(*dat_3fe0 + 0x28)); two functions in one binary disagree about what stdout is, one calling it FILE * and the other a long.
- **What it does:** Spell the libc/POSIX aggregate pointers in the built-in prototype tables by NAME instead of void *: FILE *, DIR *, stat *, dirent *, passwd *, group *, tm *, option *, timespec *, timeval *, sigaction *, sigset_t *, mbstate_t *, termios *, sockaddr *, pthread_mutex_t *, obstack *, spwd *, utmpx *, utmp *, re_pattern_buffer *, lconv *, statfs *. The Ty vocabulary of those tables is width-stable, so every aggregate pointer in them is a void * today - honest about the width and silent about the pointee, which is the one thing a declaration actually knows. The retarget is enumerated slot by slot (a blanket void *->FILE * would type the va_list of vasprintf/vsnprintf/__vfprintf_chk/verr as a stream), and it brings the stdio names neither shipped table carries: __uflow, fgetc, rewind, freopen, popen, pclose, getdelim, flockfile, funlockfile. A second round of slots was mined from the benchmark corpus's own debug twins - which pointer-to-named-struct variables ground truth holds, and which libc slot each could be reached from - and adds the rest of the stream surface (fseeko, ftello, fread_unlocked, fputc_unlocked, feof_unlocked, fgets_unlocked, setbuf, vfprintf, __getdelim), the record-at-a-time and reentrant halves of the three account databases (getpwent/fgetpwent/putpwent/getpwnam_r and their group and spwd twins), more tm/timespec/termios slots, the regex entry points, localeconv and statfs/fstatfs. Two kinds of slot are left out because naming them splits the caller's frame object: the two-element timespec/timeval arrays of utimensat/futimens/utimes/futimesat, and further sigset_t slots, which a caller hands &sa.sa_mask of a struct sigaction local. Those names are new to both shipped tables, so each supplies an ARITY where there was none as well as a pointee. One table is matched against a name the image DEFINES rather than imports: the five _obstack_* entry points, which are the implementation-reserved half of obstack.h and can only be glibc's or gnulib's copy of the same file. That is what makes obstack reachable at all - gnulib links its copy in and the linker exports the symbols, so a stripped grep, tar or coreutils image carries _obstack_newchunk in .dynsym and nothing else in it says what the first argument addresses; obstack is the widest aggregate in the measured ground truth after FILE. Each named type is interned as a shell carrying its real glibc x86-64 width (FILE 216, stat 144, dirent 280, ...), never width 0 - a zero-width pointee keeps a PTRSUB alive through RulePtrsubUndo and the printer then emits the functional PTRSUB(p,0x28) form - and is left INCOMPLETE so the exported .h declares it opaque rather than as a struct with a width and no members. On an image that carries debug info the platform's own definition is used instead, fields and all: the pass runs after the DWARF importer and adopts an aggregate of the declared width already held under the name (or under glibc's _IO_FILE spelling of FILE) - complete or still being populated - and declines the signature rather than touch a name held by anything else, a different width included. The third value, `glibc`, fills in the nine aggregates whose layout the platform PUBLISHES and an application is meant to read - FILE, stat, timespec, timeval, tm, passwd, group, option, dirent - with their real x86-64 members, so an access renders under its own name (`f->_IO_read_ptr`, `st->st_size`, `opt[i].name`) instead of `f->field_0x8`, and the loaded value takes the FIELD's type rather than whatever the cast said - `st_size` is a signed long, so a wrapper that returns -1 on failure stops printing its sentinel as 0xffffffffffffffff. Every offset and width is measured with offsetof/sizeof against the installed headers, not restated from memory (docs/features/libctypes/glibc.md). Two claims the tables refuse to make: no field is spelled as a pointer to the struct being filled (_IO_FILE::_chain is void * - completing a struct re-keys it into a new Rc, so a self-pointer taken mid-completion would strand the program on two stream types), and no layout is installed unless it is TRUE of the image - x86-64 ELF whose .dynstr names glibc (the libc.so.6 soname or a GLIBC_2.x symbol version). musl, another libc and a statically linked image all keep the opaque shells, which for a static image costs nothing because these tables are matched against imported names only. The WIDTHS are a claim too, and about the caller's frame, not only about offsets inside the shell: a named pointer handed a frame object's address grows that object to the declared width, which is right on x86-64 against glibc (`char v1 [12]` becomes `termios v1` where the program touched twelve bytes of the struct `tcgetattr` fills) and on i386 folded the caller's neighbouring locals into an 8-byte timespec declared as 16 (`v1._12_4_ = a0 + 2`). So nothing at all is named - no slot, no stream symbol, no shell - unless the image is an x86-64 ELF not dynamically linked against another C library (no .dynstr, or one naming glibc); i386, ARM, AArch64, MIPS, PE and Mach-O get the shipped void * tables, byte for byte what `off` gives, and a name declared there by hand does too. A named vote is also held to what the caller does through the pointer. A libc aggregate is often the FIRST member of a larger object (grep's kwset begins with its obstack, an rsyslog instance record with its mutex), whose address is then the one the call reads; where the caller reads that argument past the aggregate's end or before its start, forms an address at or past the end, or steps it by a constant at least as large as the aggregate that is not exactly its size (coreutils wc walks &fstatus[i].st and reads `failed` 8 bytes before it), that call's vote falls back to void * (`kuna_libcfit`) and the declared type decides only the call's cast; type propagation likewise refuses to carry the named pointer onto a value read past the end, so `kwsincr` stops printing every kwset member as an element of an obstack array (`&v1[0x1b].field_0x38`). DIR, sigaction, sigset_t, mbstate_t, termios, sockaddr and pthread_mutex_t stay opaque under `glibc` too: glibc publishes no layout for DIR, and the rest are reserved words no caller reads by name. The same tables also type the stdio STREAMS themselves, which no prototype slot can reach: `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr` are storage, not an argument, so a function that never calls a typed stdio function sees only an `undefined8` word, and on a shared object the slot has no name at all. Under any enabled value the pass emits a typed DATA symbol for each stream slot, read off the DYNAMIC RELOCATION that binds it - which is also the evidence that the name is the C library's and not a global the program spells `stdout` itself. A COPY relocation names a .bss word the run-time loader fills with libc's own `FILE *stdout`, so that slot is `FILE *` under the stream's own name; a GLOB_DAT on an UNDEFINED symbol names a GOT word holding the stream's ADDRESS, so it is `FILE **` under the minted name `stdout_ptr` - calling that one `stdout` would make the emitted `*stdout_ptr` read as an indirection the program does not perform. Because `stdout_ptr` is kuna's coinage and not the image's, the GLOB_DAT arm declines when either symbol table (.symtab as much as .dynsym) already spells it, rather than printing two addresses under one identifier. Linked ELF only, under the same width gate as the rest of the table, and a spelling that occurs twice in .dynsym is declined outright. The slots point at the same `FILE` the rest of the table uses, so `opaque` gives `stdout->field_0x28` and `glibc` `stdout->_IO_write_ptr`, and an image whose own debug info holds a different `FILE` contributes no stream symbol rather than a contradictory one.
- **When to flip:** On by default (opaque): a pointer the callee's own libc declaration names carries that name - get_prefix(FILE *f) instead of sub_2f30(long a0) on a stripped -O2 coreutils reader, fopen/fdopen/popen results as FILE *, stat/lstat/fstat filling a stat *, getopt_long reading an option * table, readdir returning a dirent *, localtime a tm *, an obstack handle as obstack * even where gnulib linked the obstack code into the program. Flip OFF to ablate the table: to check whether a pointee name came from this declaration rather than from inference, when a target statically links a private function under a libc spelling that the imports-only restriction did not catch (it would then be typed against libc's aggregate, not its own), or when a decompile-project export has to stay as close to compilable as it gets - the shells are deliberately INCOMPLETE, so the exported .c reads fields out of a type its own .h declares opaque (measured +58 cc errors on an ls export - 51 of them from reading fields out of the incomplete shells, the rest from a type name that collides with a function name of its own in the exported body; the .h itself is 0 errors either way). Off is byte-identical to the shipped void * tables, because with the gate off the pass does not run and not one named shell is interned. No datatest loads a file, so the 675 assertions cannot see this row either way; the stage corpus can, and tests/stages/kuna-libctypes.xml pins it in both arms. The flip's evidence is the corpus sweep in docs/features/libctypes/record.json. Flip to `glibc` for the field NAMES: on an x86-64 ELF against glibc it installs the published layouts of FILE/stat/timespec/timeval/tm/passwd/group/option/dirent, turning `*(unsigned char **)&f->field_0x8` into `f->_IO_read_ptr` and `*(unsigned long *)&st->field_0x30` into `st->st_size`, and giving the loaded value the field's type. Prefer it when reading stdio-heavy or stat-heavy code; stay on `opaque` when a decompile-project export must not declare a type the toolchain's own headers also declare. On a target that is not x86-64 against glibc every value is inert: no slot is named at all, because the widths are not that ABI's. The default also NAMES and TYPES the stream slots: `*(long *)(stdout + 0x28)` becomes `*(long *)&stdout->field_0x28` (`stdout->_IO_write_ptr` under `glibc`), and a shared object's `*(long *)(*dat_3fe0 + 0x28)` becomes `*(long *)&(*stdout_ptr)->field_0x28`. That reach is the function that makes no typed stdio call and the shared object whose stream never had a name - over twelve whole binaries 45 lines move, 38 of them a GOT slot gaining its name, and eight of the twelve are byte-identical because inference had already typed those streams from a typed stdio call in the same function. Its cost is local merging: a slot that takes `FILE *` stops merging with the unrelated values a scalar local had absorbed, which adds a declaration and renumbers the locals after it. Naming a data object stays `datasyms`' call - with that option off the stream slot goes back to `dat_<addr>`, since the type rides on the symbol - so ablate the stream half with `datasyms off` and the whole table with `libctypes off`.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · ghidra · analysis-enablement · kuna-analysis-libctypes
- **Example:** `option libctypes off`

### `libgccsigs` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a SPARC32 caller stores the low word of a 64-bit quotient from a local nothing assigns; __divdi3 is called with four 32-bit arguments and only %o0 is read back; *p = v1; after a __divdi3 call where v1 is never written.
- **What it does:** Seed the libgcc DI-mode contract `long long __divdi3(long long, long long)` onto a SPARC32 big-endian ELF (`sparc:BE:32:default:default`) that names `__divdi3`, defined or imported. The helper's widths come from GCC machine modes, not the C data model: it takes two eight-byte operands in %o0:%o1 and %o2:%o3 and returns the eight-byte quotient in %o0:%o1, high word first. Without the contract the caller sees an unknown callee that writes only %o0, so a caller that stores only the low word (`*p = (int)(a / b);`, the `st %o1` after the call) stores a local nothing assigns. With it the call prints `__divdi3(CONCAT44(a0,a1),CONCAT44(a2,a3))` and the stored word is `(int)__divdi3(..)`. A DWARF or explicit `--assert prototype` declaration keeps precedence, a stripped image names no helper and is unchanged, and every other target and helper (`__moddi3`, `__udivdi3`, `__umoddi3`) keeps its inferred contract.
- **When to flip:** Off by default: the locked eight-byte result still costs a caller that RETURNS arithmetic on the quotient. Return recovery keeps a caller's two return words only when each is a bare slice of the call result or a literal and nothing else reads the quotient (`return a / b;`, a quotient kept across a call, a guarded `return -1`), so `return a / b + 1;` prints `int inc(..)` with only the high word, `return -(a / b);` prints `int neg(..)`, and `return f ? a / b : c;` prints `void sel(..)`, dropping both values; with the option off all three return every word (in the first-register-low join `bejoin` leaves without evidence). Of 21 authored caller shapes at clang -O2, 14 lose words that way: +1, +c, negation, abs, `>> 3`, an unsigned `>> 32`, ^c, |c, *c, a sum of two quotients, an accumulation loop, a quotient an argument replaces on one path, a clamp (`if (x > 100) x = 100;`), and the `sel` phi. Turn on for a SPARC32 binary whose callers store or pass the quotient (`*p = (int)(a / b);`, `g(a / b)`) or return it unchanged, where the off output reads an unassigned local; check any `int` or `void` caller that should return a `long long` against the disassembly.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/external-refinement · kuna · correctness-fix · pr-1252-libgcc-divdi3
- **Example:** `option libgccsigs on`

### `strings` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** string constants render as raw addresses or unnamed data instead of quoted char[N] literals; no data symbols at ascii runs in rodata; four-character commands such as quit, show, bind, or fork render as hexadecimal addresses.
- **What it does:** Run the string-literal analysis pass: detect NUL-terminated ASCII strings (minimum length 4) and plant a typelocked char[N] data symbol at each. The four-character threshold keeps command and mode literals such as quit, show, bind, fork, and dup2 visible while the separate UTF-16 arm retains Ghidra's length-5 default.
- **When to flip:** On (default) lays char[N] data at detected strings; off leaves those addresses undefined.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/code-data-partition · kuna · analysis-enablement · kuna-analysis-strings
- **Example:** `option strings off`

### `widestrings` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a wide Windows API argument renders as a one-character string literal; LoadLibraryW("n") or FindWindowW("O",0) in the emitted C; kuna strings --encoding utf16 reports a literal the decompiled C truncates to its first character; a UTF-16 string address carries no data symbol while the ascii ones do; an anti-debugging check names no DLL or window class.
- **What it does:** Scan the loaded image at 2-byte (UTF-16LE) width as well as 1-byte, and plant a typelocked wchar2[N] data symbol at each wide literal -- the allCharWidths arm of Ghidra's StringsAnalyzer that kuna's 1-byte port left as a documented seam. Read at 1-byte width a UTF-16LE literal is a ONE-CHARACTER string (`L"ntdll.dll"` is 6e 00 74 00 ..., whose first NUL closes the run after `n`), so nothing is marked up there, the constant keeps whatever char * the type lattice gave it, and the printer reads to the same NUL: every wide Windows-API argument rendered as its own first character -- LoadLibraryW("n"), FindWindowW("O",0). The widened matcher is the 1-byte MinLengthCharSequenceMatcher over 2-byte little-endian code units and nothing else: the same printable-ASCII recognizer over each unit's low byte, the same require-NUL-end rule, the same minimum length of 5, over exactly the address set the 1-byte pass scans, on even addresses only. The two widths cannot both claim a run -- a wide unit demands a zero high byte, so five consecutive 1-byte-charset bytes never occur inside a wide run -- and the 1-byte facts are committed first regardless, so the established width owns any address both could reach. With the symbol planted the existing printer path does the rest: the char type's size 2 is what emits the L prefix and reads the bytes two at a time.
- **When to flip:** On by default. A wide (UTF-16) string argument renders as a one-character literal -- LoadLibraryW("n") where the binary says L"ntdll.dll", FindWindowW("O",0) where it says L"OllyDbg - [CPU]" -- which is most of what a Windows anti-debugging or anti-VM check contains. `kuna strings --encoding utf16` already reported those literals in full while the decompiled C did not, and the difference between the two surfaces is the tell. Flip OFF to restore markup that is exactly the 1-byte pass's -- e.g. on an image whose 16-bit data tables read as plausible wide text, or to ablate this width's contribution.
- **Where / provenance:** P1/code-data-partition · ghidra-upstream · analysis-enablement · re-wide-api-string-args
- **Example:** `option widestrings off`

### `widestrings32` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a wchar_t or char32_t string literal argument renders as an address such as &dat_2004; a wide literal renders as its first character in a narrow string; L"..." appears only where a libc wide-string prototype types the argument; a wide default such as s = L"(NULL)" renders as s = &dat_2038.
- **What it does:** Plant a typelocked wchar4[N] data symbol at each 4-byte wide string literal (a wchar_t literal of an ELF or Mach-O target, or a char32_t one), so the printer renders L"hellow" where it printed the literal's address (lenw(&dat_2004)). The matcher is the 1-byte one widened to 4-byte code units read in the image's byte order on 4-aligned addresses of read-only data: each unit a printable-ASCII (or tab/CR/LF) value, closed by a zero unit. An int table of character codes is byte for byte such a literal, and one that runs on past its zero ({97,98,99,100,101,0,7,8}, a switch lookup table) would be read past it, so a run is planted only when the image backs it as a string: no sized data object of the symbol tables overlaps it (a declared array keeps its name), and either it lies in a mergeable string section of 4-byte entries (a relocatable object's .rodata.str4.4), or it holds at least five units of at least three distinct characters, something points at its start (an operand the scan found, a pointer slot of a data section, a dynamic relocation), what follows its terminator past at most alignment padding is the next literal or object, not a next element (the section end, a table use or a symbol start whose first unit is no character or opens a string, or something an operand, a data slot or a relative-offset table names that opens a string: a zero-terminated wide run or a narrow string of four characters or more), and no code adds a computed index to an address inside it (lea rcx,t then mov eax,[rcx+rax*4]). An operand inside a run nothing points at starts the literal there.
