What declines the drop there is the recovered list itself, because a register-save prologue reads every argument register the convention has and the list therefore carries the one the drop would take. A callee that was never decompiled first states nothing, which makes the rule inert on a single-function kuna decompile, a narrowed decompile-all, a --jobs N run and under --option protoorder off. The callee's BODY is read twice more, and both are required. A bounded entry walk that positively sees those bytes READ before they are written declines the drop (the proves_input half of the per-image entry-liveness summary calleedeadarg builds), and it is what answers for a callee kuna never recovered as variadic -- u-boot's printf is called from 1,924 sites and its va_list prologue speaks for all of them. And the callee must not be able to FORWARD the register to a read no recovery saw. The entry walk ends every path at the callee's first call, so what the register meets past one is asked of that call's TARGET: a declared, non-variadic prototype answers it, and so does the target's own body with the same question put to it recursively; everywhere else -- an indirect call or tail call, a CALLOTHER, an indexed register-file access, an undecodable instruction, a recursive component, an import whose PLT stub jumps through its GOT slot -- the register has to be written already. Naming a target is not accounting for it. That second reading is what a prototype cannot give: `long fwd(struct box *o,long a,long b) { if (!a) return 0; return o->fn(o,a,b); }` compiles under gcc -O2 to `test %rsi,%rsi; je; jmp *(%rdi)`, and `long wrap(void *o,long a,long b) { if (!a) return 0; return ext3(o,a,b); }` with ext3 an unsignatured import has no pointer at all; both recover exactly the TWO parameters a drop would leave behind and forward the third to a function no recovery read. Neither reading can admit a drop, only refuse one. The trial must be TRAILING, so the list keeps its positional shape and no other argument moves. At least one argument must remain, since an empty list is calleearityfwd's failure shape. And no already-final call to the same callee entry in this function may have passed an argument in that storage -- the subtractive twin of calleearity's witness rule, which is also what orders this pass against the additive arity family: it runs immediately after calleearity in buildInputFromTrials, and a slot the sibling rule promoted outranks the clobber evidence. The drop is markNoUse, which calleearitylive/fwd/body all read as definitely-not-used, so none of them puts the argument back. Dropping the argument also NARROWS THE PRECEDING CALL'S RETURN VALUE where that call was the register's only writer: the `SUB168(v,8)` that extracted the rdx half of a 16-byte return loses its only reader and goes with the argument. No drop in the 770-binary corpus does that under this rule -- the one that did, bash expand_prompt's `xrealloc`, is declined now that the import its callee reaches has to answer for rdx -- but docs/features/argclobber/ce-forward-thunk-2param.c shows it happening the moment the rule is wrong, and it is the same mechanism that would delete a real struct half at a callee whose own prototype is under-recovered.
- **When to flip:** On by default -- but only where a callee was decompiled BEFORE its caller, because the evidence the drop needs is the callee's own recovered prototype and `protoorder` is what parks it. A serial whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` is that surface. A single-function `kuna decompile` (it forks one `decomp_dbg` per function), a run narrowed by `--addr` or `--functions`, `--jobs N`, `decompile-project`, `decompile-graph` and `--option protoorder off` all state nothing, and there the option is inert: a serial run and a `--jobs` run of the same binary can therefore differ by exactly these dropped arguments. The tell it fixes is a call that renders with one more argument than the callee takes, where that last argument is a local nothing ever assigns -- a `// rdx` (or other caller-saved register) declaration with no write anywhere in the function, read only at that one call, with sibling calls to the same callee passing fewer. Measured over the 770 stripped ELFs of decbench `full_run_address_2026-09-11` (O0, O2 and O2-noinline; no run exited non-zero), 19 functions change, one per binary, and each loses exactly one trailing argument at exactly one call site. Every one lands on the callee's TRUE arity, checked against the unstripped twin: `__addvsi3(int,int)` and `__mulvsi3(int,int)` from libgcc at 15 of them, `fmt(FILE *, char const *)` at the two coreutils `fmt` mains, `ext2fs_dblist_sort2(dblist, sortfunc)` at `e2fsck_pass2`, and `efi_create_handle(efi_handle_t *)` at u-boot. The two `fmt` mains also GAIN the second argument at their under-recovered sibling site, so all three calls render `sub_3700(stdin,...)` with two. Twenty register-storage locals disappear and none appears; 34 declarations go net. Hunks outside the argument itself: the dead remainder that fed it and its copies, declarations reordering once one is gone, one folded single-use divisor, and a `while` re-rendered as a `for` (the 11 O0 openssh `permute_args`, whose dead loop-tail copy went with the argument). Over the 444-slice campaign corpus (10,748 scored functions) `type_match` does not move at all: 1,147 perfect in both arms, aggregate identical, 0 improved and 0 worse, and the decompiled-variable count decbench scores is the same for every one of the 10,748 -- the metric cannot see this change, because register locals are never exported and a call's argument is not a variable of the caller. Flip to `off` if a call LOSES an argument the callee really consumes. The one shape that can still do that is a callee whose own parameter list kuna UNDER-recovers by exactly one slot, at exactly the register the clobber wrote, with every other argument still accounted for; the eight programs in `docs/features/argclobber/` are the classes this rule declines, and the forwarding ones among them are declined for different reasons -- `ce-forward-thunk.s` recovers one parameter where two arguments would remain, so the prototype accounting refuses it, while `ce-forward-thunk-2param.c` (through a pointer), `ce-import-forward.c` (through an unsignatured import, no pointer anywhere) and `ce-forward-thunk-2frame.c` (an ordinary direct call in front of the first) each recover exactly the two that would remain and are refused only because `rdx` is unwritten where the callee forwards it and the target cannot answer for it. Note that `protoorder` does NOT decline a variadic callee -- its variadic guards live in the `lock` mode and the declared-`...` decline cannot fire on a stripped image -- so a stripped SysV variadic is stated; what declines the drop there is that its register-save prologue reads every argument register, leaving the recovered list carrying the one the drop would take.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/active-input-trial-scoring · ghidra · correctness-fix · typecampaign-phantom-argument
- **Example:** `option argclobber on`

### `passthrough` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a wrapper renders void f(void) { g(); } although g takes an argument in the same output; a call renders with no arguments while the callee's declaration in the same file takes one; a tail-call thunk returns void while the function it jumps to returns a value; decompiling the caller shows a parameter-less function whose only instruction is a jmp to a function with parameters; DWARF gives a forwarding function a parameter kuna does not.
- **What it does:** Give a function the parameter it forwards untouched to a callee that reads it, and the return value of a tail call it hands straight back. A call's argument trials come from Heritage::guardCalls (heritage.cc:1444), which registers one per HERITAGED storage range, and a range is heritaged only when some op of the function reads or writes it: a register the function only forwards is named by no op, so the call gets no trial, no argument, and the function's own input never gets a reader or a parameter. gzip -O2 gzip_base_name is `endbr64; jmp last_component` and kuna printed `void sub_d290(void) { sub_dfd0(); }` while recovering the callee as `char *sub_dfd0(char *a0)` in the same run. Where the register IS heritaged, AncestorRealistic::execute (funcdata_varnode.cc:2159) refuses an input Varnode at the call slot outright. The evidence this option acts on is the callee's own RECOVERED prototype, which `protoorder` states for every callee a whole-binary decompile-all decompiled first: a register is an argument when that prototype has a parameter starting at it, the list is one protoorder's locking mode would accept as an arity claim (the callee's body does not read the next argument register -- a variadic's register-save prologue does -- the list does not saturate the register file, and it sits where the convention puts those types), the callee's body takes the register (its bounded entry decode reads it before writing it, or its statement records it handed on to a declared parameter or to a callee that takes it, or -- where that decode cannot finish -- its first heritage saw it read; a list that is not an arity claim qualifies when every register it names is taken that way), and the value at the call is the function's own incoming register. A function calling itself asks its own body, so a recursive call keeps the register it forwards (grep treenext) even in a single-function decompile. The width is the one the callee's body consumes (`edi` for an int). The rule only adds: every other rule (upstream scoring, then the calleearityfwd, calleearitylive and calleearitybody rescues) settles the call's list first, and at the end of ActionActiveParam a list that is a leading run of the stated one gains the stated registers that follow it, up to the first the function does not forward; an argument supplied while scoring would turn off the sibling rescue that completes tar sysinttostr's first tail call. For a register no op of the function touches, ActionFuncLink gives a call no other call can precede a read of it and a trial; heritage registers the visible range at every other call as usual and keeps only the function's own RETURN off it; and every trial on the range is scored inactive -- where the option-off run's hole-filling trial starts -- never definitely-not-used, which would make forceNoUse drop every later argument (gcc -O2 `noop(); twoarg(p,3)`). When every live RETURN is reached from a direct call with nothing in between, every such callee states a non-void return in the same register or register pair (x86-64 rdx:rax, i386 edx:eax, ARM r1:r0; a callee with no parameters states its return too), and the function never touches those registers, the RETURN reads them and the tail call's result is the function's return value, typed by the callee's recovered return type. A register that carries no argument (x86 eax, MIPS v0) may be written before the call, which overwrites it, as long as nothing between the call and the RETURN reads or writes it; an argument register that is also the return register (ARM r0) may not, since `mov r0,#5; b g` is how a void function calls g(5). The `r0 = r0` (MIPS `v0 = v0`) the ARM and MIPS specs inject as the mode switch of every `bx lr`, `pop {...,pc}` and `jr ra` is not a touch, nor the vector-count access that marks a SysV variadic function or call, so `bl f; pop {r4,pc}`, `jal f; ...; jr ra` and a MIPS `jr $t9` tail call qualify as x86-64 `call f; ret` does; a returned register the body touches itself keeps its call-site argument trials scored as with the option off, so `bl g; bl f; pop {r4,pc}` still passes g's result to f. A pair is kept whole or not at all: a register the call's model does not kill (xmm1 of a struct {double,double} on x86-64 gcc) is not the call's result at the RETURN, and keeping xmm0 alone would return half the value as an integer. And the claim yields to a return value the function computes itself in another storage class: `float f(int x,float y){ g(x); return y*2.0f; }` leaves g's result untouched in r0 (x86-64 rax, MIPS v0) and its own in s0 (xmm0, $f0), and returns the float, as with the option off; a value of the same class (the r1 of `bl g; mov r1,#0`) and a value that is zero at every RETURN (what -fzero-call-used-regs leaves in every call-used register a forwarder does not return in) keep the claim. A callee states a return only where its own body computed one in every byte and on every path: gnulib's `void version_etc_arn` ends its fallthrough on a `__fprintf_chk` and keeps that call's RAX clobber, so kuna recovers it as returning `long`, and without that gate every `version_etc_ar` wrapper inherited the same wrong return (212 of 4,267 gained returns across 444 decbench slices; 6 of 4,088 with the gate). A callee that stated nothing (single-function decompile, a narrowed or sharded run, an import, protoorder off, and under `protoorder types` a callee in a recursive component) changes nothing, the function's call of itself aside. Two refusals keep a caller off a parameter the callee's own recovery invented. A stated parameter whose value, through value-preserving operations, only reaches an argument slot of a variadic call -- one the callee set up as variadic, or a declared `...` prototype past its named parameters -- is never claimed: openssh xcalloc's third parameter is gcc's `push %rdx` stack-alignment filler at a call to sshfatal, gnulib open_safer's is `open`'s mode, and the ABI lets a caller leave that register unset. And a claim the positional list can only reach across a register this function writes before reading is declined, because that register would become a parameter nothing sets: the protoorder fixture's overrec sets rsi to 16 and forwards rdx, and rendered `void overrec(unsigned long *a0,unsigned long a1,long a2)` with a1 in no statement against the call site `overrec(v1)`.
- **When to flip:** On by default. Over 574 slices in 25 projects -- the 444-slice decbench corpus AND 130 slices of 17 projects disjoint from it (openssh, e2fsprogs, dpkg, kmod, dash, iproute2, gnutls, zlib, ...) -- 4,107 of 4,346 gained parameters are confirmed by the unstripped twin's DWARF prototype, NONE are contradicted, and the remaining 239 belong to forwarding thunks DWARF does not describe at all; no function and no call site loses an argument (docs/features/passthrough/dwarf-confirmation.md). The return arm is a judgement, not a proof, and is where ON costs something: a source-`void` wrapper that tail-calls a value-returning function compiles to the same `jmp` as a wrapper that returns what it calls, so 5,458 of 5,615 gained returns are DWARF-confirmed and 157 are contradicted -- 6 on the decbench corpus but 151 on the disjoint one, concentrated in projects that write many one-line `void` wrappers (e2fsprogs bitmap accessors, openssh blf_key). A return in a register pair is taken on the same terms, so it shares both limits the bytes cannot resolve: a wrapper repeats a pair its callee's own recovery invented (coreutils strintcmp becomes `undefined16` because numcompare is), and a wrapper that truncates the pair (`return (int)wide(a,b);`) compiles to the same `jmp` and is given the whole pair. On ARM and MIPS the return arm also takes a wrapper that calls and then returns (`bl f; pop {r4,pc}`, `jal f; ...; jr ra`): over 92 debug-stripped ARM firmware binaries (decbench O0, O2 and O2-noinline) 223 functions gain a return that way: 182 DWARF-confirmed, 39 DWARF `void` and 2 with no DWARF entry (82.4% of those DWARF describes); betaflight (49 of 74) and cleanflight (28 of 34) are -Og builds, where no sibling call turns a one-line `void` wrapper into a tail `b f`, and without them it is 105 of 113 (92.9%), against 157 of 164 (95.7%) for tail-jump returns on the same set. No MIPS corpus with DWARF was measured. It acts only where a callee was decompiled BEFORE its caller (serial `decompile-all`, `decompile-project`); a single-function `kuna decompile`, a run narrowed by `--addr` or `--functions`, `--jobs N` and `--option protoorder off` leave every call but a function's call of itself alone, and no argument moves at -O0, where the register is already named by an op (an x86 -O0 wrapper that loads its arguments through rax before `call f; leave; ret` does gain f's return). Reading the callee's body where its entry decode stops (a call, a large body) and a function's calls of itself adds 222 call arguments over 14 binaries (x86-64 gcc -O2/-O0 and clang, Cortex-M firmware, an ARM library); of the 167 whose callee has a DWARF prototype, 156 match it and the other 11 are register-level arguments DWARF does not count (a hidden struct-return pointer, a 64-bit integer in two registers, libgcc's assembly soft-float compares). Set OFF to get upstream's reading back: an input register at a call is not an argument unless the caller moved a value into it, and a tail call's result is not the caller's return value.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/active-input-trial-scoring · ghidra · correctness-fix · typecampaign-passthrough-arity
- **Example:** `option passthrough on`

### `mixedtailret` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** a function that returns a value on one path and tail-calls a function on the other is printed void; if (6 <= *a0) return; getv(); // tail-call where the source returns *a0 on that path; a function returns xmm0 although its callee and its other path return an int in eax; the return value a function tests before returning it is lost beside a tail call.
- **What it does:** Return the value a function tested to choose between returning it and tail-calling a value-returning function. `int keep(int *p) { int x = *p; if (x > 5) return x; return getv(); }` compiles to `mov (%rdi),%eax; cmp $5,%eax; jle L; ret; L: jmp getv` (clang -O2), and kuna prints `void keep(int *a0)` and drops the value: the `ret` path's eax is also compared, so upstream's ancestorOpUse (funcdata_varnode.cc) refuses it as a return value, and passthrough's tail-call arm takes a tail call's result only when EVERY live RETURN hands one back. With the option on, when at least one RETURN hands back a call whose callee's recovered prototype (protoorder, decompile-all) returns a value in one register, a RETURN reached from no call is taken as returning that register too when, read from the raw p-code before the first heritage: the function itself wrote the register last on every path into the RETURN, no wider than the callee states it (no call in between, no path from the entry that leaves the incoming register); the nearest conditional branch above the RETURN on its single-predecessor chain whose other side reaches the claimed tail call tests that value, in the register or in the one it was copied from (gcc's `cmp $5,%edi; jg L; jmp getk; L: mov %edi,%eax; ret`), and the RETURN is not on the side where that test found it equal to a constant (read for x86 `test`/`cmp $K` with je/jne, also on a 32-bit register copy, a sete/setne byte tested with `test`, and AArch64 cbz/cbnz and `cmp w0,#K` with b.eq/b.ne); and from where it is computed the value only decides branches, moves between registers and reaches the claimed tail calls -- no load or store through it, no store of it, no arithmetic kept in a register, no other call while it sits in an argument register. Where the return register also passes the first argument (ARM, AArch64, RISC-V, PowerPC) the claimed callee must take no parameter there. The claim then runs as passthrough's tail claim does, except that it does not yield to a value of another storage class (the xmm0 gcc's -fzero-call-used-regs scrub zeroes before one ret and a tail callee leaves alone before the other). Off by default because the bytes cannot tell the function that returns the value from a void guard that leaves it in the return register: clang's ARM `ldr r0,[r0]; cmp r0,#5; bxgt lr; b work` is both `void thr(int *p) { if (*p > 5) return; work(); }` and `int keep(..)`.
- **When to flip:** Off by default. Set it ON for a function printed `void` (or with a bare `return;` on one path) beside a `return f(..); // tail-call` on another, when you know the function returns a value: its callers read the return register after calling it (look at them, or at `kuna xrefs --to`), its name or the source says so, or DWARF from another build does. It acts only in decompile-all, where protoorder states each callee's recovered return before its callers; a single-function `kuna decompile` states nothing and leaves the function as before. Known misfires with it on, all functions that are void in the source and leave the value they tested in the return register, which then get a return value they do not have (the value printed is the one the register holds, so no value is wrong, but the return type is made up): lazy initializers (`if (inited) return; init();`), reference-count puts and once-guards whose tested counter or flag stays in eax, range checks that return early on a value they loaded, and on ARM and PowerPC any `void` guard of the `if (*p > 5) return; work();` shape. In a test file of 18 such void guards, 9 gain a return, 37 times over their gcc and clang -O1, -O2, -O3 and -Os builds. A void guard whose equality test kuna does not read as one gets `return 7;` or `return 0;`: a truth byte compared with `cmp` (`sete %dl; cmpb $1,%dl; je`), a value tested after movzbl/movsbl, a constant held in a register (`movl $7,%ecx; cmpl %ecx,%eax`), and PowerPC condition-register tests. Over 54 decbench x86-64 binaries (O2, O2-noinline, O0), 10 ARM firmware images and 813 objects clang -O2 -g builds for AArch64, ARM, RISC-V, MIPS, i386 and PPC64LE, decompile-all with the option on changes no function, so on real code it neither helps nor hurts there; it fixes the shape of #881.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/output-prototype · kuna · correctness-fix · gh-881
- **Example:** `option mixedtailret on`

### `calloverlap` -- auto | off | in | full, default `auto`

- **Symptoms:** call emitted with no arguments or fewer arguments than the disassembly passes; call result read from a local that is never assigned; enclosing function loses its own parameter list and return type (void f(void)); argument register written whole-width by pxor movdqa movdqu por pand orpd or movq before the call; second call binds a stale pre-call value where the first call should have defined it.
- **What it does:** Recover ABI argument and result slots contained within wider dataflow register ranges. Auto applies both guards only to a named eight-byte register containing one named, low four-byte general ABI slot on a truncated 32-bit address target, such as an e500 GPR. The surrounding bytes remain separate and call-clobbered. Other registers and address spaces retain legacy behavior. In enables the input guard for all contained slots; full also enables the output guard. Complete multi-slot general-register partitions are registered at every level. Off disables these partial-range guards.
- **When to flip:** Leave auto for scalar calls on e500 and equivalent narrow-ABI register models. Use full to investigate missing floating-point arguments or results in wider registers. Full can expose mixed integer/float argument-ordering and vector-lane rendering limitations, so those broad guards remain opt-in. In is for isolating argument recovery and can leave a call result unresolved. Off reproduces the previous partial-range behavior.
- **Where / provenance:** P3/call-guard · ghidra-upstream · correctness-fix · GH-275
- **Example:** `option calloverlap full`

### `indexaliasguard` -- off | load | global | full, default `global`

- **Symptoms:** stack array declared and read but never initialised in the emitted C; a run of direct frame stores vanishes when the same slots are later read through a pointer; constants loaded from .rdata into a local buffer do not appear in the decompilation; accumulator or key schedule buffer looks uninitialised before an XOR loop walks it; value stored through a pointer does not appear to reach the frame slot it aliases; a global read back after a store through a pointer prints the value stored before that store; a global read before a store through a pointer is printed after it; a store to a global before a pointer load is missing when the global is stored again later; a loop that bumps a global around a pointer load prints with no store to the global.
- **What it does:** Restore the index-alias arm of upstream Heritage::guard (heritage.cc:1194), which kuna shipped stubbed out behind a hard-coded `highPtrPossible == false`. Where a pointer can reach the range being heritaged, upstream adds two kinds of guard op, and this option selects how much of them runs. `load` runs Heritage::guardLoads (heritage.cc:1570): an addrforce CPUI_COPY read of the range in front of every indexed-stack LOAD whose discovered guard range covers it, so a slot that is only ever READ through a computed pointer still has a reader at the point the pointer is dereferenced. The COPY is artificial -- Heritage::handleNewLoadCopies propagates it away once heritage has finished, keeping only the addrforce marks it earned. `global` (the default) adds the global half of Heritage::guardStores (heritage.cc:1538): an indirect_store CPUI_INDIRECT on a global range in front of every STORE into the global's own space, skipping a read-only range and a STORE through the stack pointer, and stopping once a function has 1024 of them (a range past that point keeps the `load` output), and RulePropagateCopy does not move a stored value into one of these INDIRECTs, so the global's store stays where the binary makes it. Without it a pointer STORE has no effect on a global, so a load of the global after `gi = a; *p = k;` prints `a`, and a value read from the global before such a STORE and used after it prints as a read of the global after it. `global` also adds the LOAD guard for a global, which upstream never builds: an addrforce CPUI_COPY read of a persistent, writable range written at least twice in front of every LOAD from its space that may read it (not a constant address outside the range, not the stack pointer or an x86 segment base plus a constant), so a store to a global that a pointer load may read is kept when the global is stored again after the load; RulePropagateCopy and RuleMultiCollapse leave such a kept store's joins alone so it prints once, and ActionMarkImplied keeps a LOAD explicit when its value is live across a store to a global in its space, so the load prints ahead of the store as the binary makes it. `full` adds the INDIRECT in front of every STORE that can reach any range, the stack included, which is what upstream always does; on a frame slot its INDIRECT chain survives into the output as write-backs of values the slot already held. `off` is the pre-port state: neither arm runs, so a frame slot written by a direct `MOV [ESP+k],REG` and read only through a `LEA`-derived pointer has no reader at all and ActionDeadCode deletes the store. kuna::highPtrPossible is the upstream inline (architecture.hh:408) minus the cspec <nohighptr> range list, which only the PIC families set.
- **When to flip:** `global` by default (DIV-147 restored `load`; `global` moves 0/675 datatest assertions). The `load` symptom is a global read back after a store through a pointer that may point at it, printed as the value stored before that store (`gi = a0; *a1 = a2; return a0 >> 4;` where the binary reloads `gi` after `*a1 = a2`), or a global read before such a store printed after it (`*a0 = a1; return gi;` where the binary returns what it read first). The `off` symptom is an array that is used before it is set: a stack buffer initialised by a run of direct frame stores, then walked by a pointer loop, prints with its declaration and all of its reads but none of its initialisation -- the analyst sees `unsigned int v11 [4];` followed by `*v6 = *v6 ^ ...` and concludes the buffer starts as garbage, when the binary loaded four constants into it. The `load` symptom is also a store to a global that vanishes when the global is stored again after a load through a pointer: `gi = gi + 1; s += *p; gi = gi - 1;` in a loop prints with no store to gi, and `gi = a; x = *p; gi = b; return x;` prints `gi = a2; return *a1;`. Flip `load` to reproduce kuna's output before the global guards, `off` to reproduce kuna's pre-indexaliasguard output or to bisect whether a new addrforce mark on a frame slot came from the load arm. Flip `full` to reproduce upstream Ghidra exactly, or when a value written through a pointer looks like it is not reaching the frame slot it aliases; expect noisier output (measured +5 lines on the 1.9% of functions the arm touches at all).
- **Where / provenance:** P3/heritage-guard · ghidra-upstream · correctness-fix · re-quadratic-transform-loses-four
- **Example:** `option indexaliasguard full`

### `namestyle` -- angr | ghidra, default `angr`

- **Symptoms:** iVar1/uVar2/param_1 ghidra-style names wanted instead of v1/a1 (set ghidra); v-numbered locals and sub_/dat_/label_ names in the default output; byte-for-byte comparison against upstream ghidra naming.
- **What it does:** Master default-name scheme: angr-style (locals vN, args aN, global data dat_<addr>, unnamed functions sub_<addr>, labels label_<addr>, plus a // rax / // stack - 0x10 source-location comment per local) vs upstream Ghidra (iVar/uVar/pcVar, param_N, <type>Ram<addr>, func_, code_).
- **When to flip:** Set to ghidra to reproduce upstream Ghidra naming byte-for-byte; angr (default) makes default output read like the angr decompiler.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/naming-policy · angr · presentation-default · angr-naming
- **Example:** `option namestyle ghidra`

### `realtypes` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** undefined8/xunknownN placeholder types wanted for upstream comparison (flip off); size-guessed unsigned long/int/char types shown for values the inference never typed.
- **What it does:** Render residual TYPE_UNKNOWN (xunknownN) values as real C types by size — 1->char, 2/4/8->unsigned short/int/long (conservative on sign), pointer-to-unknown->void * — instead of the xunknownN/undefined<N> placeholder.
- **When to flip:** On (default) emits real C types for un-inferred values; off restores the upstream xunknownN/undefined<N> rendering for byte-for-byte comparison.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/literal-format · kuna · presentation-default · kuna-realtypes
- **Example:** `option realtypes off`

### `voidtailreturn` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a void function ends with a redundant return; the source does not have; GED counts one extra exit node against an otherwise perfect function; the last statement of a void function is a bare return.
- **What it does:** Elide the trailing bare `return;` of a void function -- the statement the C source it was compiled from does not have, because the source falls off the end of the body. kuna (faithfully to Ghidra) always prints the function's final RETURN, so a void function ends `... }` newline `return;` newline `}`. Four conditions must all hold, checked once per function in `elidable_void_tail_return`: the prototype returns void (a `return <value>;` is never redundant); the op is the tail of the LAST structured leaf, found by descending only the containers that print no construct of their own (Graph/Ls) so a return nested inside an if/loop/switch arm is never touched; that leaf is not an unstructured goto target (bash `rl_echo_signal_char` prints `label_115e79:` directly above its trailing `return;`, and eliding it would leave a label with no statement -- invalid C); and exactly one structured leaf carries that RETURN op, because `returndup`/`gotoreduce` clone a shared epilogue by ALIASING one op across several leaves, so suppressing by identity would also delete genuine mid-body early returns. A BlockCopy mirror is resolved through to the bblocks block it stands for, which is the normal shape of a structured function's trailing block.
- **When to flip:** On by default (DIV-98): a void function no longer ends with the bare `return;` its source does not have. Flip OFF to restore upstream Ghidra's trailing `return;`, for example when diffing against Ghidra output or reading code whose source ends a void function with an explicit `return;` (the 62 regressions below are that shape); the XML datatest and stage scripts that pin the upstream rendering set it off. Measured bidirectionally over the whole O0 decbench slice (32,329 functions / 265 slices, `scripts.decbench.optsweep`): GED-perfect 15,308 -> 15,933 (**+625** for the option in isolation), 687 moved TO perfect against 62 moved OFF (11.08 : 1, McNemar z = +22.84) -- +439 of it on binaries under 500 KiB, where the `aggressive` preset already turned it on, and +186 on binaries >= 500 KiB, which only the default reaches, aggregate GED 259,329 -> 253,985, improved 1,561 / worsened 186, and EVERY architecture net-positive (x86-64 +282, ARM +338, PE-x86 +5) with no net-negative project. Controls: 21,478 unchanged bodies score identically, 0 slug-only diffs, baseline arm agrees with the tree's published verdict on 31,584/32,329. Speed +0.17% (coreutils/ls O0, interleaved min-of-5). The 62 regressions are the shape where the SOURCE itself ends with an explicit `return;` (concentrated in betaflight 24 / cleanflight 21 register-poke helpers), which the binary cannot distinguish. The measured motivation is structural: pyjoern merges FUNCTION_END into its predecessor only when that predecessor's sole successor is FUNCTION_END, so when a function's tail is an `if` or a loop the source CFG has NO node there -- and kuna's printed `return;` re-materialises one (+1 node, +1..2 edges, and an is_exitpoint role flip that alone breaks GED's isomorphism test). 68 of the 250 decbench sample-set outputs carry exactly one bare trailing `return;`.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/brace-form · kuna · presentation-default · kuna-voidtailreturn
- **Example:** `option voidtailreturn off`

### `importdata` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a data import read through __got renders *dat_<slot>; __stack_chk_guard shows as a dereferenced dat_ address; imported globals are anonymous even though their GOT slot is named; an ELF shared object reads stdout or environ as *dat_<slot> or *stdout_ptr.
- **What it does:** Render a data read through a loader-marked import slot as the import itself. A data import (Mach-O __got / __auth_got, a dyld-cache coalesced GOT slot, a PE IAT entry) is reached through a slot the dynamic loader fills with the import's address: `ldr x8,[slot]; ldr w8,[x8]`. The slot is already named for the import and painted `externref` (peimportcall), which is what lets ActionDeindirect resolve a CALL through it to the import; a DATA read is not a call, so it printed as a dereference of the anonymous slot, `*dat_<slot>`. On: a LOAD whose pointer is such a slot renders as the import (`imported_counter`, `__stack_chk_guard`), resolved exactly as ActionDeindirect resolves a call through the same slot (query_function on the externref persist address). Calls are unaffected (deindirect consumes them first), and a read through anything that is not an externref import slot is untouched. Needs the slot painted externref: on PE/Mach-O that is peimportcall, and on ELF the elfgotimports pass, committed under this same gate, which names each GLOB_DAT GOT slot of an undefined symbol (x86-64, AArch64, i386, ARM) for its import and paints it externref. On ELF that painting also lets ActionDeindirect bind a call through such a slot (`(*dat_e9f30)()` becomes `__cxa_finalize()`), the binding peimportcall gives PE and Mach-O. A GLOB_DAT slot of a symbol the image defines is never painted: dynrelocs already folds it to the object (`exported_value`, `&exported_value`).
- **When to flip:** On by default: a data read through a GOT/IAT import slot names the import -- the stack-protector guard, XPC type objects, global counters -- so `if (*dat_1041cc6c8 == ...)` reads `if (__stack_chk_guard == ...)`, and on an ELF shared object `return *dat_3fe8;` reads `return imported_counter;` and `*stdout_ptr` reads `stdout`. Flip off to keep the slot dereference `*dat_<slot>`, for example to see which slot a read goes through or to diff against Ghidra output.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/naming-policy · kuna · presentation-default · kuna-importdata
- **Example:** `option importdata off`

### `castimplied` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a libc argument is cast to the very type the parameter declares, memchr(v10,(int)v4,n); a widening cast assigned to a variable already declared that type, v2 = (long)v1; with long v2; return (unsigned long)v1; from a function declared unsigned long; several casts stacked over one byte, (long)(int)(unsigned int)(unsigned char)c; kuna prints more casts than IDA on the same function.
- **What it does:** Leave out a cast that C's own conversion rules already perform on exactly those types. `CastStrategyC::isExtensionCastImplied` (cast.cc:249) hides an extension only when integer arithmetic or a comparison against an explicit operand of the same metatype reads it, and returns false for every other reader, so kuna prints `memchr(v10,(int)v4,n)` where `memchr` takes an `int`, `v2 = (long)v1;` into a `long`, `return (unsigned long)v1;` from a function declared `unsigned long`, and `(long)(int)(unsigned int)(unsigned char)c` for one byte widened to 64 bits. C converts an argument to its parameter's type when a prototype is in scope (C11 6.5.2.2p7), the right operand of `=` to the type of the left (6.5.16.1p2), and a returned value to the return type (6.8.6.4p3), and an integer conversion depends only on the value it converts (6.3.1.3). When on, `kuna_castimplied` decides at print time -- the IR is not changed -- which integer conversions (`CPUI_CAST` between integer types, `INT_SEXT`/`INT_ZEXT` printed as a cast) can go. A conversion BELOW another integer conversion that fixes the result type goes when it preserves its operand's value, judged on the operand's printed C type (a declared variable, a cast that stays, a truncation printed as a cast, a load through a pointer printed `T *`); an operand whose C type the text does not state (arithmetic, which C promotes; a constant; a call) never lets it go, and a sign change or a narrowing always stays. The TOP of a chain goes when it is an identity (its operand already has that C type), or when it is a value-preserving widening that flows straight into a direct call's argument whose parameter type is type-locked (a declared or measured prototype -- never a trial, never a varargs position, never a per-call-site override such as a resolved format string, never an argument `truncarg` narrowed), into the right side of a `lhs = e;` statement whose local or parameter is declared with exactly that spelling (not an arm of `c ? a : b`, whose type is the arms' common type), or into `return` from a function declared with exactly that spelling. Implied `COPY`s print as their operand and are looked through. Float conversions, pointer conversions, conversions to `bool`, enums, truncations, `truncarg`'s argument casts and `boolbyte`'s `(bool)(unsigned char)` are never touched. C output only; Rust has no implicit integer conversions.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a cast C would perform by itself is left out -- `strchr(s,c)` rather than `strchr(s,(int)c)`, `v3 = v5;` into a `long v3` rather than `v3 = (long)v5;`, `return v1;` from an `unsigned long` function, and one cast rather than four over a byte widened to 64 bits. Set it off to see every conversion ActionSetCasts inserted, exactly as upstream Ghidra prints them, for example when checking which conversions the binary performs at a call or an assignment.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/cast-policy · ida · presentation-default · kuna-castimplied
- **Example:** `option castimplied on`

### `declorder` -- natural | name, default `natural`

- **Symptoms:** v10 and v11 declared between v1 and v2; local declarations in string order v1, v10, v11, v2; a numbered local hard to find among ten or more declarations.
- **What it does:** Declare a function's locals in natural number order: `v1, v2, ..., v9, v10, v11` instead of the string order `v1, v10, v11, v2, ..., v9`. The declaration pass sorts its locals by name, and a plain string sort puts every two-digit name between `v1` and `v2`, so a function with ten or more locals scatters its numbered declarations and a reader looking up `v2` scans past `v10`..`v19` first. `natural` compares the ASCII digit runs inside two names by numeric value and everything else character by character, with plain string order as the tiebreak, so the order is total and agrees with name equality. Only the printed order moves: the symbol, rendered-line and group collapses and the repeated-name suffixes still run over the name-sorted list, and `kuna_declorder` reorders the surviving declarations once their final spellings are known. It applies to angr-style names (the default `namestyle`); Ghidra-style names carry hexadecimal offsets (`local_1c`) that a decimal comparison would scramble, so `namestyle ghidra` keeps the string order. Over 8 stripped decbench binaries (O2 gzip, dash, find, ls, grep; O2-noinline kmod; O0 bzip2, sort) under `--mode aggressive`, 291 of 3,225 functions change, every one only in the order of its declaration lines; 0/675 datatest assertions move.
- **When to flip:** On by default: locals declare as `v1, v2, ..., v10`, the order IDA declares its numbered locals in. Set it to `name` for the plain string order (`v1, v10, v11, v2`) the declaration pass used before.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/naming-policy · ida · presentation-default · kuna-declorder
- **Example:** `option declorder name`

### `libcnames` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a local holding open()'s result named v1; read's byte count kept as a vN; a buffer length from strlen named vN; a local passed to a libc function keeps a vN name; kuna names fewer locals than IDA on libc-heavy code.
- **What it does:** Give a numbered local the name the C library gives it, as a second name for its number. The built-in libc tables (`libproto`, `libcsigs`, `libctypes`) carry glibc's declared parameter names, leading underscores stripped (`read (int __fd, void *__buf, size_t __nbytes)` gives `fd, buf, nbytes`), and, where the result is one kind of thing whatever the arguments, a conventional name for it (`fd` for `open`, `n` for `read`, `len` for `strlen`, `p` for `malloc`, `fp` for `fopen`, `tp` for `localtime`). They ride on the prototype a table parks, so only a call a table prototype reaches counts, and they are kept out of the callee's parameter names, so its printed signature and name locks do not change. `kuna_libcnames` reads each local's evidence before the naming walk: the value a library call returns (`fd = open(a0,0);`), counted only when every library result the local holds agrees; then a library argument it is passed whole as when the name says what the value is (`read(fd,...)`, `write(a0,a1,n)`); then a name that only says which side of one call a value is on (`dest`/`src`, `s1`/`s2`), counted only when every such name agrees. A name equal to a type the code can print (`tm`, `FILE`) or a C or Rust keyword is passed over. The walk numbers every local exactly as with the option off and records that numbering, and only then does a numbered candidate print its library name, so `v4` is the same variable in every mode. A clash takes `_2`, `_3`, ... in call order, and no spelling repeats a name any variable of the function prints (a global's included), the scope holds, or a callee has. A directive reaches the local by either name, and a replay records the number: after `name fd src` the second descriptor stays `fd_2` and no local becomes `fd`, and a local whose library name a rename took prints its number. Over 14 stripped decbench binaries under `--mode aggressive` (O0 gzip, crontab, wc, bzip2, cat, dash; O2 bzip2, init, login, gzip, crond, tail, kmod, grep), 968 of 10,106 numbered locals print a library name in 546 of 3,297 functions, and every changed function differs from the option-off output only in those names, every other local keeping its number; against the source of the `compiled/` twins at the same call and slot, 415 of them could be located: 91 carry the source's own name and 324 another spelling of the same meaning (`fp` for `inStr`, `len` for `namelen`, `tp` for `tm`), none a misleading one. 0/675 datatest assertions move. No stage assertion of another feature moves with it on.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a local reads `fd = open(a0,0); n = read(fd,v4,0x200);` where it would read `v1 = open(a0,0); v3 = read(v1,v4,0x200);`, and every other local keeps its number. A directive may name such a local `fd` or `v1` in either setting. Set it off for `vN` names only, for example to diff against Ghidra output or to keep the numbering a script expects.
- **Where / provenance:** P6/naming-policy · ida · presentation-default · kuna-libcnames
- **Example:** `option libcnames off`

### `floatglobals` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a double parameter stored into a global prints as unsigned long and moves ahead of the integer parameters; a float parameter copied into a global prints as unsigned int; a global passed to a float parameter prints as a union reinterpretation ((union { unsigned int from; float to; }){ .from = dat_10001d78 }).to; firmware calls of float helpers wrap every global argument in a union.
- **What it does:** Let a float vote accept a global the whole program only moves through floating-point registers. A global has one declaration for every function, so the float votes refuse one: `void fy(int *p, double b) { gd = b; *p = 1; }` printed `fy(unsigned long a0, ..)`, an integer the convention passes in `rdi` where the machine reads `xmm0`, and a caller handing `gd` to a `double` parameter printed `sink(((union { unsigned long long from; double to; }){ .from = gd }).to)`. With `on`, the first float vote of a run whose only objection is a global has the analysis tier scan the whole program once (`kuna_analysis::listing::kuna_floatglobals`): every function of the inventory and every function it calls is walked, switch tables included, with its registers and stack slots followed as constants through its control flow, so a load or store the decompiler resolves to a global is seen however the address is formed (RIP-relative, literal pool, `adrp`, `movw`/`movt`, a GOT slot, a register the loader seeds at the entry). Each access is filed with its width and whether the value goes to or comes from a floating-point register or a float operation; an immediate stored there, a general-register move and a soft-float helper's argument are integer accesses. A writable global every access of which is a float access of one width, 4 or 8 bytes, that no other access overlaps and whose address is never stored where the walk lost the stack pointer, is a float. The function that asked is decompiled again with the answer, and every later function reads it: the parameter-input vote accepts a store of the parameter into such a global (`void fy(double a0,unsigned int *a1)`), a read of one passed in a float register takes the float type (`sink(gd)`), and `protoorder`'s float votes no longer count one as evidence against a float. Before the scan is asked, the function's own code must move the global only as a float -- every access of it whole, no value written there or read from it by an integer operation, its address not handed on, and every load and store through a pointer indexed from it a whole float move (a global its Symbol declares a scalar refuses any index) -- so a function that also adds to the bits (`g7 = *(long *)&gd + 1` in one case of a switch) refuses. The answer never declares the global: a type-locked float global that some code reads as an integer prints a conversion, so the global keeps its type and only the votes hear the evidence. A run that decompiles one function does not scan an image with more than 256 KiB of code and refuses the global instead. i386 and SPARC, whose position-independent code reaches globals through a register a thunk call sets, are not scanned.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a float parameter stored into a global, and a global handed to a float parameter, print as the floats they are on x86-64, AArch64 and ARM hard-float (Cortex-M firmware's union reinterpretations of float globals fall away), and a global some code moves through a general register -- a `memcpy` pun, a `movl $0, g` that zeroes a double, a Cortex-M4F double helper fed a float in `r0` -- keeps the integer reading. Turn it off to get the per-function refusal back (every global refuses a float vote), or when a run must not pay the one whole-program decode a float function's first vote triggers.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · ida · type-inference · GH-888
- **Example:** `option floatglobals off`

### `boolbyte` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a parameter is declared char and every use of it is if (a0) or !a0; a one-byte local is char but only ever assigned 0 and 1; a flag argument reads as a character, so a call site looks like it passes text; char v1; followed by v1 = 0; v1 = 1; if (v1); DWARF says _Bool and kuna says char or unsigned char.
- **What it does:** Declare a byte whose every read is a truth test as `bool` instead of `char`. `TYPE_BOOL` is only ever minted as the OUTPUT of a comparison -- `TypeOpEqual` and the other `booloutput` ops return `getBase(size, TYPE_BOOL)` -- and nothing in `ActionInferTypes` mints it for the value being compared: `TypeOpEqual::getInputLocal` votes `getBase(1, TYPE_INT)` for that, and the cached one-byte `TYPE_INT` is the ASCII `char` ("Char is preferred over other int types", `TypeFactory::cacheCoreTypes`). So a flag byte comes out `char`, as coreutils basename -O0 shows: `void sub_2b45(unsigned long a0, long a1, char a2)` whose only use of `a2` is `v1 = (a2) ? 0 : 10`, where the program declared `_Bool use_nuls`. When on, `kuna_boolbyte::truth_value_type` walks the byte's transitive readers through value-preserving identity -- COPY, MULTIEQUAL and INT_ZEXT, breadth-first with a visited set and a ten-hop cap, so the cap is a property of the graph rather than of the pop order, and running out of hops refuses -- and offers a `bool` candidate when every terminal read is a truth test and at least one of them is a real one: a CBRANCH condition, a BOOL_NEGATE/AND/OR/XOR operand, or an INT_EQUAL/INT_NOTEQUAL against zero. CPUI_INDIRECT is NOT value-preserving and refuses on both sides of the walk: an INDIRECT output is the value after the op it annotates, so a call whose callee may have written the storage breaks the chain in both directions -- crossing it would declare `bool` for a byte a callee fills with 200. A RETURN of the value is neutral, carrying neither acceptance nor refusal, because a `_Bool`-returning function is indistinguishable from a `char`-returning one from inside the callee. Everything else refuses, the call argument most deliberately: `putchar(c)` must not make `c` a bool just because something else also tests it. A Varnode the function itself writes must additionally carry a non-zero mask of at most 1, which is `ActionNonzeroMask`'s transitive "every def writes 0 or 1, or copies something that does" fact, computed in the pass that runs immediately before this one -- and it is what lets `x == 1` and `x & 1` count as truth tests for a proven flag while refusing them on an unproven byte, where they distinguish 1 from 2 and test parity respectively. A function INPUT has no def and always carries the full mask, so for a parameter the use shape is the whole of the evidence: a byte the function only ever branches on is what a `_Bool` parameter looks like from the inside. The candidate is FOLDED into the same `getLocalType` fold by `Datatype::type_order` rather than installed as a replacement seed, so a more specific vote still wins -- `SUB_BOOL` is 10, which beats `SUB_INT_CHAR` 19 and `SUB_UINT_PLAIN` 16 but loses to a callee's locked parameter type. Nothing else in the type system moves: the `TYPE_BOOL` propagation gate that refuses to carry bool into a Varnode whose mask exceeds 1 is left exactly as upstream wrote it, so the seed cannot travel along a copy chain into a value that can hold more than 0 or 1. One printer arm comes with the declaration: `CastStrategyC::isSubpieceCast` (cast.cc:411-432) lists the destination metatypes a SUBPIECE may print as a cast and TYPE_BOOL is not among them, because upstream never puts one there, so without the arm a truncation into the new `bool` falls to the functional form and prints the raw `SUB41(x,0)` p-code intrinsic -- an undeclared identifier, the class `subright` exists to keep out of the emitted C. With the option on such a truncation prints as a cast, and whole-binary counts of the intrinsic go DOWN rather than up (tar -O2 4 -> 1, ls -O2 1 -> 0, du -O0 1 -> 0). The cast is `(bool)x` only when every bit of `x` above the byte is proven zero, and `(bool)(unsigned char)x` otherwise: a C conversion to bool tests the whole operand, and a bool can reach a truncated byte through a sibling copy (`unsigned char c = x & 0x201, d = c; ... d = 0;`), where `(bool)(x & 0x201)` would be 1 for x = 0x200.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a one-byte parameter or stack local whose every use in the body is `if (v)`, `!v`, `v == 0`, `v ^ 1` or `v ? a : b` -- the shape a `_Bool` takes once the compiler has erased the type -- is declared `bool`, so a flag argument reads as a switch (`hash_find_entry(..., bool delete)`, gnulib's `bool ok` chains, option parsing) instead of as a character. Turn it off when you need kuna's declarations to stay in the upstream Ghidra vocabulary, when you are looking at code that really does pack flags into character data, or when a script addresses locals by the generated `vN` names an older run printed: §6 merges by type, so a `bool` and a `char` in one storage stop being merge candidates and two `bool`s start -- over eight whole binaries 10 of the 105 functions the default changes gain or lose a declaration, or have an expression come to name the other half of a split, and the remaining `vN` locals renumber. The flag constants re-render with the type (`v = '\x01'` becomes `v = 1`). Off is the upstream fold exactly: the candidate is never offered and the printer's truncation arm is not consulted.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · ida · type-inference · kuna-boolbyte
- **Example:** `option boolbyte off`

### `charbyte` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** a string pointer is declared unsigned char * and its bytes print as (char)*p; a comparison against a character constant prints as a number: v3 != 9, *p == 0x2d; a wrapper takes unsigned char *a1 and passes (char *)a1 to mbrtowc or strlen; strchr("...",(int)(char)*v1); a loop variable that walks text is unsigned char.
- **What it does:** Keep `char` for a byte loaded through a `char *` when the only unsigned vote on it is the zero-extension x86 uses to load every byte. `movzx` loads a byte whether the program meant it signed or not, so `*p` is a LOAD followed by INT_ZEXT, and `TypeOpIntZext::getInputLocal` votes `getBase(1, TYPE_UINT)` for the byte; in `getLocalType`'s fold `SUB_UINT_PLAIN` (16) outranks `SUB_INT_CHAR` (19), so the byte starts propagation as `uint1`. The `char *` that later reaches the LOAD's address cannot displace it -- `propagateTypeEdge` only moves a Varnode to a MORE specific type -- and the byte then pushes `unsigned char *` back over the pointer, which it does win. A string walk comes out in the wrong vocabulary, as coreutils fmt -O2 get_line shows: `v1 = (unsigned char *)*dat_c100; v7 = strchr("([\'`\"",(int)(char)*v1);`, and every mbrtowc wrapper takes `unsigned char *a1` and passes `(char *)a1`. When on, `kuna_charbyte::note_edge` watches the LOAD edges while `ActionInferTypes` propagates and records each byte whose pointer carries `char *` while the byte holds `uint1` only because of the zero-extension -- seen from whichever end the propagation order reaches first. If anything was recorded, the pass starts over: the local types are rebuilt, `kuna_charbyte::seed_char` seeds those bytes `char` (the fold they would have had without the zero-extension's vote), and propagation runs again by the unchanged rules. No edge is overridden: overriding the pointer edge instead would leave everything the byte had already typed `uint1` behind, and `char v1; ... v1 == 0xe9` is never true in C, whereas re-seeding lets the constant take `char` with the byte (`v1 == '\xe9'`). "Only because of the zero-extension" is checked on the readers: an INT_ZEXT must read the byte and no other reader may vote TYPE_UINT, so a byte that is masked, compared unsigned, shifted right, divided unsigned or passed as an `unsigned char` argument keeps `uint1`. The widened value is never claimed -- the INT_ZEXT output keeps its type and the printer shows the zero-extension of a `char` as the `(unsigned char)` cast it is -- and a byte read through an `unsigned char *` never meets a `char *`, so a byte from an `unsigned char` table stays `unsigned char`. The second propagation is kept only if every Varnode ends at the first propagation's type or the same type with `uint1` read as `char`, through pointers and arrays (`kuna_charbyte::keep_or_restore`); otherwise the first propagation's types are put back, because a fresh propagation can tip a contest the rule has no stake in (bash -O2 param_expand: a string pointer joined with an `int *` parameter came out `int *`). Two kinds of byte are never retyped, recorded or not (`kuna_charbyte::read_without_cast`, `kuna_charbyte::is_counter`): a byte that reaches a CALL, CALLIND or CALLOTHER argument, a RETURN or a BRANCHIND switch, directly or through copies, joins and one-byte arithmetic -- kuna shrinks a call argument to the byte when the `movzx` that widened it folds away, and C would sign-extend a `char` argument with no cast to show it (`logit("%d",c)` passes -128 for 0x80 where the binary passes 128), and a `char` switch variable never reaches `case 0x80:` -- and a counter, whose own one-byte sum or difference is stored back through the address it was loaded from (`*p = c + 1`), because the only `char` it meets is that sum's default signed vote. Either one in the second propagation, including a sibling byte read through the retyped pointer (`logit("%d",a0[1])`), puts the first propagation's types back, and so does a byte that took `char` while the pointer it is loaded through did not, which would print as a cast of its own load (`(uint4)(uint1)(char)v2[1]`), or a pointer that took `char *` while one it copies into or out of stayed `unsigned char *`, which would print as two variables joined by a cast (`v5 = (unsigned char *)&a0[1]`). The second propagation runs only in a function where something was recorded.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a byte read through a `char *` whose only unsigned vote is the `movzx` that loaded it is declared `char`, so a string walk reads in C's own vocabulary (`char *a1`, `if (v3 != '\t')`, `*v4 == '-'`) instead of `unsigned char *a1` with `(char)` casts and numeric constants (`if (v3 != 9)`, `*v4 == 0x2d`, `strchr("...",(int)(char)*v1)`, `mbrtowc(a0,(char *)a1,...)`). It retypes a byte only where C shows how each read of it is widened: the zero-extension prints as the `(unsigned char)` cast it is (`__ctype_b_loc()[(unsigned char)c]`) and constants compared with it become character literals; on 34 binaries every distinct value-bearing form that reads a retyped byte, on changed and unchanged lines alike, evaluates the same as the off arm's for all 256 byte values. A byte that reaches a call argument, a return or a switch, where C would sign-extend a `char` silently, and a counter whose own sum is stored back keep `unsigned char`, and so does every byte read through the same pointer. Turn it off when you need kuna's byte types in upstream Ghidra's vocabulary, or when diffing against output from before it was on: because the speculative merge only joins variables of one type, a `char` byte and an unrelated `unsigned char` value that used to share a declaration can split into two (or two `char *` join), renumbering the `vN` locals after them, and a constant added to such a byte prints the way kuna prints arithmetic on any `char` (`c + '\xd0'` for `c - 0x30`). With `structsynth` on, a synthesized struct whose pointer field moves from `unsigned char *` to `char *` can become identical to one already synthesized and share its name, which shifts the `struct_N` numbers of the functions decompiled after it.
- **Where / provenance:** P5/type-propagation · ida · type-inference · kuna-charbyte
- **Example:** `option charbyte on`

### `castarith` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** *(unsigned int *)((long)a0 + 0xac); every read through one parameter is a cast to (long) and back; (char *)((long)v4 + 0x10) assigned to a pointer variable; (void *)((long)a0 + 8) passed to a callee; two casts for one field read where IDA prints one.
- **What it does:** Print a pointer plus a whole number of elements as pointer arithmetic instead of an integer round trip. A pointer plus a constant byte offset reaches `ActionSetCasts` as a plain `INT_ADD` whenever P5 could build no `PTRSUB` or `PTRADD` for it -- a `void *` base has no field at the offset and no element size -- and the ported rules price an `INT_ADD` as integer arithmetic: `getInputCast` converts the pointer to `long` on the way in and `castOutput` converts the sum back to a pointer on the way out, so a 4-byte read at +0xac prints `*(unsigned int *)((long)a0 + 0xac)`, two casts for one read. The cast census measured this as the largest single source of kuna's casts (3,771 on the 4,815 functions kuna and IDA share; IDA prints the shape 0 times). When on, `kuna_castarith::rewrite` runs inside the cast pass, right after the PTRADD/PTRSUB repairs, on every `INT_ADD` of a pointer-typed value and a constant whose result is used as a `T *`. `T` is the value a lone LOAD reads or a lone STORE writes through the sum (the sum's own pointee when that is the same type or an integer of the same width), otherwise the sum's own pointee, and a `void` pointee counts in bytes for a value that stays in the function. If the offset is a whole number of `T`s, the op becomes `PTRADD(base, #k, #sizeof T)` over a `(T *)` cast of the base -- no cast when the base is a variable whose printed declaration points at `T` or at an integer of its width, and a retargeted cast when the base is itself an implied cast read only here -- and the printer renders it the way it renders every `PTRADD`: `((unsigned int *)a0)[0x2b]` under a dereference, `&((T *)p)[k]` as a value (`(T *)p + k` with `arraynotation off`). The value is identical: `k * sizeof(T)` is the original offset, the base is converted pointer to pointer with no integer in between, the element is the access width, C's `sizeof` of the printed `T` is that same width, and the printed index reads back as `k`. The integer form stays wherever the printed C could convert a value instead: an enum element (kuna prints every enum as a plain `enum`, which C sizes as an `int`, while a packed enum, `-fshort-enums` or a C++ `enum class : uint8_t` is 1 or 2 bytes in the binary, so `((color *)p)[3]` would read 12 bytes past `p`), an element the target's C data model has no type of that exact width for (`long double`, a 16-byte integer), a negative index of 2^31 elements or more (C types the literal `0x80000000` as `unsigned int`, so `p[-0x80000000]` would index forward, while the integer form's byte offset is a `long`), an offset that is not a whole number of elements, a variable index, an aggregate or padded element, a word-addressed space, a sum read as an integer, an address several accesses share, a store of a value the pass has not typed yet (unless its opcode fixes the kind), a `void *` sum passed to a call or returned (its `char *` would reach the whole-program prototype votes), and a constant that names a global or is address-like beside an integer cast to a pointer (`table[i]`). Every output language but C is untouched. One structuring decision can follow: `gotoreduce on` counts casts in its return-call-tail budget and runs after the cast pass, so a tail the fewer casts bring within the budget is duplicated (`// return-dupe`) instead of reached by a `goto`.
- **When to flip:** On by default: a `void *` or wrongly-sized base read at constant offsets prints one cast per access (`((unsigned int *)a0)[0x2b]`) instead of two (`*(unsigned int *)((long)a0 + 0xac)`), and a base already declared as the accessed pointer prints none (`a0[0xf]`). Turn it off to see upstream Ghidra's spelling, which keeps the byte offset visible; the index shown by the default is the offset divided by the element size. It never fires on a record base, which already prints `p->field`, and a struct pointer read past its last field is indexed like any other base.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/cast-policy · ida · presentation-default · kuna-castarith
- **Example:** `option castarith off`

### `castindex` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** *(long *)((long)v7 + v19 * 8); (long)v24 - (long)v14 passed as a length; free(*(void **)((long)v1 + (long)v2 * 8)); an array walk through a void * base prints two casts per element; a pointer difference of two char * is cast to long on both sides.
- **What it does:** Print a pointer plus a variable index as a subscript, and the difference of two byte pointers as `p - q`, instead of an integer round trip. `castarith` keeps a pointer plus a CONSTANT in pointer terms; a pointer plus a variable reaches `ActionSetCasts` as the same plain `INT_ADD` and is priced the same way, `(long)` on the pointer and a cast back on the sum: `*(long *)((long)v7 + v19 * 8)`. A pointer minus a pointer is an `INT_SUB`, whose operands the default input-cast rule converts to `long`: `(long)v24 - (long)v14`. When on, `kuna_castarith::rewrite_index` runs at `castarith`'s seam, on an `INT_ADD` of one pointer-typed value and one non-constant integer whose result is used as a `T *` (`T` chosen, and refused, exactly as `castarith` chooses it). When the variable is an implied `x * sizeof(T)` (or `x << s`) the add alone reads, the op becomes `PTRADD(base, x, #sizeof T)` and the scaling op is dropped; when `T` is one byte the variable itself is the index. The base follows `castarith`'s rules, and the rewrite happens only where it saves a cast, counted part by part (the index's extension, the base, and the sum, whose consumers are asked through the pass's own input-cast rule). The printer renders it as every `PTRADD`: `((long *)v7)[v19]` under a dereference, `&((T *)p)[i]` as a value. The value is unchanged: the element size is the scale, C scales the subscript by the same `sizeof`, and C converts an integer subscript by its own type's signedness, which the extension-input rule already made the extension's (an implied `SEXT`/`ZEXT` prints bare under a `PTRADD` in upstream too). `kuna_castarith::pointer_difference` accepts an `INT_SUB` of two pointers to the same one-byte integer type whose result is an integer of the pointer's width; the pass then leaves both operands uncast and casts the result against the signed pointer-width integer, so it prints `v24 - v14`: C's difference of two `char *` is their byte difference, and its type, `ptrdiff_t`, is the integer the two `(long)` casts produced, so the result's own cast is decided exactly as before. The integer form stays for a scale that is not the element's size (`p + i * 16 + 8` read at 8 bytes; no record is invented for the base), an index that is a pointer, float, enum or a value the pass already cast, a sum that is itself another pointer's subscript, a scaling op the pass has not reached, a rewrite that would only trade one cast for another, the difference of wider or of two different pointees (`long *` minus `long *` is an element count, not the byte count), and every refusal `castarith` makes for the element. Every output language but C is untouched, and `castindex off` prints byte-for-byte what the build without it prints.
- **When to flip:** On by default: an array walk through a `void *` or wrongly-typed base reads `((long *)v7)[v19]` (one cast) instead of `*(long *)((long)v7 + v19 * 8)` (two), an `int` index loses its `(long)` because C converts a subscript itself, and a byte-pointer difference reads `v24 - v14` (none) instead of `(long)v24 - (long)v14` (two). Turn it off to see upstream Ghidra's spelling, which keeps the byte arithmetic visible, or to ablate this cast class alone (`castarith` is independent: it handles a constant addend).
- **Where / provenance:** P9/cast-policy · ida · presentation-default · kuna-castindex
- **Example:** `option castindex off`

### `ctypes` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** int4/uint1/uint4/float8/float10 appear in the emitted C instead of C type names; the same function mixes `unsigned int` with `int4`; `code *` appears as a function-pointer type; the emitted C does not compile because its type names are not C.
- **What it does:** Spell the NAMED core types as the target's own C type names -- int4 -> int, uint1 -> unsigned char, float8 -> double, float10 -> long double, code * -> void * -- resolved against the compiler spec's decoded <data_organization>, so an 8-byte integer reads `long` on LP64 and `long long` on ILP32/LLP64. Extends `realtypes`, which relabels only residual TYPE_UNKNOWN; that split is why one function can declare `unsigned int v3;` and `int4 v1;` in the same block. Sizes no C type has (3/5/6/7, 16-byte integers) keep their undefined<N> form rather than being widened, because widening a truncating cast changes its meaning.
- **When to flip:** The emitted C uses Ghidra's internal type vocabulary (int4/uint1/float8/code) instead of C type names, or mixes the two within one function. ON in the `aggressive` and `fast` presets, and `auto` turns it on at every input size (including the `reliable` tier it selects from 500 KiB up to 2 MiB) -- so this is the default rendering of `kuna decompile`, `decompile-all`, `decompile-project` and the web front-end on any binary. The shipped catalog default is OFF, which is what the XML datatest corpus and an explicit `--mode reliable` run at: 42 datatest assertions pin the Ghidra spellings.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/literal-format · kuna · presentation-default · kuna-ctypes
- **Example:** `option ctypes on`

### `dedupvardecls` -- on | off, default `on`

- **Symptoms:** the same local declared once although many HighVariables share the stack slot; flip off to see one declaration line per high (e.g. int4 option_index repeated hundreds of times).
- **What it does:** Collapse local-variable declarations onto one line per mapped ScopeLocal symbol (same containing symbol + same identifier, declaring the symbol's own type when the highs disagree about it) and then onto one line per fully-rendered signature (type + name + array adornment + storage comment) of one object -- the same bound or referenced Symbol, since two distinct variables that print alike are still two variables -- so a stack slot mapped onto many scalar HighVariables is declared once instead of one line per high (the scalar analogue of the existing composite-symbol declaration collapse).
- **When to flip:** On by default (DIV-7): a stack slot is declared once even when many same-named scalar HighVariables share it (e.g. x86_64/cvs main, where the per-high rendering repeats `int4 option_index; // stack - 0x3c` ~200x), including when two live ranges of the slot recovered different types and so rendered two differently-typed declarations of one name -- invalid C (DIV-52). Set OFF to restore the one-declaration-per-high rendering.
- **Where / provenance:** P9/naming-policy · angr · presentation-default · angr-duplicate-decls
- **Example:** `option dedupvardecls off`

### `callwide` -- on | off, default `off`

- **Symptoms:** an untyped MIPS32 big-endian producer loses its low return word despite a declared 64-bit consumer; producer and caller disagree about a complete big-endian eight-byte integer return.
- **What it does:** Retain an eight-byte integer return in the ABI order only when a complete bounded sealed non-PIC MIPS32-BE executable proof finds a declared eight-byte consumer, both producer-written words at every return, and representable uses at every direct caller. A frozen whole-image verdict governs the producer, all callers and project declarations before rendering. ARM and other architectures, missing declaration provenance, returnable or indirect control, unsupported storage, incomplete bytes and exhausted bounds refuse promotion. Newly needed DWARF subregister returns also require the current narrowext policy to define their full return register (compiler for this MIPS ABI); the option never changes that policy. Requires bejoin evidence; off and the other bejoin modes preserve their existing behavior. Default off while validation is pending.
- **When to flip:** Enable for a big-endian register-pair producer whose untyped return loses a low word despite a caller forwarding both words unchanged to one declared eight-byte integer parameter. Check whole-image admission and emitted C/header agreement; this option does not infer width from ambiguous producer instructions or open caller sets.
- **Where / provenance:** P4/output-prototype · kuna · new-caller-evidence · callwide
- **Example:** `option callwide on`

### `bejoin` -- off | evidence | callers | on, default `callers`

- **Symptoms:** a long long return on a big-endian 32-bit target prints CONCAT44 with the low word first; a long long read from memory on PowerPC, MIPS, SPARC or ARM big-endian returns CONCAT44(p[1],p[0]); a 64-bit product, sum or shift returned on PowerPC, MIPS, SPARC or ARM big-endian comes back with its halves swapped; an AVR function returning a 16-bit int prints a read of R25R24 nothing assigns.
- **What it does:** Join a value returned in two registers in the order the ABI returns it. PowerPC (r3:r4), MIPS o32 big-endian (v0:v1), SPARC (o0:o1), ARM big-endian (r0:r1), AArch64 big-endian (x0:x1, a 16-byte value) and AVR's gcc ABI (R25:R24) put the most significant half in the first return register, and their output rule says so (`join_reverse`), but return recovery and the two-register CALL output arm joined every pair first register low, so a `long long` came back with its halves swapped: `(long long)a * b` on PowerPC printed `CONCAT44(a1 * a0,(int)(... >> 0x20))`. `evidence` decides once per function, from that function's own instructions, and both the function's RETURN and every call to it read the verdict, so the two agree in any decompile order and any run (`--functions`, `--jobs`, one `kuna decompile`, a front-end session): before any pipeline runs the driver walks the raw p-code of the function and of each direct callee, once per image (kuna_bejoin::evidence::seed), and a call the pipeline resolves only mid-pass (a `-mlong-calls` call, a constant function pointer) to a proven callee sends the function through the pass again with that verdict. A function is proven when every path's RETURN holds, both registers written and not read again, a sign extension (the first register is the second shifted right arithmetically by all but one bit, `mr 4,3; srawi 3,3,31`), a zero extension (a literal zero beside a value), or the two halves of one product whose low half an instruction of its own made (PowerPC `mullw` beside `mulhw`, MIPS `mflo` beside `mfhi`, ARMv4/v6 `umull r2,r3` then `mov r1,r2`) -- the extended value computed or another register's argument, never the second register's own entry value, a load, a call's result or a by-product, and read by nothing else on any path, a path ending in a call that does not return included (gcc -Os computes an `exit` argument in a branch delay slot). It is also proven when every RETURN holds, the low word read by nothing but moves and stack spills, the two words of one object read from memory (two loads of adjacent words, the high word's at the lower address: `lwz 4,4(3); lwz 3,0(3)`, `ldmia r0,{r0,r1}`, SPARC's `ldd`, also reloaded from the stack frame), or the pair a direct call to a proven callee handed back with its low word moved back into place by the function (`mr 31,4; bl ext; mr 4,31`), when it branches straight into a proven callee (a tail call), and when the remaining RETURNs hold two literals or a proven callee's pair left where the call put it; a callee chain that loops back is not proven. An `int` returning one word of a 64-bit object loads only that word, unless the object is volatile: `(int)(*(volatile long long *)p >> 32)` compiles to the bytes of `*p` and reads as the `long long`. A proven callee's pair is read high word first, and a call reading only its first register reads the high piece. Everything else keeps the first-register-low join, which C's truncation reads as the right `int`: an `int` worked out from the high half of a 64-bit temporary can compile to the same bytes as the `long long` (`umull r1,r0` is both `((u64)a * b) >> 32` and `(u64)a * b`; `addc 4,4,6; addze 3,3; add 3,3,5` is both `(a + b) >> 32` and `a + b`). `callers` (the default) adds the callers' reads: a function is also proven when one of its direct callers reads the second register after the call, before writing it or making another call (a move, a store, an operation, a compare; not a call, a RETURN, a branch, a register window's bulk copy, a register XORed with itself, an instruction nothing of which depends on the register's value (PowerPC's `subfe 4,4,4`), or, past a branch, a store of several registers or a register pair, which gcc merges into SPARC's `std %o0` or ARM's `stm` with a dead second word, or the delay slot of a conditional branch, which the delay slot filler may take from the branch target; a site whose fall-through reaches, before any branch, an instruction another branch of the caller targets or the target of a direct call, whose walk reaches a word the caller loads as data, after which a branch tests a flag nothing set since the call, in a caller that jumps through a register, or in gcc's `f.cold` part gives no evidence, because a call kuna does not know never returns is followed by unrelated code: `bl f; __builtin_unreachable()` by the block a `bne` reaches, an ARM or Thumb literal pool, a jump table's case, a static function whose symbol `strip -x` removed, or a rare block the hot part enters, and a function's extent ends at the size its symbol states, so a walk does not leave it; and no site whose walk reaches a C++ landing pad, which the unwinder enters with the selector in the second register: the pads come from the `.eh_frame` LSDAs and the `.ARM.exidx`/`.ARM.extab` data, a caller whose LSDA does not decode gives none, and so does every caller of an image whose C++ exception tables cannot be placed), or when a caller that hands its pair back untouched to its own RETURN is proven, because a caller compiled against `int f()` never reads a register the call clobbered: a 64-bit sum (`addc`/`adde`, `addu`+`sltu`, `addcc`/`addx`, `adds`/`adc`), ARM's single `umull`/`smull`/`umlal` and `return g();` without a tail call then join high word first wherever a caller stores, compares or adds both words.
